audits.stage: Intake: dumgen analyzeSentence (sentence-analysis/*), plus the click-time analysis selection that reads it (tf-demo selectAnalysisTarget, with classifyTarget as the fallback)
audits.howItWorks:
SUBMIT (app/tf-demo/server/linguisticOrchestration.ts:300-360). splitInSentences -> dumgen.segment (deterministic) -> Effect.forEach(accepted, analyzeAcceptedSentence, {concurrency: 4}) (line 351). persistSubmittedText (line 354) runs only after every sentence has finished. The UI awaits the whole action before it shows the text (src/views/library-view.tsx:59-70). So the user-visible intake latency is about ceil(N/4) waves times the slowest sentence in each wave. If an analysis fails, catchAll (lines 381-390) logs it and stores the sentence without an analysis.

analyzeGermanSentence (operation.ts:22-70):
1. placeSegments (placement.ts). Deterministic: it splits fused words by the fusion table, gives abbreviations their expansion as surface, and handles clitics.
2. Questions are lexemeQuestions + phrasemeQuestions over placement.resolvable (the input Segment indices):
   - m_a_b: a 3-way Choice for every ordered pair (questions.ts:41-53)
   - route_i: 17 options (lines 55-58)
   - role_i: 9 options (lines 59-62)
   - id_i: only for spellings that have authored DET/PRON/AUX candidates; per-cell rubric options plus NoMatch and Unresolved (lines 63-80)
   - fix_i: a 4-level Score; pk_i: 7 options (lines 90-99)
   - same_a_b: a Noul for every unordered pair (lines 100-108)
   - Count: Q(n) = 1.5n(n-1) + 4n + #id.
3. State is sent whole with every chunk (about 2.5k tokens): {sentence: <sN>-tagged, criteria: notation + realizationCriteria (6,858 chars), fixedness (1,782 chars)}.
4. chunk() splits by COUNT, 220 per call, in insertion order: all m_ first, then route/role/id per index, then fix/pk, then same_ (lines 112-124).
5. Promise.all over the chunks. Each jev call has a 10 s timeout and 0 retries (universal/trace.ts:20-27, judgment.ts:131-137), and answer validation is strict (judgment.ts:28-62). Any chunk failure fails the whole sentence.
6. assembleAnalysis (pure, assemble.ts):
   - union-find over the symmetrized Include mass, joining at >= 0.6; both directions are required
   - groupVote route mass
   - NOUN article guard
   - splitMultiHead using role==Head
   - fused words forced apart: the ADP becomes a singleton and the article piece joins the next NOUN that has no article (lines 302-380)
   - identity mass for each target's head index only
   - phraseme layer: union-find over head-head pairs with same_ >= 0.5 (lines 386-409), kept when mean fix_ >= 1.5 and pk_ names a Kind.

WHICH ANSWERS ARE CONSUMED:
- m_ and route_: all of them.
- role_: only by splitMultiHead and head choice. Free is mapped to Head (lines 290-295).
- id_: only for each target's head. The host sees it only through effectiveRoute on singleton targets (analysis.ts:214-223).
- fix_ and pk_: only for heads in multi-head components (39 of 620 fix_ answers ended up in emitted phrasemes).
- same_: only head-head pairs (1,310 of 1,991 in the replay).

CLICK. selectAnalysisTarget (app/tf-demo/server/sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts):
1. Requires analysis.stitchedText === stored stitchedText (line 41).
2. Maps offsets back to stored indices and calls resolvedUnitAt (analysis.ts:336-369). That returns the Phraseme when its Kind is not None; otherwise the effectiveRoute of the Lexeme target.
3. Requires the clicked stored Segment to be fully covered (line 81), then runs validateEncounter.
4. Otherwise dumgen.classifyTarget runs: 1 jev call, 6.3 questions, p50 300 ms, p90 350 ms; 8-10 of 243 cases end Unresolved (.runs/dumgen/*, 2026-09-22).

Only {family, kind, memberSegmentIndices} reaches resolveGrammar. Roles, identity mass, fixedness and kindMass never reach click-time grammar. The DET/PRON identity is re-derived at click time (features call + locateAuthoredIdentity + an optional identity jev call).

OFFLINE MEASUREMENTS. Scripts are in /tmp/intake-audit/*.ts; no API calls. They use production builders and assembly, and replay the stored run /tmp/intake-clicks-anchored-lexeme-top-layered-trimmed-roles-phraseme-score-1.json (110 sentences, 238 clicks, same question wording as production minus id_).
- Replayed through the production assembly plus an emulated host selector: 152/238 pass on the analysis path; 9/238 clicks (3.8%) fall back to classifyTarget. All 9 are deterministic: 6 from a capitalization bug, 3 fused-word clicks. The route never wins Unresolved (0 of 620).
- Question counts on the eval click corpus: mean 78.5 per sentence, p90 145, max 1,252 (6 chunks).
- On a 12-sentence realistic prose sample: n mean 14.4, 387 questions per sentence, 1-4 chunks, about 63k input tokens per sentence (estimated at 3.43 chars/token, calibrated on the lab's 16,194 tokens per sentence).
- Mix: m_ is 46-56% of questions and about 65% of output tokens (~63 output tokens per m_ answer); same_ is 23-28%.

calls.name: analyzeSentence chunk (jev judgment, stage analyzeSentence, route de/sentence)
calls.when: always: once per accepted German sentence with at least one ResolvableText Segment; ceil(Q/220) chunks, all fired with Promise.all
calls.sequentialAfter: dumgen.segment (deterministic). Chunks run in parallel with each other and with up to 3 other sentences (host concurrency 4). persistSubmittedText waits for every sentence
calls.approxInputTokens: About 2.5k of state per chunk, repeated in every chunk. Per sentence: 16.2k on the eval click corpus (lab-measured); an estimated 63k for 15-token prose. Estimated per-chunk size by count-based chunking: 25k for m_-only chunks, 37-52k for the chunk holding route/role/id (n=12-28), 77k at n=46
calls.questions: Q(n) = n(n-1) m_ + n route_ + n role_ + n fix_ + n pk_ + n(n-1)/2 same_ + #id_ (about 2 per short sentence, 4 per prose sentence). n=5: 50 questions; n=10: 175; n=12: 246 (2 chunks); n=15: 375; n=20: 650 (3 chunks); n=28: 1,246 (6 chunks); n=46: 3,308 (16 chunks); n=100: 15,250 (70 chunks). Latency: p50 355-385 ms for single calls of up to about 145 questions; about 1.2 s per full 220-question chunk (lab maximum of 7,391 ms summed over 6 chunks; 4.7-5.1 s over 4 chunks)

calls.name: classifyTarget (click-time fallback)
calls.when: conditional: no stored analysis (analysis failed or non-German); analysis.stitchedText differs from stored (capitalized fused word); click on a fused word; route or Phraseme Unresolved; invalid Encounter. Replay: 3.8% of eval clicks, and 11% of occurrences in the prose sample
calls.sequentialAfter: loadResolutionContext; runs before resolveGrammar, on the click critical path
calls.questions: 6.3 per call on average (membership for each other occurrence plus route). p50 300 ms, p90 350 ms; 3.3-4.1% end in a whole-click Unresolved (8-10 of 243)

unusedOrRedundantInputs: same_ pairs that involve a non-head occurrence are never read. assemble.ts:398-404 only looks up same_{min}_{max} between target heads. In the replay 681 of 1,991 same_ answers (34%) were never read, and 148 (7%) pair two occurrences of one Lexeme target (for example article and noun).

same_ pairs involving an article form (der/die/das/den/dem/des/ein*) can be dropped deterministically: 0 of 620 resolved units change in the replay. That removes 19% of same_ on prose and 26% on the eval corpus.

m_ pairs across clause punctuation. 365 of 1,991 pairs (18%) cross punctuation in the eval corpus, and 45% of m_ questions do on prose. 0 of 141 joins at tau cross punctuation. Pruning them (with correlator anchors exempt) changes 0 of 620 resolved units.

role_ answers are consumed only by splitMultiHead and head choice (assemble.ts:186-217, 331-334). The host never reads member roles: sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts only uses family, kind and offsets. Removing all roles changes 1 of 238 click passes (152 to 151). The Free option is redundant: memberRole maps Free to Head (assemble.ts:292), and merging Free into Head changes 0 passes. role_ is still only 7% of questions, so dropping it is not worth doing.

id_ questions for AUX-only spellings (hat, ist, wird, worden, war...) are 17% of id_ on prose and 21% on eval. Their only effect is the effectiveRoute override on a singleton, which flipped VERB to AUX once per run (1 of 256 singletons). ADR 0026 says AUX is not a route.
id_ answers for non-head occurrences (articles inside NOUN targets, auxiliaries inside VERB targets) are computed but never read. identityMassOf is called only for headIndex.

IdentityMass (headword group plus cells plus definition) is stored per target but never passed to click-time resolveGrammar. For DET/PRON the click re-derives identity: features call, then locateAuthoredIdentity, then an extra jev identity call on Gap/Ambiguous.

fix_ overlaps pk_. The README measured the `vote` policy (pk_ mass alone, None may win) scoring the same as `score` (fix_ floor). It is also only read for heads in multi-head components (39 of 620 answers reached an emitted phraseme).

The `fixedness` state field (1,782 chars, about 520 tokens) is re-sent with chunks that contain only m_ questions, and `criteria` (6,858 chars, about 2k tokens) with chunks that contain only same_. Every chunk resends the full state (operation.ts:38-50).
The Unresolved options on m_, route_ and role_ were never the argmax in the replay (0 of about 5,200 answers). They add output tokens but decide nothing. They are cheap, so keep them.
promptProblems: realizationCriteria (criteria.ts:14-34) is targetCriteria with 5 string replacements, and it is still framed around a click that does not exist at intake: 'Select the complete fixed unit containing the clicked occurrence', 'All fixed-member clicks must select exactly the same unit', 'Article clicks resolve the same noun', 'clicking Weg in Der Weg ist das Ziel gives [Der,Weg]', 'exclude their neighboring verb when they are clicked, and exclude them when the verb is clicked', 'Classify the whole identity, not the clicked anchor's standalone POS'. It also ends with 'Uncertainty or contradictory membership must remain Unresolved; do not repair, trim, extend or replace the assembled group', and there is no assembled group at intake. Do NOT reword this without measurement: rewording collapsed membership (114 vs 164 of 238, README 'Two layers').

The replacement sentence 'A fused preposition and article (im, zum, ins, zur) is one ADP unit whose article part belongs to the following noun.' (criteria.ts:25) drops the original's 'unless inside a larger fixed expression'. Together with assemble.ts:303-305 ('A fused word never joins a group whole... whatever the matrix said'), intake cannot produce the gold multiword adverbs zum Beispiel, zum Teil and im Allgemeinen. That is 6 of 238 eval clicks failing: routed ADV [Teil], or Collocation.

The criteria .replace() calls are unchecked (criteria.ts:14-34). All 5 patterns currently match (verified by the output length and content), but if targetCriteria is edited, the Funktionsverbgefüge/Idiom sentences would silently come back into the Lexeme layer. The README showed that version glues whole proverbs into one NOUN word.

The route_ question asks 'what is the Family/Kind of the complete fixed unit' (questions.ts:56), but the options are Lexeme Kinds only and the criteria say expressions are not units. 'Family' is vestigial.

role_: 'Head' and 'Free' overlap for single-member units. The README measured 155-157 of 852 answers choosing Head on singletons, and the code maps Free to Head anyway. 'Auxiliary' lists 'sein, haben, werden, or recipient-passive bekommen' (criteria.ts:84-85), while the criteria also accept kriegen and erhalten as recipient-passive auxiliaries.

id_ instructions offer AUX identities and explain when they apply (identity.ts:160-161). Identity only matters for singleton heads, and a serving auxiliary is never one, so an AUX option can only cause a wrong VERB->AUX flip (observed 1 per run).

fixednessCriteria lists 'eine Entscheidung treffen, eine Frage stellen' as Collocations (criteria.ts:38). The click corpus gold rules trifft/stellt eine Entscheidung/Frage as Lexeme (README: 6 clicks lost to this conflict), so either the gold or the criteria are wrong.

The comment at questions.ts:112 says 'request budget is about 32k tokens shared by state and questions', but chunking is by question count. Estimated chunk sizes for eval sentences with n=12-28 are 37-52k tokens, and those succeeded in the lab. So either the comment is wrong, or long sentences (n>=30, where the mixed chunk is estimated at 60-77k tokens) are close to failing.

The lab's per-sentence latency sums chunk durations (prototypes/intake/corpus.ts:163), but production runs chunks in parallel. The README's p90 and max figures overstate wall-clock for chunked sentences and hide the per-chunk growth.

hypotheses.title: Capitalized fused words (Im/Am/Beim/Zum...) invalidate the whole sentence's analysis at click time
hypotheses.claim: placeSegments pushes the fusion table's lowercase component spans instead of the source casing. So a sentence starting with Im/Am/Beim/Zum/Vom/Ins/Zur gets analysis.stitchedText 'im …' while the stored text is 'Im …'. selectAnalysisTarget then returns null for every click in that sentence, and each of those clicks pays a classifyTarget round trip with click-time classification accuracy.
hypotheses.evidence:
- universal/fusion-table.ts:127 lowercases the form before lookup.
- sentence-analysis/placement.ts:64-71 pushes component.span ('i'+'m', 'bei'+'m').
- tf-demo sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:41: `if (analysis.stitchedText !== stored.stitchedText) return null;`.
- Offline check (/tmp/intake-audit/textmismatch.ts): 4 of 330 corpus sentences mismatch ('Im Leitartikel', 'Im Workshop', 'Beim Nähen', 'Im Allgemeinen').
- Replay: 6 of 238 eval clicks and 18 of 620 occurrences fall back for this reason alone.
- Prose sample: 15 of 173 occurrences (8.7%), from one 'Im Sommer …' sentence.
- Without the check the same stored answers pass 156 instead of 152 (/tmp/intake-audit/sweep.ts).
- classifyTarget costs p50 300 ms / p90 350 ms, and 8-10 of 243 runs end Unresolved (.runs/dumgen, 2026-09-22).
hypotheses.proposedChange: In placement.ts, take each component's text from segment.text.slice(cursor, cursor + component.span.length) so the source casing is kept (the spans sum to the form length); keep surface as authored. Add a unit test that the placed Segments join back to the stored Stitched Text for capitalized fusions. Short-term host guard: compare case-insensitively when the lengths match.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Speed: removes one jev round trip (~300 ms p50, ~350 ms p90) from every click in affected sentences. That is about 2.5% of eval clicks and up to 8-9% of prose occurrences, since sentence-initial 'Im/Am/Beim …' is common. Reliability: removes the 3-4% whole-click Unresolved risk of classifyTarget on those clicks and recovers about +4 of 238 passes on the analysis path.
hypotheses.risk: Very low. Offsets are unchanged (same lengths). Check that nothing downstream expects lowercase component text; the fixtures gold is keyed by offset.
hypotheses.experiment: 1) Offline: rerun `bun /tmp/intake-audit/audit.ts replay` after the fix. Expect clickFallback to go from 9 to 3 and the 'text' reason to 0. 2) Live: add 'Im Sommer fahren viele Deutsche ans Meer.' and 'Beim Nähen verlor sie den roten Faden.' to sentence-analysis/de and run `bun run build:js && bun --env-file=../../.env.local cli/evaluate.ts --experiment sentence-analysis/de --revision capfix`. 3) In tf-demo, submit one such sentence and check that inspection shows 'Select target · analysis', not 'classified'.

hypotheses.title: Serve fused-word clicks (im, zum, am…) from the analysis instead of classifyTarget
hypotheses.claim: By design, a click on a fused word always falls back to classifyTarget. The anchor is the ADP piece, whose target excludes the article piece, so the stored Segment is never fully covered. The gold (and targetCriteria) for most such clicks is the fused word as a singleton ADP, which the analysis already implies.
hypotheses.evidence:
- sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:27-31 and 81: 'When the clicked Segment itself is not a member … the caller classifies'.
- assemble.ts:309-319 makes the adposition piece a singleton target with provenance 'fusion-table'.
- Replay: 3 of 238 clicks and 6 of 620 occurrences hit 'clickedNotMember'; 4 of 173 prose occurrences are fused words.
- Gold for fused-word clicks in target-classification source-data: 7 are Lexeme/ADP [clicked], 5 are Phraseme (already served, since a Phraseme covers both pieces), 3 are multiword ADV (see intake-fused-multiword-adverbs).
- targetCriteria: 'A fused preposition/article source word (im, zum, zur, ins) is a singleton ADP unless inside a larger fixed expression.'
hypotheses.proposedChange: In selectAnalysisTarget or resolvedUnitAt, when the clicked stored Segment is a fusion and the anchor's Lexeme target has provenance 'fusion-table' (ADP) with no Phraseme over it, return {family: 'Lexeme', kind: 'ADP', memberSegmentIndices: [clickedIndex]}.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Speed: about -300 ms on fused-word clicks (2-4% of occurrences). Reliability: avoids classifyTarget's 3-4% Unresolved and its accuracy (~60%) on these clicks.
hypotheses.risk: Low. Confirm that resolveGrammar handles an ADP target whose single member is a fused word the same way it does after classifyTarget; it should, since classification returns the same shape. Multiword-adverb cases (zum Beispiel) stay wrong either way.
hypotheses.experiment: 1) Offline: patch the emulated selector in /tmp/intake-audit/audit.ts and rerun the replay; expect +3 analysis-path clicks and 0 clickedNotMember. 2) Live: run `cli/evaluate.ts --experiment grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/adposition` and check that the fused cases pass, then click 'im'/'zum' in tf-demo and check the inspection path.

hypotheses.title: Stop blocking text display on all sentence analyses; raise effective parallelism
hypotheses.claim: The user waits for every sentence's analysis before the text appears, and sentences run 4 at a time. Realistic sentences (n >= 12) need 2-4 chunks of 220 questions at about 1.2 s each, so a 25-sentence text waits about 7 waves x ~1.1 s ≈ 7-8 s. Most of that is avoidable queueing, not model work.
hypotheses.evidence:
- linguisticOrchestration.ts:333-352: Effect.forEach with {concurrency: 4}, then persistSubmittedText (line 354).
- library-view.tsx:59-70 awaits submitText before navigating.
- Limits: textSubmissionLimits.ts:5-7 allow 25 sentences.
- Per-chunk latency: 220-question chunks take ~1.2 s (lab maximums of 7,391 ms over 6 chunks and 4,699-5,127 ms over 4 chunks); single calls of ≤145 questions have p50 355-385 ms.
- Prose sample: 8 of 12 sentences need 2-4 chunks (/tmp/intake-audit/audit.ts inventory).
hypotheses.proposedChange: A) Persist the text and Segments first and return the textId. Analyze sentences in a scheduled action (top of the text first) and patch each analysis in as it arrives. Clicks before that use the existing classify fallback. B) Independently, replace per-sentence concurrency 4 with a global in-flight jev limiter (for example 12-16 requests) over chunks, so long sentences do not starve short ones.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: A: the text shows in about the time of segment + persist (<0.5 s instead of ~3-8 s for 10-25 sentences). B alone: about 2-3x faster intake for texts with more than 4 sentences.
hypotheses.risk: A: clicks in the first seconds pay classifyTarget (+300 ms, lower accuracy), and the UI needs to tolerate analyses arriving later. B: jev rate limits; the lab needed 429 backoff (lab.ts:141-160), and production has no retry (see intake-retry-partial-failure).
hypotheses.experiment: Build a 25-sentence prose text and submit it in tf-demo dev (Convex 3210 / Vite 5174) 3 times each at concurrency 4, 8 and 12. Record submitText wall time from the inspection spans, count 429/timeout failures, and count sentences stored without an analysis. For A, prototype the schedule-and-patch flow and measure time to first paint and time to the last analysis.

hypotheses.title: Chunk by estimated size and interleave families instead of 220 questions in insertion order
hypotheses.claim: Per-call latency grows with question count at the top end: about 300 ms at 6 questions, ~370 ms p50 at ~77, ~1.2 s per 220-question chunk. The wall-clock of a sentence is its slowest chunk. Chunking by count in insertion order also packs all route/role/id questions (1.5-3.4k chars each) into one chunk, estimated at 37-52k tokens for n=12-28 and 77k at n=46, against a stated 32k budget.
hypotheses.evidence:
- questions.ts:112-124: fixed 220, insertion order.
- Measured per-question sizes (chars): m_ 340, route_ 1,862, role_ 1,475, id_ 2,000-3,400, fix_ 564, pk_ 724, same_ 378.
- Estimated per-chunk tokens (3.43 chars/token, calibrated on the lab's 16,194 tokens per sentence):
  - n=14: 38k + 17k
  - n=19: 25k + 47k + 20k
  - n=28: 25k, 25k, 25k, 52k, 28k, 20k
  - n=46: 9x25k, 77k, 34k, …
- Output: ~54-75 tokens per question on average; m_ about 63 each.
- Lab p90 rises with questions per sentence: 552 ms (10.9 q), 594 (40.8), 860 (47.5), 1,009 (76.8), 1,227 (77.6).
- README 'questions shape': 80 questions per call hit max_tokens_exceeded, so there is a real ceiling.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Chunk to a size budget: about 60-100 questions, or a budget weighted by option count, so a 17-option route counts about 5 times an m_. Interleave families round-robin so no chunk concentrates route/role/id. Send only the state fields a chunk references (drop `fixedness` from m_/route/role-only chunks and `criteria` from same_/fix/pk-only chunks). Keep Promise.all, behind the global limiter from async-intake-and-concurrency.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Wall-clock per sentence for n >= 12: from about 1.2 s to about 0.5-0.7 s (a slowest chunk of ~80 questions instead of 220). Removes the oversize-request failure mode for long sentences.
hypotheses.risk: About 2-3x more requests per long sentence (rate limits). Accuracy impact is unmeasured, though jev answers questions independently over shared state and the grammar-batch evidence suggests neutral-or-better. Dropping state fields per chunk could shift answers slightly.
hypotheses.experiment: Change the lab to record the per-sentence MAX chunk duration as well as the sum (corpus.ts:163). Run `bun prototypes/intake/lab.ts --layered --layers both --shape layered-trimmed --route-policy groupVote --threshold 0.6 --phraseme-policy score --chunk 220` vs `--chunk 80` vs `--chunk 40`, 2 runs each, on the 110 click sentences plus 12 prose sentences (n 8-22) and 3 synthetic sentences with n=30/40/50. Metrics: pass (±7 noise, compare case by case), max-chunk wall p50/p90, failures.

hypotheses.title: Do not ask m_ for pairs separated by clause punctuation (correlator anchors exempt); drop same_ pairs with an article
hypotheses.claim: Membership joins never cross punctuation in the measured data. The only gold units that cross it are correlators, which a small closed anchor list can exempt. Pruning those m_ pairs (treated as Exclude), plus same_ pairs involving an article form, removes 31% of questions on prose and 14% on eval and changes no resolved unit.
hypotheses.evidence:
- Stats on the stored run: 1,991 pairs, 141 joins at tau 0.6. Joins by distance: 104 / 17 / 14 / 4 / 1 at distances 1-5, plus 1 at 11. 365 pairs cross punctuation; 0 joins cross it.
- Gold: 2 of 128 multi-member units cross punctuation, and both are correlators ('Einerseits …, andererseits', 'Je …, desto'); no Phraseme gold crosses punctuation.
- Replay of the combined prune (/tmp/intake-audit/combined.ts): 0 of 620 resolved units changed. Prose: 4,640 to 3,218 questions; chunks at 220 go from 26 to 21, and at 80 from 63 to 46.
- Contrast: a distance window loses 2 clicks even at >10 tokens (4 at >3), because the verb bracket is long. Do not use distance.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In lexemeQuestions, skip m_a_b when a Punctuation Segment in [,;:()–—„“"?!] lies between a and b, unless either token is a correlator anchor (einerseits, andererseits, je, desto, umso, entweder, oder, weder, noch, sowohl, als, auch, nicht, nur, sondern, so, dass, teils, zwar, aber, um, zu, ohne, statt). In components(), treat an unasked pair as 0 Include, not as 'unresolvable'. In phrasemeQuestions, skip same_ when either token is a der/die/das/den/dem/des/ein* form. For the Satzklammer, prune only between adjacent comma regions, not across an enclosed region (to keep 'hat, obwohl …, gearbeitet').
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Mainly reliability and cost: 27-31% fewer requests and tokens per prose sentence, fewer chunk-failure points, less rate-limit pressure. Wall-clock gains only once chunks are small (with chunk-by-size-balanced). Accuracy neutral in the replay.
hypotheses.risk: The corpus has few multi-clause sentences with a verb bracket interrupted by an embedded clause ('Er hat, als er kam, angerufen'). The adjacent-region rule reduces the risk but it is unmeasured. The correlator list must be complete.
hypotheses.experiment: 1) Offline replay (done: 0 changes). 2) Add 10-15 gold sentences to sentence-analysis/de: embedded-clause Satzklammer, separable particle after an embedded clause, nicht nur …, sondern auch; so …, dass; entweder …, oder; and 3 proverbs with commas. 3) Lab: `--layered --layers both --shape layered-trimmed --route-policy groupVote --threshold 0.6 --phraseme-policy score`, pruned vs full, 2 runs each on 110 sentences plus the new ones. Compare pass case by case, members ok, questions/sentence, calls/sentence.

hypotheses.title: Bound the intake fan-out for very long sentences
hypotheses.claim: Question count is quadratic, and the submission limits allow 2,000-character sentences (about 250 tokens). One such sentence would fire about 94k questions as about 427 parallel requests (~11M input tokens, ~$0.45), and 25 of them about 10k requests. That invites 429s, which with 0 retries drop the analyses, and exposes the oversize-chunk risk.
hypotheses.evidence:
- Formula check (/tmp/intake-audit/audit.ts inventory): n=46 gives 3,308 questions in 16 chunks; n=100 gives 15,250 in 70.
- textSubmissionLimits.ts:5-7: MAX_SOURCE_SENTENCE_CHARACTERS = 2000, MAX_SOURCE_SENTENCES = 25.
- operation.ts:40-51: Promise.all with no limit.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Apply the clause-window pruning (prune-membership-across-clauses), which makes the count roughly linear in clauses. Add a global in-flight limiter. Above a cap (for example n > 60 after pruning), analyze clause by clause, or skip the analysis and rely on the click fallback.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes a pathological failure and cost mode; no effect on typical sentences.
hypotheses.risk: Clause-by-clause analysis could split units that span clauses (rare; see the correlator exemption).
hypotheses.experiment: Run production analyzeSentence on 3 synthetic sentences with n=30, 50 and 80. Record calls, failures (max_tokens_exceeded, 429, timeout) and wall time, with and without the guard.

hypotheses.title: Retry failed intake chunks instead of dropping the sentence's analysis
hypotheses.claim: Intake uses the click-path policy: 10 s timeout, 0 retries, strict validation that the answer count matches, and Promise.all. So one 429, timeout or malformed answer among up to 220 silently drops the whole sentence's analysis, and every click in that sentence then pays classifyTarget. Intake is not click-critical, so retries are nearly free.
hypotheses.evidence:
- trace.ts:20-27: timeoutMs 10,000, maxRetries 0.
- judgment.ts:28-30: 'Judgment answer count differs from questions' becomes InvalidModelOutput.
- operation.ts:40-51: Promise.all.
- linguisticOrchestration.ts:381-390: catchAll stores no analysis.
- The lab needed 429 backoff (lab.ts:141-160) and used a 30 s timeout (harness.ts:33). With that it had 0 failed sentences in about 1,500 sentence runs, so the risk is rate-limit and tail driven, not model driven.
hypotheses.proposedChange: For analyzeSentence only: retry each failed chunk up to 2 times with backoff on 429/5xx/timeout/InvalidModelOutput; use allSettled and re-ask only the failed chunks; timeout 20-30 s. Record a 'SentenceAnalysisRetried' event.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Fewer sentences stored without an analysis, so fewer click fallbacks (each +300 ms and 3-4% Unresolved). The size of the gain depends on the production failure rate, which is unknown: read it from the inspection data.
hypotheses.risk: Longer intake in the worst case (bounded by the retries). Duplicate cost on retries is negligible (jev input costs $0.042/M).

hypotheses.title: Offload canonical-form proposals to intake to remove the click-time Luna canonical-form call
hypotheses.claim: Most first-encounter open-class clicks have a canonical form that is neither the joined members nor a member. With no stored Lemma candidate, the features call answers CandidateIsNotCanonical and resolveGrammar runs a sequential Luna generation on the critical path. One Luna call per sentence at intake can propose headwords for every occurrence. At click time the proposal becomes a canonicalFormAlternatives option that the existing jev `canonical` choice can accept, skipping the Luna call.
hypotheses.evidence:
- Computed from grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/*/corpus.json: the canonical form differs from both the joined members and every single member in 87% of verb cases (76/87), 68% of adjective, 57% of adverb, 42% of noun and 46% of adposition cases.
- grammatical-resolution/judgments.ts:280-297: the canonical options are only stored lemmas plus (for NOUN) the members.
- Lines 568-569 and 612-676: CandidateIsNotCanonical triggers executeGeneration on gpt-5.6-luna.
- Memory: Luna ~1 s median and 2.7 s tail (emoji; same model and configuration).
- prototypes/README: 'Verb p50 includes Luna canonical-form generation, which is now the dominant remaining cost on that route.'
hypotheses.proposedChange: At intake, run one Luna call per sentence in parallel with the jev call. It takes the tagged sentence and returns, per <sN>, the dictionary headword of the word that occurrence realizes (separable particle and auxiliary resolved to their verb, e.g. steht…auf → aufstehen, hat…gearbeitet → arbeiten; nouns in nominative singular). Store it on the analysis. At click time, add the proposal for the target's head to canonicalFormAlternatives (new input to resolveGrammar). Keep the Luna generation as the fallback when the judge rejects every option.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes about 1 s median (2.7 s tail) from most first-encounter VERB/ADJ clicks and about 40% of NOUN clicks. Estimated cost about $0.0006 per sentence at Luna fast-tier prices. Intake wall-clock becomes max(jev, Luna) per sentence, and is off the critical path if intake is made async.
hypotheses.risk: The judge might accept a wrong proposal it would otherwise have rejected, leading to a wrong lemma. Proposals for Phraseme targets are weaker. Adds one Luna call per sentence even for sentences never clicked (the cost is small).
hypotheses.experiment: Generate proposals offline for every sentence in the grammar corpora (verb 77, adjective 32, noun 45, adverb 49, idiom 27, collocation 20 eval cases) with one Luna call per case sentence. Add a prototype flag that injects the proposal into canonicalFormAlternatives. Run `cli/evaluate.ts --experiment grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb` (and adjective, noun, phraseme/idiom, phraseme/collocation) with and without it, 2 runs each. Metrics: pass (compare case by case), share of cases whose trace contains generateCanonicalForm, resolveGrammar p50/p90 latency.

hypotheses.evidence:
- Replay of the stored lemma rubric runs (/tmp/intake-audit/idlemma.ts): kind correct 159/160 with id_ vs 137/136 without; pass 158/158 vs 136/134.
- Click corpus identity runs (/tmp/intake-audit/idreplay.ts): 3 of 256 singletons flipped per run; 1 was VERB->AUX; 0 net pass change (148/148, 151/151).
- AUX-only spellings are 17-21% of id_ questions (prose: 8 of 48; eval: 46 of 215).
- derive-aux: 21 of 22 and 18 of 18 AUX derivations need no jev call.
- analysis.ts:214-223: the override applies only to singletons.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Filter AUX members out of candidatesFor at intake, or ignore AUX identities in effectiveRoute. Skip id_ when no DET/PRON candidate remains.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 1 fewer id_ question per prose sentence, and fewer output tokens (AUX options). Removes the rare wrong AUX route on copula/possession clicks.
hypotheses.risk: Low. AUX identity is not consumed anywhere else on the click path.
hypotheses.experiment: Offline first: rerun idreplay.ts with AUX options removed from the stored id_ distributions. Then run the lab `--corpus lemma --identity --identity-shape rubric --runs 2` and the clicks corpus with the filtered candidates. Metrics: DET/PRON route-correct and click pass.

hypotheses.title: Precompute click-time grammar feature answers for every analysis target at intake
hypotheses.claim: The analysis already fixes each target's members and route. A second intake round with all targets marked could answer the route's feature, orthography and normalization questions for every target, so analysis-path clicks skip the jev features call (~330 ms p50) and its follow-ups (noun article, lexical strings, DET/PRON identity). With intake-headword-proposals, click-time grammar could then need no model call at all.
hypotheses.evidence:
- prototypes/intake README 'Grammar features at intake': batching 2-8 decoy targets did not degrade the scored noun target (all features correct 15 solo vs 22-23 batched of 44; field accuracy 0.834 vs 0.865-0.880; p50 358 to 384-422 ms).
- Design A: noun grammar 330 ms and verb 341 ms per click are single jev round trips on the critical path.
- The click pipeline is strictly sequential up to the emoji step: selectTarget → resolveGrammar → reading resolution.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Prototype: after assembly, build per-target feature questions (grammarFeatureFields per route) over one state with every target marked and indexed, asked in size-bounded chunks. Store the raw answers per target. At click time, when the selected target equals the stored one, project the stored answers. Resolve only `canonical` deterministically against stored lemmas and proposals, falling back to the live call otherwise.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About -330 ms on every analysis-path first click, plus the removed follow-ups. Intake grows by one sequential round per sentence (~0.4-1.2 s), which is acceptable if intake is async.
hypotheses.risk: Mixed-route batching is unmeasured (grammar-batch only tested nouns). The state grows with all routes' policy text. Dictionary-dependent parts (canonical alternatives) must stay at click time. This is a large design change.
hypotheses.experiment: Extend prototypes/intake/grammar-batch.ts to mixed routes: noun, verb and adjective cases with decoys of other routes from the same sentence, each carrying its own route policy. Compare solo vs batched on the noun (45), verb (77) and adjective (32) eval cases, 2 runs each. Only if batched ≥ solo, build the store-and-project prototype and time tf-demo clicks.

audits.stage: Click-time grammar: resolveGrammar (battery/dumgen/src/concrete-lang/de/production.ts:115-226) → resolveGrammarJudgments (grammatical-resolution/judgments.ts:130-844) and its follow-ups (authored-identity.ts, noun-article.ts, the Luna text call, the lexical-strings call)
audits.howItWorks:
Critical path: nothing after grammar can start until it returns. tf-demo calls dumgen.resolveGrammar(encounter, context.lemmaCandidates) at app/tf-demo/server/linguisticOrchestration.ts:633. The draftKnowledge fork (l.480), findStoredReadings (l.505) and the emoji stage all need the resolved Lemma, so every grammar millisecond is click latency. An 'Unresolved' failure is caught at l.644 and the whole click is saved as Unresolved.

Inputs: lemmaCandidates come from convex/resolutionContext.ts:92-168. That query takes up to 64 spellings (clicked word, 1-4-word phrases around it, every word in the sentence, each in three casings) and collects Lemmas whose canonicalForm or Surface normalizedSurface matches, up to 64 Lemmas. judgments.ts:152-165 keeps only Lemmas of the same route. Their headwords become canonicalFormAlternatives. For NOUN, the raw members (including the article) are added as alternatives too.

Round trip 1, always: one jev 'features' batch (judgments.ts:193-362).
- State: markedContext, members, route, canonicalFormCandidate (the members joined with spaces), canonicalFormAlternatives, storedLemmas (full Lemma objects), a policy object and reviewedIdentities.
  - policy = sharedPolicy (≈560 tokens) + for verbal kinds verbalIdentity (225) and verbalComposition (917) + for NOUN nounPolicy + for partial kinds coveragePolicy + routeGuidance (0 for VERB/AUX, 989 for PRON).
  - NOUN also gets the indexed sentence, the target and articlePolicy (371).
  - VERB also gets lexicalStringCandidates.
- Questions (7-29 per call):
  - support, spelling, historicalStatus;
  - inflection, when the schema has a bag;
  - every catalog feature (NOUN article/case, verbal voice and AUX Lemma features excluded);
  - orthography_i and normalization_i per member;
  - coverage (Idiom, DiscourseFormula, Proverb, Aphorism);
  - identity for AUX, or canonical for every other route except DET;
  - speculative NOUN attachment and Case;
  - speculative VERB text.hasSepPrefix (all character prefixes of every member);
  - governedPreposition (multi-member verbal targets).
- selected() (l.364-374) turns any Unresolved answer into a failure of the whole click. support is read first (l.383).

Follow-ups, strictly sequential:
- (a) DET/PRON (l.525-537): a code lookup, locateAuthoredIdentity. If it does not give a unique Hit, one jev 'identity' call runs (authored-identity.ts:32-63), even when the compatible list is empty. DET NoMatch becomes CatalogMiss. PRON NoMatch falls back to the canonical answer.
- (b) Luna gpt-5.6-luna text generation (l.608-690) when canonical=CandidateIsNotCanonical (and the Lemma is not authored or copied mechanically) and/or any normalization=Generate.
  - Input: markedContext, members, route, needed, judgedCore, governedPreposition, canonicalFormPolicy.
  - The judged Surface bag is sent only when members must be generated (l.641-647).
- (c) VERB only (l.705-766): a jev 'lexical-strings' call when hasSepPrefix=Present and the speculative string was not chosen. Its candidates are all prefixes of normalized members plus canonical-form words.
- (d) NOUN only: resolveNounArticle (noun-article.ts:131-266) derives Case from the attached article. A jev 'NOUN/case' call runs only when more than one compatible case remains and the speculative Case is not among them.

Output: code builds the output and validates it against the route schema. production.ts turns it into the Attestation and raises CatalogMiss for unauthored closed routes. Worst sequential chains: VERB features→Luna→lexical-strings, NOUN features→Luna→case, PRON features→identity→Luna.

Measured (4 stored verb runs, .runs/dumgen/{60813031,11c68aae,55488b4d,e3220fab}, 308 ops):
- features p50 320 ms / p90 379 ms, 5.56k input and 1.2k output tokens.
- Luna canonical call fired in 171 of 308 ops, p50 828 ms, p90 1238 ms, max 13 s.
- Op p50 1032-1044 ms.

Offline 'perfect judge' replay, no model APIs (/tmp/grammar-audit/oracle.ts): every grammar corpus was run through production resolveGrammar with gold-driven fake judge and executor. On the 880 evaluation cases, a sequential Luna call is needed in 278 (32%): VERB 92%, Idiom 93%, ADJ 69%, Collocation 55%, ADV 53%, CCONJ 52%, ADP 45%, NOUN 42%, X 32%, INTJ/NUM 26%, PART/PROPN 24%, DiscourseFormula 14%, SCONJ 12%, Proverb 11%, Aphorism 8%, SYM 6%, PRON 1%, AUX 0%. When the gold Lemma is offered as a stored candidate, this drops to 40 of 880 (4.5%, all of them typo normalization).

calls.name: features (de/<Family>/<Kind>/features)
calls.when: always
calls.sequentialAfter: selectTarget (stored Sentence Analysis, or the classifyTarget jev fallback) and loadResolutionContext
calls.approxInputTokens: ≈1.5k (CCONJ/SCONJ/INTJ) to ≈6k (VERB/Idiom). Measured VERB p50 5562 input and 1201 output tokens. State ≈1/3 and questions ≈2/3 of chars. storedLemmas add 40-90 tokens per Lemma (up to 64).

Median 7 (CCONJ) to 25 (Idiom/Aphorism) questions.

calls.name: identity (de/Lexeme/DET|PRON/identity)
calls.when: conditional: DET/PRON when locateAuthoredIdentity gives Ambiguous or Gap (not a unique Hit). It fires even when the compatible list is empty and the only options are NoMatch/Unresolved. 1-6% of eval cases under the perfect judge; the real rate is higher because any wrong cell feature causes a Gap.
