calls.when: conditional: canonical=CandidateIsNotCanonical (Lemma not authored and not a mechanical DiscourseFormula/Proverb/Aphorism copy) or any normalization=Generate. Perfect judge: 32% of eval cases, 92% VERB. Measured: 171/308 VERB ops (56%, lower only because 71 ops wrongly accepted the candidate and 43 failed on support first).
calls.sequentialAfter: features (and the PRON identity call when it fires)
calls.approxInputTokens: ≈275 input tokens, ≈17 output tokens (measured). Provider processing p50 ≈590 ms, total p50 828 ms, p95 1668 ms, p99 3.8 s, max 13 s. No timeout is set.

calls.name: lexical-strings (de/Lexeme/VERB/lexical-strings)
calls.when: conditional: VERB with hasSepPrefix=Present when speculative text.hasSepPrefix was not answered with a candidate. 8/308 ops (2.6%); all 8 then failed 'Unresolved hasSepPrefix'.
calls.questions: hasSepPrefix: text_i over every character prefix of every normalized member and canonical word, + Unresolved

calls.name: NOUN/case (de/Lexeme/NOUN/case)
calls.when: conditional: NOUN with a marked bag when more than one Case is compatible with the attached article and the speculative Case is not among them or is Unresolved. Design A measured 1.09 jev calls per noun case, so ≈9%.

unusedOrRedundantInputs: storedLemmas (judgments.ts:335): full Lemma objects (40-90 tokens each, up to 64, so ≤5.7k tokens for PRON). No question refers to `storedLemmas`; only their canonicalForm strings are used, and those are already in canonicalFormAlternatives and again in the canonical question's options. The evaluation harness (src/evaluation/grammar-operation.ts:94) never passes lemmaCandidates, so this whole path, including distractor effects, is untested.
reviewedIdentities (judgments.ts:354): sent as [] on every non-AUX route. On AUX it repeats the identity options, which are already JSON.stringify(lemma) (≈140 tokens twice).

policy.route (judgments.ts:352): the empty string for VERB and AUX (routeGuidance has no VERB/AUX key), yet the spelling (l.202) and inflection (feature-questions.ts:585) questions say 'Under `policy.route`'.

NOUN: nounArticleState adds `sentence` (indexedContext) and `target`, which repeat markedContext and the membership. canonicalFormAlternatives includes the article member itself ('den', 'Die') as a candidate headword (judgments.ts:161).

canonical question asked but not used: PRON 100% of eval cases (the Lemma comes from the authored lookup), DiscourseFormula 89%, Proverb/Aphorism 92% (mechanical copy). Speculative text.hasSepPrefix is ignored in 85% of VERB clicks; NUM/SYM case/gender/number in 87% (Citation). Per-call latency does not grow with question count, so this is noise, not latency.

Intake outputs computed and thrown away at click time: selectAnalysisTarget returns only family/kind/memberSegmentIndices (app/tf-demo/server/sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:82). Member roles (Article, GovernedPreposition, SeparableParticle, Reflexive, Expletive, Auxiliary) and the DET/PRON identity mass never reach resolveGrammar. Passing the roles is not worth it for accuracy: in the stored VERB runs grammar-time lexicallyReflexive, expletive, perfect and future are 308/308 or 300/300 correct.

text.hasSepPrefix candidate list: every character prefix of every member in both casings ('a','an','ang','ange',…,'angekündigt'), p50 9 and max 24 options, asked on every VERB click, although the string can be derived in code from the canonical form (15/15 gold).
promptProblems: judgments.ts:108 sharedPolicy.identity says 'Spelling Canonical does not mean Grundform: finite and declined forms may be Canonical.' This is about the `spelling` label but uses the same word as the canonical options ('CandidateIsCanonical'). In the stored VERB runs jev accepted an inflected candidate as the headword in 71/308 ops (23%), including 'erholt sich' with P≈0.9, 'Lauf', 'bekommt', 'darf', 'es gibt' and 'hat'. These ops write a wrong Lemma without failing.

judgments.ts:110 policy.canonicalForm says 'Inflection does not prevent identical spelling.' and the only example (l.346) is 'finite gehen has Canonical Form gehen'. Both encourage accepting inflected forms. There is no counterexample (erholt sich → sich erholen, ging → gehen).

judgments.ts:281: the canonical question warns only 'do not copy an inflected noun just because its spelling is Canonical'. There is no equivalent warning for verbs or adjectives, which are the routes that fail.

judgments.ts:195 support: 'Under `policy`, can the fixed target in `markedContext` support a coherent analysis on `route`?' This is a meta-judgment over the whole ≈1.7k-token policy, together with policy.target 'Return Unresolved when a valid analysis is not defensible.' It answered Unresolved on 43/308 VERB ops although no VERB case has gold Unresolved: 22% of multi-member targets, 7% of single-member ones. It also reacts to unrelated policy text: the wip-adr0029 wording raised support failures from 8 to 14-15 per 77-case run.

judgments.ts:99-100 and 736-737, Unresolved option for lexical strings: 'None is defensible, or the feature is Absent; do not revise the feature judgment'. Because the speculative question is asked even when the feature is Absent, Unresolved is the right answer 85% of the time. When it is Present, the options are raw character prefixes, and jev still chose Unresolved in 10/44 gold-Present cases.

text-guidance.ts:8 VERB canonical guidance says 'never the whole auxiliary chain' but not 'never the auxiliary itself'. The Luna input omits the judged perfect/future/passive bag when only canonicalForm is requested (judgments.ts:641-647). Luna returned werden for 'wird finden'/'wird reisen', bekommen for 'bekommt geliefert' and haben for 'hätt bestellt': 7/57 errors on targets with an auxiliary, against 0/114 without.
verbal-guidance.ts:16 'Membership and the VERB/ADJ route are fixed.' ADJ never receives this text (verbal kinds only). Line 14 also has a stray line-break artifact (' Its grammatical auxiliaries').

feature-questions.ts:154-191 ADP governedCase offers 29 non-German cases (Abessive, Benefactive, …, Terminative) next to Nom/Acc/Dat/Gen for a German adposition. The ADP corpus gold uses only Gen/Dat/Acc/null.

feature-questions.ts:521-522, Unresolved option on every feature: 'This feature applies, but the supplied evidence does not support a defensible value; do not use Unmarked for uncertainty'. Every such Unresolved kills the whole click through selected(). For low-stakes features (historicalStatus, hyph, abbr, foreign) a safe default would be better than a failure.

Several VERB-side instructions point at state fields that are absent or empty. 'Under `policy.route`' is empty for VERB/AUX. The canonical question also mentions alternatives, which are always empty in evaluation and for first encounters in tf-demo.

hypotheses.title: Add code-generated headword candidates to canonicalFormAlternatives so the sequential Luna call is not needed
hypotheses.claim: Inflected, sentence-initial and discontinuous targets never have their headword among the alternatives, so a correct judge must answer CandidateIsNotCanonical and a sequential Luna call (p50 828 ms) follows. Many of these headwords can be derived in code, and a jev Choice over them costs no extra round trip.
hypotheses.evidence: canonicalFormCandidate is members.join(' ') (judgments.ts:151). Alternatives are stored headwords plus NOUN members only (l.158-165). Perfect-judge replay: Luna needed in 278/880 eval cases (VERB 92%, ADJ 69%, ADV 53%, CCONJ 52%, ADP 45%, NOUN 42%). Of the 274 canonical-form cases, 60 are trivially derivable: 28 are the lowercase-initial joined candidate ('Und→und', 'Vielleicht→vielleicht', 'Nachdem→nachdem'), 20 are ellipsis-joined correlators ('entweder oder→entweder … oder'), 7 are one member ('wird reisen→reisen', 'warten auf→warten') and 5 are reordered ('sehnen sich nach→sich sehnen'). A rules-only prototype (/tmp/grammar-audit/candgen.py: suffix stripping, ge-/zu- removal, separable-particle reattachment, 'sich X', a closed sein/haben/werden/modal table, adjective/noun stems with umlaut reversal) covers 131/274 (48%): VERB 49/71, ADJ 17/22, CCONJ 17/27, ADP 11/15, NOUN 10/19, ADV 13/26. It yields a median of 5 candidates. With a correct candidate offered, perfect-judge Luna falls from 278 to 40 of 880. Stored-run replay: VERB ops take p50 1162 ms with Luna and 320 ms without.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In resolveGrammarJudgments, add to canonicalFormAlternatives, for every route: the lowercase-initial joined candidate; ' … '-joined members when the members are not adjacent; each member and its lowercase-initial form; for verbal targets, 'sich '+X when a reflexive member exists. Add per-route morphological candidates: VERB stems of the lexical (non-auxiliary) member with any detached separable particle reattached, plus a closed table for sein/haben/werden/modals (authored AUX realizations can supply the sein/haben/werden forms); ADJ/ADV degree/declension stems; NOUN/PROPN plural and genitive stems. Exclude article spellings. Keep CandidateIsNotCanonical as the fallback to Luna.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Luna removed from roughly half of the clicks that need it now (48% of eval-set Luna cases; probably more on real text, which has fewer typos). VERB replay p50 1066 → ≈330-400 ms, p90 1447 → ≈1.2 s. Each removed call saves p50 828 ms and the 13 s tail. Reliability: jev gets an explicit correct option instead of choosing between an inflected candidate and 'missing text', which should cut the 23% false CandidateIsCanonical on VERB (see false-candidate-is-canonical).
hypotheses.risk: Near-miss distractors ('etabliern' next to 'etablieren', 'liegn') could be selected, giving wrong Lemmas with no failure. More options per Choice. The strong-verb, idiom and suspended-compound residual still needs Luna.
hypotheses.experiment: On a variant branch (bun run build:js), run bun --env-file=../../.env.local cli/evaluate.ts --experiment grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/{verb,adjective,noun,adverb,adposition,coordinating-conjunction} and grammatical-resolution/de/phraseme/idiom --revision <label> --judgment-timeout 30000. Do 2 baseline and 2 variant runs, since the stored runs predate governedPreposition. Compare contractPass case by case and read .runs/dumgen/<run>/cases.jsonl traces for Luna rate, canonicalForm accuracy (split into CandidateIsCanonical / candidate_i / NotCanonical) and op p50/p90. Accept if Luna calls drop by at least 30% and no case regresses beyond the ~5-case noise.

hypotheses.title: Stop letting the 'support' question fail Lexeme clicks; keep it only for Collocation and other gold-Unresolved routes
hypotheses.claim: 'support' is the single largest cause of whole-click failures on VERB, and on these corpora it catches nothing the other questions would miss.
hypotheses.evidence: Stored VERB runs: 43/308 ops failed with 'Unresolved applicable question support' (15/14/6/8 per 77-case run); the verb corpus has 0 gold-Unresolved cases. P(Unresolved) was 0.50-0.90 on failures and ≤0.49 on passes. By target size: 32/148 multi-member ops failed (22%) and 11/160 single-member ops (7%). In 27/43 of the failures, all other feature answers matched gold (/tmp/grammar-audit/supportcounterfactual.py). Across all 21 grammar corpora only 18 eval cases are gold Unresolved: Collocation 7, PRON genitive holes and foreign 8, DET foreign 1, NOUN 'den Haus' 1. It is sensitive to unrelated policy wording (wip-adr0029: 14-15 failures against 8 at baseline).
hypotheses.proposedChange: Remove `support` from the Lexeme question batch, or record it as an event without calling selected(). Keep it for Phraseme/Collocation, where routeGuidance relies on it for 'free composition / idiom contradicts the route'. Incoherent answers still fail through the schema parse (IncoherentApplicableFeatures, judgments.ts:599-607).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 10-19% fewer VERB whole-click failures (6-15 of 77 per run), roughly 60% of them becoming correct attestations. Similar gains are likely on other multi-member routes (NOUN with article, ADP circumpositions, CCONJ correlators). No latency change.
hypotheses.risk: Misassembled targets (the P4 stray-article case) could produce a wrong Attestation instead of Unresolved. assembleTarget's multi-article guard and the intake membership matrix reduce this. The gold-Unresolved PRON genitive-hole cases must still end Unresolved or CatalogMiss.
hypotheses.experiment: Variant without support on Lexeme routes. Run all 21 grammatical-resolution/de/* experiments, 2 runs baseline and 2 variant. Metrics: count of 'Unresolved applicable question support', contractPass case by case, and outcomes on the 18 gold-Unresolved eval cases (collocation, pronoun jedes/jedwedes/jegliches Gen, foreign he/All/the, noun dev-bad-agreement). Also rerun prototypes/p4-noun-article-membership.ts eval to check that garbage assemblies still fail.

hypotheses.title: Fix the wrong 'CandidateIsCanonical' answers (23% of VERB ops) with an infinitive-shape guard and clearer wording
hypotheses.claim: jev accepts inflected verb forms as headwords. The wrong Lemma is persisted and reused by later clicks (findAttestationForSegmentValue), and it becomes a lemmaCandidate for future clicks.
hypotheses.evidence: Stored VERB runs: canonical answer against gold gives CandidateIsNotCanonical correct 213, false CandidateIsCanonical 71, CandidateIsCanonical correct 24. Examples: 'erholt sich' (P 0.86-0.92), 'erinnert sich an', 'Lauf', 'bekommt', 'darf', 'es gibt', 'hat'. Failure breakdown of the 308 VERB ops: 168 pass, 51 op failures (43 support, 8 hasSepPrefix), 77 wrong canonicalForm, only 14 with any other mismatch. A deterministic check (headword = optional 'sich ' + one lowercase word ending in -en/-ln/-rn/-un, or sein/tun) catches 63/71 false acceptances and wrongly rejects 0 true ones. Luna is 164/171 correct when it runs. Misleading wording: judgments.ts:108 and l.110 (see promptProblems).
hypotheses.proposedChange: (1) VERB-only code guard: if canonical=CandidateIsCanonical and the candidate is not infinitive-shaped, treat it as CandidateIsNotCanonical (or as a code candidate from code-canonical-candidates). (2) Rename the options to 'CandidateIsHeadword'/'HeadwordDiffers'. Remove 'finite and declined forms may be Canonical' from policy.identity, or say that spelling=Canonical says nothing about headword identity. Add counterexamples ('erholt sich → sich erholen', 'ging → gehen', 'rote → rot') to policy.canonicalForm.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: On VERB, ≈+14 correct lemmas per 77-case run, the largest single accuracy gain available. On its own the guard adds a Luna call (≈+830 ms) to about 20% of VERB clicks; together with code-canonical-candidates most of these become 0-cost candidate selections.
hypotheses.risk: The wording change may move other routes (it is shared policy), and ADJ/NOUN answers could shift either way. The guard is VERB-specific. Finite plural forms that look like infinitives ('kamen') are not caught.
hypotheses.experiment: Two variants: A = guard only (code), B = guard plus wording. Run grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb (2 runs each) and, for B, every route that asks the canonical question (adjective, noun, adverb, adposition, coordinating-conjunction, idiom). Metrics: canonical confusion matrix from traces, contractPass case by case, Luna rate and p50.

hypotheses.title: Derive the hasSepPrefix string in code; drop the lexical-strings follow-up and the speculative prefix question
hypotheses.claim: Once jev has judged hasSepPrefix=Present (302/308 correct) and the canonical form is known, the prefix string is deterministic. Asking jev to pick it among raw character prefixes causes an extra round trip and a fatal Unresolved.
hypotheses.evidence: Speculative text.hasSepPrefix on gold-Present cases: 34/44 correct, 10 Unresolved (p50 9 and max 24 options such as 'a','an','ang','ange'). The follow-up fired in 8/308 ops (p50 306 ms) and all 8 failed 'Unresolved hasSepPrefix' ('angekündigt' → Unresolved 0.66, 'weitergeleitet' 0.86, 'ausgesprochen' 0.85). Code derivation (longest closed-list separable particle that starts the canonical headword after 'sich ') matches gold in 15/15 VERB corpus cases. Code: judgments.ts:60-91, 308-312, 694-766.
hypotheses.proposedChange: When hasSepPrefix=Present, set core.hasSepPrefix to the longest particle from a closed German separable-particle list (ab, an, auf, aus, bei, ein, fest, fort, her*, hin*, los, mit, nach, vor*, weg, weiter, zu, zurück, zusammen, …, plus ambiguous durch/über/um/unter/wider/wieder, which stay gated by jev's Present) that prefixes the canonical headword and appears in a member or its detached particle. Remove text.hasSepPrefix. Keep the lexical-strings call only as a fallback when no particle matches.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes one jev round trip (~306 ms) on ~3% of VERB clicks and 2.6% of VERB whole-click failures (4/77 in the baseline run). Also removes one noisy question from every VERB call.
hypotheses.risk: Lexicalized particle verbs outside the list, and ambiguous particles when jev's Present is wrong (it was wrong 6/308 times).
hypotheses.experiment: Variant on grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb, 2 runs each. Metrics: 'Unresolved hasSepPrefix' count, lexical-strings call count, coreFeatures.hasSepPrefix accuracy against gold. Offline check first: run the derivation over all VERB and Idiom gold in the corpora.

hypotheses.title: Start the Luna canonical-form call in parallel with the features call on routes that usually need it
hypotheses.claim: On VERB, Idiom, ADJ, Collocation, ADV, CCONJ, ADP and NOUN the features call and the Luna call are serial, although Luna needs almost nothing from the features answers.
hypotheses.evidence: Replay of stored VERB traces: successful Luna-path ops take p50 1162 / p90 1687 ms. With max(features, Luna) instead of the sum: p50 835 / p90 1265. All successful ops: p50 1066 → 742, p90 1447 → 1047. The Luna input (judgments.ts:621-640) uses judgedCore (hasSepPrefix, lexicallyReflexive, verbType) and governedPreposition only as hints; the rest is markedContext, members and the policy. Perfect-judge Luna need: VERB 92%, Idiom 93% (code candidates cover 0/25 idioms). Cost per extra call: 275 input tokens × $0.40/M + 17 output tokens × $2.40/M ≈ $0.00015.
hypotheses.proposedChange: For routes where NotCanonical is at least ~40% under the perfect judge, fire generateCanonicalForm at the same time as the features judge, on a child AbortSignal. If the answer is candidate_i or CandidateIsCanonical, abort it or throw it away. If the answer is NotCanonical, use it only if it agrees with the judged core: 'sich ' prefix iff lexicallyReflexive; derived separable particle present; governed preposition absent. Otherwise re-run the current sequential call. Record dependsOn=[] for the speculative call.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: ≈-320 ms p50 and ≈-400 ms p90 on Luna-path clicks. Before code-canonical-candidates this is ~60% of VERB clicks; after it, mostly Idiom and Collocation plus the VERB/ADJ residual. Extra cost about $0.00015 per click.
hypotheses.risk: Without judgedCore, Luna may disagree with jev (reflexive, prefix), which triggers a sequential fallback and makes that click slower than today. There are more trace calls. The benefit shrinks if code-canonical-candidates removes most Luna use.
hypotheses.experiment: Offline check: re-run the 164 stored VERB Luna inputs with judgedCore and governedPreposition removed (a direct executeGeneration script) and compare with gold and with the judged core. That is 164 Luna calls. Then run a variant on grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb and phraseme/idiom, 2 runs each. Metrics: op p50/p90 from traces, rate of speculative results rejected for inconsistency, canonicalForm accuracy.

hypotheses.title: Prefetch resolveGrammar at intake for every Sentence Analysis target and hand it to the click as checkpoints.grammatical
hypotheses.claim: When a click is served by the stored Sentence Analysis, its target is decided at intake, so grammar can run before the click. That removes the whole grammar stage (320 ms to 1.1 s p50) from the click path without changing dumgen.
hypotheses.evidence: selectAnalysisTarget is a pure function of the stored analysis (app/tf-demo/server/sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:33-83). resolveSegment already skips grammar when checkpoints.grammatical is given (linguisticOrchestration.ts:450-452). Stored VERB grammar: p50 1066 / p90 1447 ms; no-Luna ops 322 ms. The intake README grammar-batch experiment found that marking other targets in the same sentence does not degrade feature accuracy (15 → 22-23 all-correct). About 5.4 targets per sentence. Cost per target ≈ jev 5.5k tokens × $0.042/M = $0.00023, plus ~0.5 × $0.00015 Luna ≈ $0.0003.
hypotheses.proposedChange: After persistSubmittedText (or lazily when a sentence scrolls into view), run dumgen.resolveGrammar for each resolvedUnitAt target in the background, with the same lemmaCandidates query. Store the ResolvedGrammatical keyed by (sentenceId, memberSegmentIndices, route). At click time, pass it as checkpoints.grammatical when the selected analysis target matches; otherwise resolve as today.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 0.3 s (most routes) to 1.1 s (VERB, ADJ, Idiom) off every click served by the analysis, before the emoji stage starts. The largest grammar-side speed lever. Intake latency is unchanged if the prefetch runs in the background.
hypotheses.risk: Paid work for unclicked words (≈$0.0016 per sentence, 5x or more waste if about one word per sentence is clicked). Prefetched lemmaCandidates go stale as the dictionary grows. Needs storage and invalidation and uses jev capacity. Clicks that fall back to classification get nothing. A prefetch failure must not be persisted as a click result.
hypotheses.experiment: (1) Offline hit rate: using stored intake runs (.runs/dumgen/72ecf520… sentence-analysis/de) and the target-classification clicks, count clicks where selectAnalysisTarget is non-null and equal to the gold target. (2) Live in tf-demo: submit a 20-sentence text with the prefetch on, click 30 words, and compare the click critical path from inspection traces against the same text without the prefetch. Record the prefetch cost per sentence.

hypotheses.title: Stop Luna choosing the auxiliary as the headword: send the judged bag and name the lexical verb
hypotheses.claim: All Luna canonical-form errors are on targets with an auxiliary. Luna returns the auxiliary's infinitive because it is not told which member is the auxiliary.
hypotheses.evidence: Stored VERB runs: Luna canonicalForm correct 50/57 on auxiliary-bearing targets and 114/114 otherwise. Errors: 'wird finden→werden', 'wird reisen→werden', 'bekommt geliefert→bekommen', 'hätt bestellt→haben'. judgedSurface is sent only when members must be generated (judgments.ts:641-647). text-guidance.ts:8 says only 'never the whole auxiliary chain'. prototypes/intake derive-aux.ts identifies the serving auxiliary from the target's shape in 21/22 and 18/18 cases.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Always include judgedSurface (perfect, future, passive, verbForm) in the canonical-form request for verbal routes. Add to canonicalFormGuidance.VERB: 'With a perfect, future or passive auxiliary (hat gesungen, wird finden, bekommt geliefert, hätt bestellt) the headword is the lexical verb's infinitive (singen, finden, liefern, bestellen), never the auxiliary's.' With code-canonical-candidates, the non-auxiliary member's stem also becomes a candidate.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Fixes ≈12% of Luna outputs on auxiliary-bearing verb targets (≈2 cases per 77-case VERB run). No latency change.
hypotheses.risk: Very low. The wording applies to the VERB text route only.
hypotheses.experiment: Re-run the 57 stored auxiliary-target Luna inputs with the new input and guidance (direct executeGeneration script, 2 samples each), then run a variant on grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb. Metric: canonicalForm accuracy on the future, perfect, passive and recipient-passive cases.

hypotheses.title: Skip the DET/PRON identity follow-up when no reviewed identity is compatible; measure how often it fires
hypotheses.claim: resolveAuthoredGrammarIdentity makes a sequential jev call even when compatible is empty, and then the only possible answers are NoMatch or Unresolved. For DET both are failures; for PRON the choice only decides whether the click fails.
hypotheses.evidence: authored-identity.ts:23-63 calls judgmentCaller for any non-Hit status, with options identity_i over located.compatible plus NoMatch and Unresolved. compatible requires exact equality of all Core features (realizations.ts:248-252), so one wrong PRON cell feature out of 11 gives an empty list. Perfect judge: the follow-up fires in 1-6% of cases; the live rate is unknown because no stored PRON/DET runs exist. The intake README (#509) says PRON errors are mostly cells: 24-25 wrong-cell selections out of 212.
hypotheses.proposedChange: If located.compatible is empty, skip the call. DET → CatalogMiss directly. PRON → the current NoMatch path, or Unresolved if the product prefers that. Longer term, evaluate an in-batch speculative identity Choice over spelling-enumerated candidates (candidatesFor(text), mean 4.5 options) so no follow-up is ever needed.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: ≈-310 ms on DET/PRON clicks whose features miss the authored cell; the size depends on the measured miss rate. No change for hits.
hypotheses.risk: Low for the skip. The PRON fallback builds a non-authored PRON Lemma from possibly wrong features, which is already the current NoMatch behaviour and should be reviewed separately.
hypotheses.experiment: First run grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/pronoun and determiner (1 run) and count AuthoredRealizationLookup event statuses (Hit/Ambiguous/Gap), whether compatible is empty, and identity-call outcomes in the traces. If Gaps with an empty compatible list are at least 5%, run the variant twice on both corpora.

hypotheses.title: (Second step) Generate headword candidates for every word at intake with one Luna call per sentence
hypotheses.claim: Candidates that code cannot produce (strong verbs, irregular adjectives, idioms, suspended compounds) could be generated once per sentence at intake and served as alternatives at click time.
hypotheses.evidence: Perfect judge: offering the correct Lemma as a candidate cuts sequential Luna from 278/880 to 40/880 eval cases (/tmp/grammar-audit/oracle-self.json). Rules-only code misses 143/274 (e.g. ging, liest, spricht, kamen, gesungen, mitgebracht, beste→gut, all 25 idioms). Luna provider time is ≈590 ms for a 17-token output, so one per-sentence call costs about the same as one click call.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Next to analyzeSentence (or in the background after persisting), one Luna call per German sentence returns, for each ResolvableText segment and each intake Phraseme target, 1-3 headwords in context (separable-prefix reattachment, 'sich X', idiom dictionary form). Persist the result with the Sentence Analysis. At click time, merge into canonicalFormAlternatives.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes most remaining Luna calls left after code-canonical-candidates (on the eval sets, up to ≈86% of all Luna canonical calls combined). Saves ≈0.8 s on those clicks. Cost ≈$0.0004 per sentence. If run inline, intake gets ≈0.6-0.8 s slower per sentence wave.
hypotheses.risk: A wrong intake candidate can be picked by jev (a wrong Lemma with no failure). It adds intake latency or background complexity and a stored-analysis schema change. It overlaps with code-canonical-candidates, so do it only if the residual stays large.
hypotheses.experiment: Prototype script: run the intake Luna lemmatizer on the grammar corpus sentences, inject its output as lemmaCandidates (the public resolveGrammar API already takes them), and run grammatical-resolution routes verb, adjective, noun and idiom through a prototype harness that passes lemmaCandidates. Compare Luna rate and contractPass against code-candidates-only.

hypotheses.title: Cap the Luna tail with a timeout plus one hedged duplicate request
hypotheses.claim: The grammar text call has no timeout and a heavy tail: 5 of 171 calls took over 2 s, one took 13 s.
hypotheses.evidence: Stored VERB runs: Luna p50 828, p95 1668, p99 3801, max 13067 ms. jev p99 939 ms. No timeout in executeGeneration (universal/model.ts:66-137) or in promptsmith openai.ts. jev has timeoutMs 10000.
hypotheses.proposedChange: For generateCanonicalForm (and the emoji stage), send a second identical request if the first has not returned by ~1.5 s, take the first response, and abort the other. Add an overall timeout.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: p99 of Luna-path grammar from ≈4 s to ≈2.3 s, with about 6% extra Luna calls (≈$0.00001 per click). No effect on p50.
hypotheses.risk: Duplicate billing on hedged calls and more trace complexity. Worth less once code-canonical-candidates removes most of these calls.
hypotheses.experiment: Benchmark script: 200 generateCanonicalForm requests replayed from stored VERB inputs, with and without the hedge. Compare p50/p95/p99 and cost.

hypotheses.title: Default low-stakes Unresolved answers instead of failing the click
hypotheses.claim: Some Unresolved answers that currently fail the whole click have a safe default.
hypotheses.evidence: Stored VERB runs: historicalStatus Unresolved 4/308, spelling 7/308 (all on typo cases 'tanzd' and 'sol', which also fail elsewhere). selected() turns every Unresolved into a failure (judgments.ts:364-374). feature-questions.ts:521 tells jev to prefer Unresolved over Unmarked when uncertain.
hypotheses.proposedChange: historicalStatus Unresolved → Current. Low-stakes Core flags (hyph, abbr, foreign) Unresolved → Unmarked. Keep identity-bearing answers (canonical, identity, attachment, verbForm, case) fatal.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Small: ≈1% fewer whole-click failures on VERB. Likely somewhat more on NUM, SYM and X, which have more flag features.
hypotheses.risk: A rare genuinely Archaic or abbreviation Surface is stored with the default.
hypotheses.experiment: Measure first: in the fresh all-routes baseline run (see drop-support-gate), count 'Unresolved applicable question <id>' per question id. Implement only for ids above 1%.

hypotheses.title: (Hygiene, not speed) Drop storedLemmas from state and start evaluating the lemmaCandidates path
hypotheses.claim: storedLemmas is never referenced by a question, and the dictionary-candidate path is never exercised by any evaluation.
hypotheses.evidence: judgments.ts:335 puts full Lemma objects in state (40-90 tokens each; with 64 Lemmas ≈2.5-5.7k tokens). Only their canonicalForm strings are used, and those are already in canonicalFormAlternatives and the canonical question's options. tf-demo fills candidates from every word of the sentence (resolutionContext.ts:115-168), so other same-kind Lemmas from the sentence appear as distractors. src/evaluation/grammar-operation.ts:94 calls resolveGrammar(encounter) with no candidates. jev latency grows only ≈8 ms per 1k input tokens (intake README).
hypotheses.proposedChange: Remove storedLemmas from state (keep the headword strings), or at most keep coreFeatures for same-headword pairs. Add an evaluation variant that injects the gold Lemma plus 3-5 same-route distractor Lemmas as lemmaCandidates.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Not a speed win: ≈0-40 ms at worst and ≈$0.0002 per call. The real value is a distractor-robustness measurement for the tf-demo path that is untested today.
hypotheses.risk: Low. The Core features of a stored Lemma might currently help consistency; that is unmeasured.
hypotheses.experiment: Prototype harness passing lemmaCandidates (gold + 4 distractors) on grammatical-resolution verb and noun, with and without storedLemmas in state, 2 runs each. Metrics: rate of wrong candidate selection and contractPass.

hypotheses.title: NOT worth it: trimming policy blobs or passing intake roles to grammar for speed
hypotheses.claim: Cutting verbalComposition (917 tokens), PRON route guidance (989) or shared policy, dropping unused questions, or passing intake member roles into grammar will not measurably change click latency or accuracy. Only the specific contradictions listed under promptProblems should be fixed.
hypotheses.evidence: jev latency is flat across 21-29 questions and 5.2-6.8k input tokens in the stored VERB runs (features p50 320 ms, near the 310 ms floor). The intake README shows only ≈8 ms per 1k tokens (1.5k → 10k tokens: 358 → 422 ms). Features judged under the big verbal policy are already accurate: perfect/future/expletive/lexicallyReflexive/verbType/number 100%, passive 296/300, person 291/292. Input cost is $0.042/M, so 5.5k tokens ≈ $0.00023 per call. The losses are canonicalForm (77), support (43) and hasSepPrefix (8), not feature questions. Merging canonical-form generation into the emoji Luna call is also rejected: the Reading lookup needs the Lemma first, and the project memory warns against bundling text into the emoji call.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Do not spend effort on token trimming or passing roles. Fix only the contradictory sentences (judgments.ts:108 and l.110, verbal-guidance.ts:16, governedCase options, empty policy.route) as part of false-candidate-is-canonical.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Saves ≤20 ms per click if done anyway, so it is not worth the risk of moving accuracy. The intake README recorded a collapse (114 vs ~160) after rewording shipped criteria.
hypotheses.risk: Rewording shared policy can shift answers on many routes; any wording change needs the all-routes regression run.
hypotheses.experiment: None needed for the speed claim. If policy text is trimmed anyway, run all 21 grammatical-resolution experiments twice and compare case by case.

audits.stage: Reading resolution: resolveOrGenerateReadingEmojiDescription (dumgen reading-emoji-description/resolve.ts, driven by the resolveReading step in tf-demo server/linguisticOrchestration.ts)
audits.howItWorks:
Click path in tf-demo (app/tf-demo/server/linguisticOrchestration.ts). Once resolveGrammar returns (L450-452), the orchestrator forks draftKnowledge. The fork runs 4 Luna text drafts, preceded by 2 Convex queries and a dynamic import (L478-488). The orchestrator then runs two Convex hops together and waits for both (Effect.all, L489-516): observer.grammarAvailable, a mutation of about 42 ms p50, and dictionary.findStoredReadings(lemma), a query of about 29 ms p50 that throws above 40 readings (convex/dumdictStorage/storage.ts:29, queries.ts:54-58). resolveReading (L739-777) passes only the emoji strings of the stored readings to dumgen. Stored definitions are dropped at this point.

Inside dumgen (resolve.ts):
(0) Input goes through parse, validateEncounter and agreement (production.ts:227-246). Candidates are deduplicated.
(1) If the lemma has more than one reviewed authored Reading (only 4 of 875 authored lemma groups: AUX sein, haben, werden and PRON es), one jev choice runs (L42-81). State is markedContext, members, and readings with emoji and definition. Criteria are the German definitions plus Unresolved. Unresolved throws Unresolved, which fails the whole click.
(2) A single authored member returns its emoji with no model call (L82-85). Reuse is chosen if the emoji is among the candidates, otherwise New. Closed routes (AUX and DET) without a member give CatalogMiss (L86-92).
(3) More than 253 candidates gives Unresolved (L93-99). This is unreachable in tf-demo because the host caps at 40.
(4) With at least one candidate, one jev compare runs (L100-151). State is markedContext, members, the full lemma object and the candidates array. The candidate_i criteria are bare emoji strings, plus NoMatch and Unresolved. A candidate choice returns Reuse. Unresolved fails the click. NoMatch falls through.
(5) Luna generation runs through textModelCaller (L152-163; universal/model.ts:33-63). Model is gpt-5.6-luna with reasoning none and service_tier fast (the response reports priority). Output is text. cachePrompt is true, and promptsmith/openai.ts:33-50 sends prompt_cache_options explicit plus an explicit breakpoint on the developer message. The system prompt is prompts['reading-generation/de']: 7,944 chars, a body plus 25 demonstrations, about 1,950 tokens. Input is {markedContext, lemma: canonicalForm}. There is no timeout and no retry; the judge, by contrast, has a 10 s timeout (trace.ts:24).
(6) If the generated emoji equals a candidate that jev rejected, the stage throws InvalidModelOutput (L164-170). This was introduced in commit dcf189f1 on 2026-09-17, replacing the earlier collision-to-Reuse behaviour.

Back in tf-demo: readingAvailable is saved (about 38 ms) and the UI Reading card shows the emoji. A New reading then joins the draft fiber (Fiber.join); a Reuse polls it and drops unfinished drafts (L553-566). Then persistResolvedClick runs.

Measured in the local Convex inspection data (app/tf-demo/.convex/local/default sqlite, read-only):
- Reading starts about 40-50 ms after grammar ends.
- The Luna emoji call took 848-3491 ms over 16 calls: p50 about 1.34 s, and 5 of 16 at or above 2.6 s.
- Caching works: cached_tokens is 1552/1581 and 1922/1950.
- The TLS connection was fresh on 14 of 16 calls (connectionMs 65-240).
- 0 of 26 reading resolutions exercised the stored-candidate compare. The compare path's live frequency is therefore unmeasured.
- For New readings, commit waited on drafts after the emoji in 12 of 16 clicks, over 1 s in 5 of them.

calls.name: authoredReadingChoice (jev choice)
calls.when: conditional (lemma has >1 reviewed authored Readings: AUX sein/haben/werden, PRON es)
calls.approxInputTokens: ~600-900 (markedContext, members, 2-4 readings with German definitions; criteria repeat the definitions)

calls.name: storedReadingCompare (jev choice)
calls.when: conditional (non-authored, non-closed route, 1..253 stored candidates)
calls.approxInputTokens: ~400-800 (markedContext, members, full lemma object, candidates array duplicated as criteria)
calls.questions: 1 choice: candidate_i (bare emoji strings) + NoMatch + Unresolved

calls.name: generateReadingEmojiDescription (Luna text)
calls.when: conditional (no candidates, or compare returned NoMatch)
calls.sequentialAfter: storedReadingCompare when candidates exist; otherwise the Effect.all hop
calls.approxInputTokens: ~1,950 total, ~1,922 cached (system prompt with 25 demos) + ~30 uncached user tokens; 6-10 output tokens
calls.questions: n/a (free text, 1-4 emoji graphemes, validated by emojiGenerationOutput schema)

unusedOrRedundantInputs: The compare state repeats `candidates` (resolve.ts:106-108), and the same strings are the text of the candidate_i criteria (L114-119). Every candidate appears twice.
`members` is spread into the compare and authored-choice state by markedContext() (validation.ts:84-89). It duplicates the <TARGET> markup already in markedContext.
The compare state sends the full `lemma` object with coreFeatures (resolve.ts:107). Candidates are already scoped to this exact lemma key, so only canonicalForm carries information.

Missing input rather than redundant: stored ReadingEntry.knowledge.definition (dumdict domain-types.ts:38-44) is loaded by findDumdictStoredReadings but dropped in linguisticOrchestration.ts:754-756. The compare sees only emoji strings, while the authored path uses definitions as criteria (resolve.ts:57-61).

The 253-candidate cap (resolve.ts:93-99) cannot be reached from tf-demo. The host throws a plain Error at 40 readings (MAX_READING_CANDIDATES, convex/dumdictStorage/storage.ts:29, queries.ts:54-58), which surfaces as InternalFailed, not Unresolved.

The 5 demonstrationIds of resolve/source-data.json (key-metaphor, maus-computer, aufstehen-uprising, adp-mit-connector, idiom-mit-den-woelfen-heulen) are not injected anywhere, because jev has no demonstrations. They are still subtracted from the reading-resolution/de evaluation (experiment.ts:89-95), shrinking it from 72 to 67 cases for no benefit.

The generation `lemma` input is only canonicalForm (resolve.ts:160), with no POS or features. It may be largely redundant with the marked surface; hypothesis H2b tests this, and if it holds, generation no longer has to wait for grammar.
promptProblems: Compare question (resolve.ts:113) has a patch for one lemma inside a question that runs for every lemma: "Existential geben in es gibt/es gab means existence or availability and must not reuse its transfer/giving Reading." It is noise for nearly every call, and jev is known to be sensitive to wording (the membership reword dropped accuracy from about 160 to 114).

The compare asks jev to pick the Emoji Description that "represents the marked target's learner-facing concept", but the criteria are bare emoji strings such as "➡️", "🔗", "💬", "✅" and "🔄". Examples from the corpus: Zug has candidates [🚆, 💨, 🧲, ➡️]; um has [🔄, 🔗]. jev has to guess what each emoji means. There are no definitions or example contexts, even though the authored path in the same file uses definitions.

The compare sets "NoMatch means a defensible new concept, not uncertainty between meanings" against Unresolved defined as "The context does not support a defensible selection or no-match judgment." This pushes borderline cases to Unresolved, and Unresolved is a whole-click failure (resolve.ts:132-138). A wrong Reuse or New can be repaired later; a failed click shows the user nothing.
Authored multi-reading question (resolve.ts:55): "distinguish referential it from nonreferential subject es" is also asked when the lemma is AUX sein, haben or werden, where it does not apply.

Generation prompt, emoji count: the body says "Start from the single emoji that already carries the meaning; add another only when it removes a real ambiguity or supplies a missing part", yet 14 of the 25 demonstrations are two-emoji outputs. In run e697bfd8 (held-out, 52 cases: 37 pass, 1 FAIL, 14 needsReview), most review and fail outputs add a second emoji that leaks context or the complement: make-clean 🧹✨ (FAIL, in the rejected list), leave-open 👐🪟, look-delicious 👀😋, seem-tired 👀🫥, fresh-careful ⚠️👐, find-boring 🔎🧠.

Generation prompt, noun markup: no demonstration shows the markup production actually sends for nouns. Noun targets include their article as a member by design, e.g. "<TARGET>Die</TARGET> <TARGET>Banken</TARGET> sind geöffnet." and "<TARGET>Ein</TARGET> <TARGET>Junge</TARGET> überlebt" in the local inspection data. No demo has a split separable verb either, and the body never says a marked article belongs to the noun. The two live samples came out fine (🏦, 👦), so the observed risk is low, but the evaluation does not cover this shape.

Copula and light-verb rule ("Leave the complement out entirely, even as a second emoji") is still violated on held-out cases: sauber machen gives 🧹✨. Older live output: bleiben in 'Morgen bleiben sie geschlossen' gave 🚫🏪, and 'Die Banken sind geöffnet' with lemma 'sind' gave 🏦✅. The lemma 'sind' is itself a separate grammar bug upstream.

The collision failure (resolve.ts:164-170) is labelled InvalidModelOutput with the message "Generated Reading collides with a candidate rejected by TypeSafe". The output is valid; the two models simply disagree. tf-demo reports it as an InvalidOutput provider failure (modelExecution.ts:48-58), which hides the fact that this is a decision conflict.

hypotheses.title: Run the stored-Reading compare at the same time as resolveGrammar, using the surface-owner lemma found at context load
hypotheses.claim: On Reuse clicks (a new occurrence of a lemma already in the dictionary, the main path once the dictionary fills up), time-to-emoji and time-to-commit are grammar (about 320 ms) + hops (about 40 ms) + jev compare (about 310-400 ms), all in sequence. The compare only needs markedContext, the lemma and the stored emoji strings. The lemma is usually knowable before grammar returns: loadResolutionContext already finds lemmas that own a stored Surface whose normalizedSurface equals the clicked member text. A speculative compare for that lemma can run alongside the grammar features call, and its result is used only if grammar resolves to that exact lemma key.
hypotheses.evidence: linguisticOrchestration.ts:489-521: resolveReading waits for grammar, then Effect.all(grammarAvailable, findStoredReadings). convex/resolutionContext.ts:130-161 already queries `surfaces` by normalizedSurface and their owner lemmas. Local inspection: grammar p50 320 ms; Save GrammarAvailable 42 ms; Find stored Readings 29 ms; reading starts about 40-50 ms after grammar ends. Memory: jev latency is about 310 ms and roughly flat, concurrent jev calls are fine (analyzeSentence ran 2 in parallel), and 'a second request is justified only when the next state or options cannot be built without the first answer'. Here the compare options exist before grammar returns.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In tf-demo, extend resolutionContext.load so that, for lemmas owning a surface equal to the clicked member text and matching the analysed target kind, it also returns their stored reading emojis (and definitions, see H6). This is one query with no new hop. In resolveSegment, once the target is known, fork dumgen.resolveOrGenerateReadingEmojiDescription(compare only) for each such lemma (usually 0 or 1) at the same time as resolveGrammar. When grammar returns lemma L: if a speculation exists for lemmaKey(L) with the same candidate set, await it; otherwise interrupt and use today's path. dumgen needs a compare-only entry point or a flag that stops before generation. The commit already rechecks dictionary state.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Reuse clicks with a speculation hit save about 350-400 ms of compare plus about 30-40 ms of findStoredReadings, off a Reuse click of about 0.7-1.0 s after target selection, i.e. about 40-50% of the post-target time. A miss costs one wasted jev call (about $0.0001) and no latency. The hit rate depends on how often the same surface form recurs, and must be measured.
hypotheses.risk: Low for accuracy: the compare call is identical and only the start time changes. Medium engineering: a new dumgen entry point, orchestration branching and trace dependsOn semantics. If the dictionary gains a Reading between context load and compare, the speculation is stale. Keep today's commit-time recheck, or re-run the compare when the candidate sets differ.
hypotheses.experiment: (1) Hit-rate, offline with no API calls: instrument the tf-demo inspection step 'Select target' to log speculativeLemmaKeys and, after grammar, whether lemmaKey(resolved) is among them. Read 50+ organic clicks back from the local Convex sqlite. (2) Latency: prototype script in battery/dumgen/prototypes/ over the 49 reading-resolution/de evaluation cases that have candidates. For each, fire the route's resolveGrammar and the compare together versus in sequence, 3 repeats, interleaved. Report wall time p50/p90 and confirm the decision is unchanged case by case (jev noise: about 11/238 flips between identical runs, so compare per case).

hypotheses.title: Start Luna emoji generation speculatively: (a) alongside the jev compare, (b) at target selection with the member surface as lemma
hypotheses.claim: (a) When candidates exist, Luna starts only after the compare returns NoMatch, adding about 310-400 ms. Luna's input (markedContext, canonicalForm) does not depend on the compare answer, so both can race; on Reuse the Luna call is aborted and discarded. (b) If the lemma string adds little beyond the marked surface, generation can start as soon as the target is known, before resolveGrammar. That hides grammar (about 320 ms, or about 800 ms when that jev call is the click's first on a cold connection) plus the 40 ms of hops.
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:100-163 runs compare then generate in sequence. Luna input is {markedContext, lemma: canonicalForm} only (resolve.ts:157-161). Local inspection: generateReadingEmojiDescription over 16 calls took 848-3491 ms, p50 about 1.34 s. The UI shows the emoji at ReadingAvailable (src/views/resolution-deck.ts:54-58: 'fills in as the emoji and Knowledge arrive'). Emoji cost is about $0.00011 per call (1,922 cached × $0.04/M + about 30 × $0.40/M + about 8 × $2.40/M).
hypotheses.proposedChange: (a) In resolve.ts, when candidates.length > 0 and there is no authored or closed route, start the text generation with a child AbortController at the same time as the judgment. Abort it on Reuse or Unresolved and await it on NoMatch. The collision check stays. (b) Only if the experiment passes: a dumgen entry point generateReadingEmojiDraft({encounter}) that uses the joined member texts as `lemma`. tf-demo forks it right after selectTarget, and resolveReading uses its result when the decision is New.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: (a) Saves about 310-400 ms of time-to-emoji on NoMatch clicks only, for about $0.0001 of waste per Reuse click. (b) Saves about 360 ms on every New-reading click (about 25-30% of today's grammar-end-to-emoji time), more on cold jev connections. Time-to-commit for New readings improves only when the emoji is the slowest leg: in 12 of 16 local New clicks, commit waited on draftKnowledge after the emoji was ready.
hypotheses.risk: (a) None for quality, since inputs are identical; only the trace order changes (tests/reading.test.ts expects calls ['TypeSafe','Luna']). (b) The surface differs from the canonical form for inflected verbs, split separable verbs, plural nouns and phrasemes. Quality could drop, and it must be measured case by case.
hypotheses.experiment: (a) A prototype variant of the reading-resolution/de operation that races, 67 cases × 3 repeats alternated with baseline. Metric: wall time per case, identical decisions. (b) A sample-reading.ts-style run on reading-generation/de (52 held-out cases), variant 'lemma = joined members text' against current, --samples 3, rotating order. Metrics per case: FAIL (rejected list), pass and needsReview counts. Accept only if no case gains a FAIL and needsReview is within ±2.

hypotheses.title: Stop turning emoji collisions after NoMatch into InvalidModelOutput click failures
hypotheses.claim: When jev returns NoMatch but Luna, not shown the candidates, produces an emoji equal to a stored candidate, the whole click fails as InvalidModelOutput. The stored candidates were produced by the same Luna prompt from earlier contexts, so a collision most likely means jev gave a false NoMatch, which should have been a Reuse. It can also mean Luna conflated two senses. Either way the user gets a failed click, and there is no retry.
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:164-170. Commit dcf189f1 (2026-09-17, 'Keep reading reuse decisions in TypeSafe') replaced the earlier behaviour: previously `existingEmojiDescriptions` went into generation and collisions were recorded as GeneratedReadingCollision and treated as Reuse. tests/reading.test.ts:174-178 locks in the failure. The rate is unmeasured: no reading-resolution/de run is stored in .runs/dumgen, and local tf-demo never reached the compare.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Keep Reuse decisions in TypeSafe, per the owner's policy. On collision, retry generation once with an extra input field, e.g. `usedByOtherReadings: candidates`, and one body line: 'If usedByOtherReadings is present, those descriptions belong to other Readings of this lemma; choose a different mnemonic.' This happens only on the collision path, so there is no extra latency otherwise. With the speculative generation from spec-luna-parallel, the field could be sent up front whenever candidates exist. If the experiment shows collisions almost always coincide with the ideal Reuse, propose a policy change instead: collision becomes Reuse of that candidate, with a GeneratedReadingCollision event.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes one class of whole-click failures. Given how the corpus looks, the expected collision rate is a few percent of NoMatch outcomes. Each prevented failure saves a full retry click of about 2-4 s.
hypotheses.risk: The avoid list may lead Luna to invent a contrived near-duplicate emoji for the same sense, producing a silent duplicate Reading instead of a loud failure. Collision-to-Reuse would silently merge senses when Luna conflates them, for example 🪶 for leicht in the 'easy' sense.
hypotheses.experiment: On reading-resolution/de, skip the compare and force generation for the 28 Reuse-ideal and 21 New-with-candidates cases, --samples 3. Measure P(generated == ideal reused emoji | Reuse ideal), i.e. how often collision-to-Reuse would be right, and P(generated ∈ candidates | New ideal), i.e. how often it would be wrong. Also run the normal operation 3× and count 'collides' failures. Then compare the avoid-list retry variant on the colliding cases.

hypotheses.title: Add a per-attempt timeout, one retry and a hedged duplicate request to the emoji Luna call
hypotheses.claim: textModelCaller and executeGeneration pass only the operation signal; there is no timeout and no retry. On 2026-09-21 09:06 a live click hung for 70,141 ms before 'fetch failed' and then failed; the draft calls hung too. Luna latency in tf-demo also has a heavy tail: 5 of 16 successful emoji calls took 2.6-3.5 s, against CLI evaluation p90 of 1,049 ms and max of 1,533 ms. The tail comes from provider processing (2,410 and 2,932 ms for 6 output tokens) and from waiting at the edge (3,164 ms total with 1,067 ms processing).
hypotheses.evidence: universal/model.ts:50-62 (request without timeout) and :92-93 (options.execute(request)). promptsmith/src/openai.ts:75-87 (fetch with signal only). By contrast, judgment.ts:131-137 uses timeout 10,000 ms from trace.ts:24. Local inspection payload for step generateReadingEmojiDescription: failure 'fetch failed', durationMs 70141. Latencies over 16 calls: 848, 932, 1075, 1118, 1146, 1155, 1236, 1318, 1373, 1414, 2210, 2594, 2849, 3114, 3164, 3491. In the tf-demo samples the emoji call shares its start time with 4 concurrent draftKnowledge Luna calls; the CLI runs had no concurrent calls.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In textModelCaller (or promptsmith openai.ts): per-attempt AbortSignal.any([signal, AbortSignal.timeout(6000)]) with one retry on ProviderFailure or timeout. For the emoji route only, a hedge: if there is no response after about 1,500 ms, fire an identical second request, take whichever finishes first and abort the other. The second request hits the same cached prefix, so it costs about $0.00011.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Reliability: turns 70 s hangs into a recovery after about 6-7 s. Speed: at a 1.5 s hedge, emoji tail cases of 2.6-3.5 s drop toward about 2.4-2.6 s. That is about 150-250 ms off the mean and about 0.5-1 s off p90 in the tf-demo distribution. Extra cost is at most about 35% more emoji calls, around $0.00004 per click.
hypotheses.risk: Duplicate requests use rate-limit headroom. A timeout that is too short would turn slow successes into retries: pick 6 s, well above the observed max of 3.5 s. Traces need to record hedged or aborted attempts.
hypotheses.experiment: (1) Offline: simulate hedge thresholds of 1.2, 1.5 and 1.8 s on the recorded latency sets, using the 16 tf-demo calls plus the 52 + 54 calls in .runs/dumgen e697bfd8 and 9dd85954, to pick a threshold. (2) Live contention test with a sample-reading-style script, 50 held-out generation cases × 3 repeats: emoji alone versus emoji fired together with 4 draftKnowledge-shaped Luna calls. Compare p50/p90 of providerProcessingMs and of total time. (3) Live hedge variant against baseline, interleaved, 50 × 3: p50, p90, max and duplicate-call rate.

hypotheses.title: Answer the authored multi-reading choice (AUX sein/haben/werden, PRON es) inside the grammar jev call
hypotheses.claim: For AUX, resolveGrammar already runs a jev batch with an `identity` choice over sein, haben and werden. resolveReading then makes a second jev call to choose among that lemma's reviewed Readings (perfect, Zustandspassiv, modal passive, progressive, future, Vorgangspassiv, Konjunktiv, obligation). All options are known before grammar runs, so the second round trip is unnecessary: a speculative question in the same batch can answer it, and code keeps the answer that matches the chosen identity. PRON es works the same way through its authored identity path.
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:42-81 (separate judgment when reviewed.length > 1). grammatical-resolution/judgments.ts:183-191 and :264-278 (the AUX identity choice is already in the features batch; the comment at L302-303 says 'Speculative questions whose candidates come from raw source text ride in the same round trip'). The authored inventory has 4 multi-reading lemmas: sein ×4, haben ×2, werden ×3, es ×2. Memory: batching extra questions into one jev call 'does not contaminate them - it helps'.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In judgments.ts, when target kind is AUX, add `authoredReading`: a choice over all 9 AUX Readings with their definitions as criteria, plus Unresolved. Return it with the attestation, for example as a readingHint on the ResolvedGrammar DTO. resolveReading uses the hint when the lemma matches and skips its own jev call. Do the same for PRON when the clicked surface is 'es'. Also make the fallback question lemma-specific: drop 'referential it vs nonreferential es' for AUX.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 300-350 ms off every click on an auxiliary or on 'es'. These are among the most frequent German tokens (ist, hat, wird, war, wurde, es), though how often users click them is unknown. There is no cost change.
hypotheses.risk: Adding questions to the AUX features batch could shift the other AUX feature answers. Only 13 AUX grammar evaluation cases and 1 AUX reading case exist, so the reading corpus needs about 20 new AUX and es reading cases before anything is decided.
hypotheses.experiment: Author about 20 AUX and 'es' reading cases (perfect vs Zustandspassiv with sein, future vs passive vs würde with werden, expletive vs referential es). Run grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/auxiliary (13 evaluation cases) and the new reading cases, baseline versus the batched variant, 3 repeats each. Require no loss in grammar exact-match or reading-choice accuracy, checked case by case, and measure the second round trip removed (wall time).

hypotheses.title: Show each stored candidate's definition, not just its emoji, in the compare criteria
hypotheses.claim: jev picks Reuse or NoMatch by looking only at emoji strings, many of which are ambiguous (➡️, 🔗, 💬, ✅, 🔄, 🔮). Stored readings already carry knowledge.definition, and the authored path in the same file uses definitions as criteria. Pairing each emoji with its definition should cut both false NoMatch results (duplicate Readings) and false Reuse results (merged senses).
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:114-119 (criteria = emoji string) versus :57-61 (authored criteria = definition). dumdict domain-types.ts:38-44 (ReadingEntry.knowledge?.definition). linguisticOrchestration.ts:754-756 keeps only reading.emojiDescription. Corpus examples: reading-de-zug-chess-move has candidates [🚆, 💨, 🧲, ➡️] and ideal Reuse ➡️; reading-de-adp-um-topic has [🔄, 🔗] and ideal New.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Widen ComparisonInput.candidates to accept {emojiDescription, definition?} while keeping string[] for compatibility. Criteria text becomes `${emoji} — ${definition}` when a definition exists, and the emoji alone otherwise. Answer mapping stays keyed by index.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Fewer wrong decisions on emoji-ambiguous candidate sets. Plausibly a few cases out of the 49 compare cases; the size is unknown until measured. There is no latency change, since jev is flat in size, and the cost is negligible at $0.042/M input tokens.
hypotheses.risk: A stored definition comes from the first attestation and may be narrower than the broad emoji concept, which could push jev toward NoMatch and split senses. Readings whose drafts failed have no definition, so behaviour differs between readings.
hypotheses.experiment: Add short German definitions for every candidate emoji in the 49 reading-resolution/de cases that have candidates. Write them from each case's 'explanation', which names the intended sense, then review. Run baseline versus variant 3× each, scoring decision-only accuracy (decision, plus the emoji on Reuse) case by case, with flips tabulated separately from noise.

hypotheses.title: Measure, and probably remove, the Unresolved option in the stored-candidate compare
hypotheses.claim: In the compare, an Unresolved answer fails the whole click (resolve.ts:132-138), and the wording pushes borderline cases there ('NoMatch means a defensible new concept, not uncertainty'). A wrong Reuse or New can be repaired later in the dictionary; a failed click cannot. The rate is unknown.
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:113 and :123-124. tf-demo turns the failure into GenerationFailed (resolutionSessionExecution.ts:235-243). No stored reading-resolution/de run exists to count Unresolved answers.
hypotheses.proposedChange: First measure. If Unresolved appears on more than about 2% of cases, either drop the Unresolved option from the stored-candidate compare (keeping it for authored and grammar judgments), or on Unresolved use the probability mass: Reuse the top candidate if it outweighs NoMatch, else generate.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes a whole-click failure mode at a rate still to be measured. There is no latency change.
hypotheses.risk: Without Unresolved, genuinely ambiguous occurrences such as underspecified contexts get a forced decision and could create duplicate Readings. This goes against the codebase principle that uncertainty is an explicit answer (judgment.ts:65).
hypotheses.experiment: Run reading-resolution/de 3× at the current revision and count answers of choice == Unresolved by case. Then run a variant without Unresolved 3× and compare decision-only accuracy case by case. Do this after bun run build:js, as memory notes.

hypotheses.title: Warm or multiplex the OpenAI connection so the emoji call doesn't open a new TLS connection
hypotheses.claim: Almost every emoji call opens a new TLS connection. The emoji and the 4 draft calls start at the same moment over HTTP/1.1, so they cannot share one socket, and idle sockets are dropped between clicks. Measured connectionMs is 65-240 ms, median about 85 ms. The same effect appears to hit TypeSafe even harder: the first jev call of a click after more than about 4 s idle takes about 730-1150 ms, versus about 280-360 ms when warm. That matches undici's 4 s keepAlive default and matters for the classification and grammar owners.
hypotheses.evidence: generateReadingEmojiDescription payload metadata.timing.detailed.connection: reused=false with opened=true on 14 of 16 calls. The only reused one was 848 ms total against about 1.1-1.4 s. CLI run e697bfd8: 52 of 52 fresh connections, total minus processing p50 246 ms. TypeSafe first-call durations after idle: 857, 870, 871, 782, 825, 729, 730, 721, 800, 1151, 817, 1127 ms; within 4 s of the previous call: 348, 356, 315, 283, 277 ms. modelExecution.ts:36-39 builds a new TypeSafe client per judge call.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In tf-demo server/modelExecution.ts (host transport, not dumgen): install an undici Agent with allowH2: true and keepAliveTimeout of about 60 s, so all concurrent Luna calls multiplex over one connection. Also send a fire-and-forget warm-up request (a cheap HEAD request to api.openai.com and to the TypeSafe endpoint) at the start of runResolutionSession, which comes about 1 s before the emoji call. Reuse one TypeSafe client per action instead of one per call.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 80 ms (up to 240 ms) off each Luna call on the emoji path, and the same off drafts. If the TypeSafe observation is the same effect, about 450-800 ms off the first jev call of most clicks, which is outside this stage but very large.
hypotheses.risk: Low. HTTP/2 to OpenAI through undici needs checking in the Convex Node runtime. Warm-up requests add trivial traffic.
hypotheses.experiment: In tf-demo with inspection on, run 20 clicks spaced more than 5 s apart, before and after the change. Compare connection.reused and connectionMs on the Luna calls, and the duration of the first TypeSafe call per click (read from the local Convex sqlite inspectionSteps and inspectionPayloads). No evaluation-corpus cost.

hypotheses.title: Score reading-resolution/de by decision correctness, separately from exact emoji equality
hypotheses.claim: The resolve experiment marks a case as passing only if stableJson(output) equals stableJson(idealOutput). Of the 67 evaluation cases, 39 are New, and for those a correct NoMatch decision still fails whenever Luna's fresh emoji differs from the stored ideal. The metric mixes compare accuracy with generation randomness, so it cannot evaluate any of the compare hypotheses above.
hypotheses.evidence: experiment.ts:130-134 (exact equality). Corpus mix: 28 Reuse, 39 New, 18 with no candidates. 5 cases use the neighbour-isolation evaluator instead.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Add a decision-level evaluation: decision equality, plus emoji equality on Reuse. For New cases, reuse the accepted and rejected lists from generate/cases.ts where they exist. Also put the 5 unused demonstrationIds back into the evaluation set, from 67 to 72 cases.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Makes compare changes measurable (H1, H3, H6, H7). There is no runtime impact.
hypotheses.risk: None at runtime. Changing the evaluator makes new scores incomparable with any earlier stored reading-resolution scores, and none exist locally.
hypotheses.experiment: Re-score one baseline reading-resolution/de run under both evaluators and report how many cases change verdict purely because of emoji mismatch on New cases.

hypotheses.title: Rebalance the generation demonstrations toward single emojis and add production-shaped markup
hypotheses.claim: The demonstrations say the opposite of the instruction: 14 of 25 demos are two-emoji, and the second emoji is where the incidental participant or the complement leaks in. The demos also never show the markup production sends for article-plus-noun targets or split separable verbs.
hypotheses.evidence: prompts.ts:3 (25 examples; two-emoji ones include verwirrt, reparieren, Regenmantel, mühelos, zurücklegen, geduldig, teuer, teilen, billig, den Faden verlieren, neidisch, zurückgeben, scheinen, finden). Run e697bfd8: 1 FAIL (make-clean 🧹✨) and 14 needsReview of 52, mostly two-emoji outputs (👐🪟, 👀😋, 👀🫥, ⚠️👐, 🔎🧠, 🛟🤲, ⚖️↔️). Baseline run 9dd85954: 41 pass, 2 fail, 11 review of 54. Add one demo with an article-marked noun target and one with a split separable verb (<TARGET>macht</TARGET> … <TARGET>auf</TARGET>). hypotheses.title: Ideas that are NOT worth doing now: intake emoji precompute, shorter prompt for speed, dropping the grammarAvailable wait, the 253 cap
hypotheses.claim: (1) Generating emojis at intake (analyzeSentence) for every unit: the lemma, dictionary candidates and the compare are only known at click time. It also does not shorten commit for New readings, which waits on drafts. Draft calls: input 133-291, cached 0, processing 639-2194 ms. convex/dumdictStorage/storage.ts:29 MAX_READING_CANDIDATES = 40. Commit waited on drafts after the emoji in 12 of 16 New clicks.

audits.stage: Knowledge drafting and production (draftKnowledge on the click path, produceKnowledge after commit, Definition Text materialization)
audits.howItWorks: CLICK PATH (app/tf-demo/server/linguisticOrchestration.ts). After resolveGrammar returns a Resolved attestation, resolveSegment forks options.draftKnowledge with Effect.forkScoped (l.475-488). In production that is convex/orchestration.ts:422-455: two Convex queries (knowledgeSettings.get and relationPublication.getAuthorization, about 10 ms), then generationRequestFor, then createProductionKnowledgeDraft (server/modelExecution.ts:24-29), which calls dumgen draftKnowledge (knowledge-production/draft.ts:57-277). draftKnowledge returns early with no model calls for authored or closed routes (l.88-93). Otherwise it fires one Luna call (gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning none, service_tier fast; universal/model.ts:12-15) per text leaf, all at once: transcription (input {lemma, aspect}), definition, and one call per enabled translation language (en, ru). Those three get {lemma, markedContext, aspect, language}. A relation-candidates call is added only if semanticRelations was requested (l.195-265). Per-call failures are swallowed as KnowledgeDraftFailed and return []. The request comes from dumrel DE_REL_MAP (battery/dumrel/src/selection-policy-de.ts): every open route asks for transcription, definition and translations{en,ru}. ADJ, NOUN, VERB, Collocation and Idiom also ask for governedPrepositions. semanticRelations is filtered by qualifiedKinds, which is always [] today because COMPILED_RELATION_VERDICT.verdict is null (convex/model/compiledRelationVerdict.ts). So in production the draft is exactly 4 parallel Luna calls and never includes relations. Meanwhile grammarAvailable ‖ findStoredReadings run, then resolveReading (jev compare, then Luna emoji). For a New Reading, resolveSegment does Fiber.join(knowledgeDraft) before committing (l.550-566). A reused Reading gets Fiber.poll, and an unfinished draft is interrupted. The draft is JSON-stringified into persistResolvedClick (l.576-580). That mutation settles the session (UI shows Complete) and calls scheduleKnowledgeGeneration with knowledgeDraftJson (convex/persistence.ts:672). AFTER COMMIT (convex/knowledgeGenerationActions.ts): begin mutation, then produceKnowledge with options.knowledgeDraft (l.81-111, 182-205). produce.ts runs authoredKnowledge, then draftedTexts (a local fingerprint check on markedContext+lemma, draft.ts:280-332). One job per missing aspect/leaf runs concurrently (produce.ts:170-314). A drafted text is only validated locally through projectKnowledge; with no draft, a fallback Luna call uses a different prompt (produce.ts:262). governedPrepositions is always a fresh Luna call (produce.ts:137-158, prompt in governed-prepositions/prompt.ts:15). Each text contribution publishes incrementally through onKnowledgeContribution; governedPrepositions only goes out in the final publish. After `await Promise.all(textJobs)` (produce.ts:315) come relation candidates (the draft, else a Luna call, l.334-387) and then one jev labeling call with 2 choice questions per candidate (l.406-446). Both are dead in production. Knowledge publish calls syncDefinitionText, which schedules definitionTextActions.materialize. That step is deterministic segmentSentence only, with no model call and no analyzeSentence (definitionTextActions.ts:58-76; model/definitionTexts.ts:115-162 writes texts/sentences/segments but no sentenceAnalyses row). LIVE EVIDENCE comes from a read-only query of the tf-demo inspection tables (11 New-Reading clicks, 44 draft calls). Draft inputs were 133-291 tokens per call (962 per click), outputs 15-33 tokens, about $0.00057 per click. Per-aspect wall p50: transcription 1506 ms (max 3469), definition 1198, en 1689, ru 1297; emoji p50 2210. The commit waited on the join in 7/11 clicks: mean 457 ms, median 101, max 1966 (Commit start minus Save ReadingAvailable end). 39/44 draft calls and 10/11 emoji calls opened a new TLS connection (median connect 104 ms). produceKnowledge ran in 2-5 ms with 0 Luna calls in every committed click (drafts reused; these traces predate governedPrepositions). The evaluation harness (src/evaluation/knowledge-operation.ts:163-179) calls produceKnowledge with no knowledgeDraft. It also runs only corpora whose requests are semanticRelations (62 lexeme + 6 phraseme) or governedPrepositions (19). So the production draft prompts for definition, transcription and translations have zero golden coverage.

promptProblems: draft.ts:32 (translations): "Translate only the marked target into ${language}; return one concise word or phrase, never the whole sentence." There is no citation-form instruction, so the model translates the INFLECTED surface. 10 of 22 live outputs were inflected: sein→"were"/"были", überleben→"survives"/"выживает", sind→"are"/"являются", geöffnet→ru "открыты", geschlossen→ru "закрыты", Banken→"banks"/"банки". These are stored as Reading Knowledge, which dumrel/CONTEXT.md defines as 'owned by one exact Reading' and shows for every later attestation.

draft.ts:32 vs produce.ts:262 contradict each other on the sense anchor. The draft says "The sentence is the sense anchor"; the fallback says "The Reading's emojiDescription is the sense anchor: describe the meaning it names". Only the fallback has the worked translation example ("gestern <TARGET>anstrengend</TARGET> gives strenuous in English, not yesterday was strenuous"). Which prompt writes a Reading's stored text depends on timing (draft finished or interrupted).

draft.ts:32: "Never change the Lemma, Kind or Core Features" and "The caller attaches this text to the Reading after local validation." The output is only {text}, so the model cannot change these. Noise instructions. produce.ts:262 has the same issue: "Do not return judgments or domain objects".

draft.ts:25 (transcription): "Preserve the Lemma exactly" means nothing for an IPA output, and there are no conventions for primary stress, syllabic consonants, glottal stop or multiword units. Live outputs are inconsistent: "ˈbaŋkən" vs "ˈblaɪ̯bn̩" (syllabic n), "ɡəˈʃlɔsən" vs "ɡəˈʔœfn̩t" (glottal stop, syllabic n), "ɡants ʊnt ɡaːr" (no stress at all).

The draft/produce prompts say "Return {text:string}", but promptsmith/src/openai.ts:56-69 wraps every schema as {value:{...}} with `strict: false`. The described shape differs from the enforced one, and schemas (including enums) are NOT provider-enforced.

governed-prepositions/prompt.ts:15: "Choose prepositions only from the offered list". The list exists only in the JSON-schema enum, and strict:false means it is not enforced. An off-list answer (e.g. gegenüber for 'skeptisch gegenüber', durch, hinter) makes parseGovernedPrepositionsOutput (l.64-76) throw, and the whole aspect fails as InvalidModelOutput instead of dropping one item.

draft.ts:32 (definition): "Write a concise German definition." gives no guard against circular or antonym-only definitions. Live pair: geschlossen→"nicht geöffnet", geöffnet→"nicht geschlossen und für den Zutritt oder die Nutzung verfügbar". Definitions become clickable Definition Texts, so circular ones teach little.

The drafts trust the grammar Lemma, so grammar lemma errors turn directly into wrong Knowledge. In 3 of 11 live New Readings the lemma form was wrong: 'sind' as lemma (IPA "zɪnt"), 'Banken' as lemma (definition "Finanzinstitute…" in plural), and 'Morgen' capitalized as an ADV. This is outside this stage, but it caps Knowledge quality.

hypotheses.title: Commit New Readings without waiting for the text drafts; hand drafts to Knowledge generation after commit
hypotheses.claim: For a New Reading the click commit (session Complete, canonical cards, word colour) waits on Fiber.join of the 4 parallel Luna drafts. Nothing in the commit needs the drafts; they are only stashed as knowledgeDraftJson for runKnowledgeGeneration. The join added a mean 457 ms to Complete in live traces. It also exposes the click to a hung provider call: no client timeout exists, and undici's default headersTimeout is 300 s.
hypotheses.evidence: linguisticOrchestration.ts:550-566 ("A new Reading waits for its drafts… Fiber.join(knowledgeDraft)") and :576-580 (knowledgeDraftJson into persistResolvedClick). persistence.ts:672 (scheduleKnowledgeGeneration with the draft). Live inspection, 11 New-Reading clicks: commit start minus Save ReadingAvailable end = [1,1,1,1012,101,1434,1966,67,1,316,147] ms; mean 457, median 101, max 1966; 7/11 >0. produceKnowledge afterwards took 2-5 ms with 0 Luna calls, so drafts matter only after commit. promptsmith/src/openai.ts:75-87: fetch with only the operation signal, no timeout.
hypotheses.proposedChange: When a draft fiber is pending, call persistResolvedClick with a `knowledgeDraftPending` flag. scheduleKnowledgeGeneration then inserts the attempt as AwaitingDraft and schedules a safety run with runAfter(~20 s) (fallback prompts if the action dies). After commit, the same action joins the fiber and calls a new internal mutation attachKnowledgeDraft({attemptKey, knowledgeDraftJson}). That mutation patches the attempt and schedules runKnowledgeGeneration now if it is still AwaitingDraft. The poll/interrupt behaviour for Matched Readings stays unchanged.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Complete for New Readings: -457 ms mean, -101 ms p50, up to -1966 ms (n=11 live). Time to definition is essentially unchanged: it is already max(draft end, commit)+~80 ms, and an extra ~30 ms mutation is added. Removes the unbounded-hang failure mode from the click.
hypotheses.risk: Adds an attempt state and ordering (attach vs safety run vs Waiting attempts for the same Reading). The action keeps running after the session settles, and inspection/Record Succeeded ordering changes. Needs an idempotent attach.
hypotheses.experiment: Offline first: add a case to app/tf-demo/tests/linguistic-orchestration.test.ts with a draft that never resolves and assert persistResolvedClick is called. Live: submit a fresh ~30-new-word text in tf-demo and click each word, 30 clicks on baseline vs variant. From `bun run resolution_inspector request <id>` read (a) Commit end minus click start, (b) Commit start minus Save ReadingAvailable end, (c) that produceKnowledge still makes 0 Luna text calls, (d) time to the first 'Publish Knowledge contribution'. Compare case by case; Luna latency noise is large (emoji p50 2.2 s, max 3.5 s).

hypotheses.title: Take transcription out of the joined draft set (lemma-level: reuse from sibling Readings, else generate post-commit)
hypotheses.claim: Transcription depends only on the Lemma, yet it is one of the 4 joined drafts. It was the slowest draft call in 4/11 live clicks and has the highest provider-processing p50 (1131 ms), despite the smallest prompt. Removing it from the join alone cuts the measured join wait from 457 to 171 ms mean. A second Reading of the same Lemma regenerates the same IPA.
hypotheses.evidence: draft.ts:23-25 ('Transcription belongs to the Lemma headword; no sentence or Reading is needed'). Live per-aspect wall p50/max: transcription 1506/3469, definition 1198/2581, en 1689/2554, ru 1297/2898. Replaying the 11 traces without transcription gives join waits [0,0,0,1009,78,0,271,66,0,314,145] ms, mean 171.

Otherwise let produceKnowledge generate it post-commit through the existing fallback path (produce.ts:241-245). Tighten the IPA conventions in the prompt at the same time (see transcription prompt problem).
