hypotheses.experiment: (1) Offline replay of the inspection traces, done above: 457→171 ms. (2) Live: 30 new-word clicks as in detach-draft-join, same metric. (3) Convention variant: a prototype script (e.g. battery/dumgen/prototypes/p5-knowledge-drafts.ts) running the transcription prompt baseline vs variant over the 75 encounter+lemma cases in src/concrete-lang/de/reading-emoji-description/operation-cases.json (the reading-generation/de and reading-resolution/de sources), 3 repeats. Metrics: identical output across repeats, regex adherence (primary stress on polysyllables, syllabic n̩ in -en), wall p50/p90.

hypotheses.title: Make drafted translations lemma-level citation forms, not inflected sentence translations
hypotheses.claim: The draft translation prompt makes the model translate the inflected surface. 10 of 22 live translations were inflected, yet they are stored as Reading-level Knowledge and shown for every later occurrence. Wrong answers are being persisted silently.
hypotheses.evidence: draft.ts:32: "Translate only the marked target into ${language}; return one concise word or phrase, never the whole sentence." Live outputs: sein→were/были, überleben→survives/выживает, sind→are/являются, geöffnet→открыты, geschlossen→закрыты, Banken→banks/банки. Citation-form outputs were only ganz und gar, Ligusterweg, Junge, Morgen and bleiben. battery/dumrel/CONTEXT.md: 'Reading Knowledge: optional linguistic content owned by one exact Reading'.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Replace the translation clause with, roughly: 'Give the ${language} citation form that translates this Lemma in the sense the marked target carries here: an English base form (verbs without to), a Russian infinitive for verbs, and nominative singular (masculine for adjectives) otherwise. Keep multiword units as a phrase. Never mirror the sentence's tense, person or number.' Apply the same change to the produce.ts:262 fallback, or better unify both (see unify-text-prompts-and-evaluate).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 40-45% of new-Reading translations become citation forms. No latency change; output length is unchanged.
hypotheses.risk: Over-normalisation where the sense is inherently plural (pluralia tantum), or phrasemes where a contextual rendering is better. Needs manual review of the polysemy cases.
hypotheses.experiment: Prototype script over the 75 operation-cases.json encounters (en+ru), baseline vs variant, 2 repeats, about 600 Luna calls. Metrics: citation-form rate (rule check on POS plus manual review), sense correctness on polysemy cases (bank-seat, maus-computer, sauer-acidic), and flips case by case.

hypotheses.title: One sense-anchored call for definition + all translations instead of one call per leaf
hypotheses.claim: Definition, en and ru each re-derive the sense from the same marked sentence in independent calls. The slowest-of-N amplifies provider tail latency (per-click slowest draft median 1941 ms vs single-call medians of 1198-1689 ms). Independent calls can also pick different senses for the definition and the translations.
hypotheses.evidence: draft.ts:95-191 builds one executeGeneration per leaf. Live: per-click max-of-4 draft wall median 1941 ms, individual calls p50 1198-1689 ms. Examples of the tail: 'waren' en 1881 ms vs the other three ~1000; 'überlebt' definition 1936 vs ru 1297. The memory rule only forbids bundling text into the EMOJI call; bundling text drafts together is allowed.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Replace the definition/translation leaf calls with a single call returning {definition: string|null, translations: {en?: string|null, ru?: string|null}}, keeping the sentence-anchored instructions. Keep per-leaf validation so one bad leaf does not drop the others. Keep transcription separate (or remove it, see transcription-off-click-path).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Speed: removes 2 of the 3 sense round trips. Expected draft p90 gain ~0.3-0.8 s, partly offset by ~40-60 more output tokens (+0.1-0.3 s). This only matters for click latency if detach-draft-join is NOT adopted, otherwise it affects time to definition. Reliability: definition and translations share one sense decision.
hypotheses.risk: One failure or garbled output loses all three texts, where today they fail independently. A longer output means a higher mean latency per call. Quality could shift, so it needs a comparison.
hypotheses.experiment: Prototype over the 75 operation-cases.json encounters, 3 repeats: baseline (3 parallel calls, record max) vs merged (1 call). Metrics: wall p50/p90 of the sense texts, invalid-output rate, and manual agreement of definition/translation senses on the polysemy subset.

hypotheses.title: Reuse warm HTTP/2 connections for Luna calls (and pre-warm at click start)
hypotheses.claim: Almost every Luna call on the click opens a fresh TLS connection. The click fans out 4 drafts + 1 emoji concurrently over HTTP/1.1, and sockets go cold between clicks (undici keepAliveTimeout default 4 s). Each call pays ~100 ms connect.
hypotheses.evidence: Live http traces (metadata.timing.detailed.connection): 39/44 draft calls and 10/11 generateReadingEmojiDescription calls had reused=false, median connectionMs 104 (65-146). server/modelExecution.ts:36 builds a new executor per options, and promptsmith/src/openai.ts:75 uses globalThis.fetch with the default dispatcher. Only the 'überlebt' click (executorRequestOrdinal 6-11 on a warm instance) reused connections.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In the Convex 'use node' action modules, set once: setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({ allowH2: true, keepAliveTimeout: 60_000, keepAliveMaxTimeout: 120_000 })) (undici). At click start, fire one zero-token warm-up request (HEAD/GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models) in parallel with classify/grammar (≥600 ms of jev time). HTTP/2 then multiplexes the 5 concurrent Luna calls over the warmed socket.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About -100 ms on every critical-path Luna hop: emoji generation (all New Readings), canonical-form generation (verbs), and drafts when they bound the join. Roughly -100 ms p50 per new-word click, and -100 to -200 ms on verb routes.
hypotheses.risk: undici HTTP/2 maturity in the Convex node runtime. The server may refuse h2 or reset idle streams. Adds one warm-up request per click (no tokens, no cost).
hypotheses.experiment: Local script: 20 rounds spaced 6 s apart (beyond the default keep-alive), each firing 5 concurrent Luna draft calls on operation-cases.json encounters. Compare the default dispatcher vs Agent({allowH2, keepAlive}) with warm-up. Metrics: connection.reused ratio, connectionMs, wall p50/p90 from the promptsmith http trace. Then verify on 20 tf-demo new-word clicks by reading `connection.reused` in inspection payloads.

hypotheses.title: Put the governable-preposition list in the prompt text and drop off-list items instead of failing the aspect

hypotheses.title: Bound each draft Luna call with a timeout (and optionally one hedged retry)
hypotheses.claim: Draft calls have no client-side deadline. While the commit joins drafts, one stalled provider response holds the whole click until undici's 300 s header timeout. This is rare, but it is a whole-click stall with no failure recorded.

hypotheses.expectedImpact: Caps the worst-case click stall from draft calls at ~6 s instead of up to 300 s. Hedging would also trim the p90 of time to definition.
hypotheses.risk: A too-tight timeout drops texts that the fallback then regenerates post-commit (the slower path).
hypotheses.experiment: Fault-injection unit test with an execute that never resolves, asserting the draft settles in ≤6 s. Live: count draft calls above the threshold in inspection over the next 100 new-word clicks.

hypotheses.proposedChange: Nothing now. When relations return, generate candidates post-commit only (not in draftKnowledge) and start them concurrently with textJobs, labeling as soon as candidates arrive.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: 0 ms today. After re-enablement it avoids adding a likely ~1-2 s call to the click join, and saves one Luna round trip (~1-2 s) on relation completion.
hypotheses.risk: None today. Mention it only so the relation re-enablement work does not reintroduce latency.
hypotheses.experiment: None until re-enabled. Then run knowledge-analysis/de/lexeme (62 cases) with the candidates call started concurrently vs sequentially and compare end-to-end produce wall time.

hypotheses.title: Ideas checked and rejected (or low value)
hypotheses.claim: Several plausible changes do not pay off. (a) Skipping speculative drafts for clicks that match a stored Reading saves only ~$0.0006 per click and no latency. (b) Offloading Knowledge drafts to intake needs the Lemma, which intake does not produce, and would cost N words × 4 Luna calls per sentence for words mostly never clicked. (c) Moving governedPrepositions into the draft is not worth it: it is not rendered in tf-demo yet, runs post-commit, and would widen the joined fan-out. audits.stage: tf-demo end-to-end click orchestration (Convex Resolution Session: selectSegment → runResolutionSession → resolveSegment → persistResolvedClick) plus the intake path (submitText)
audits.howItWorks:
PRODUCTION CLICK PATH. The client calls the mutation api.resolutionSessions.selectSegment (src/hooks/use-segment-selection.ts:29-30), not the legacy orchestration.resolveSegment action. Timings below are medians from the local Convex DB. I copied app/tf-demo/.convex/local/default/convex_local_backend.sqlite3 to /tmp and read it read-only. It holds inspection steps for 19 clicks and 3 text submissions (2026-09-21/22) and resolutionRuns traces for about 35 runs.

1. selectSegment (mutation, resolutionSessions.ts:53-321). If the segment already has an attestationMembership it returns Available (43-80 ms round trip, no model call). Otherwise it inserts the session and calls scheduler.runAfter(0, runResolutionSession) (lines 249-258). Browser round trip: median 91 ms.
2. Scheduler plus node action start (orchestration.ts:315-369): about 53 ms, with outliers of 207, 260 and 401 ms.
3. beginRun (mutation, resolutionSessions.ts:395-507, 39 ms). It claims the run, and loadResolutionContext runs inline in the same hop (line 468). That call loads the sentence, the stored Sentence Analysis and lemmaCandidates (up to 64 spellings × 2 index queries, resolutionContext.ts:98-169). The Convex adapter (resolutionSessionLifecycle.ts:58-64) passes context.analysis on in its STORED form: masses are arrays of {key, share} pairs. fromStoredSentenceAnalysis is never called on this path. That conversion exists only in the unused action adapter (orchestration.ts:509-512).
4. selectTarget (linguisticOrchestration.ts:668-737) calls selectAnalysisTarget → resolvedUnitAt → argmax (analysis.ts:145-165). On the stored array form, argmax returns 'Unresolved', so the function returns null EVERY time and dumgen.classifyTarget runs one jev call. Evidence: 19 of 19 logged clicks were 'Select target · classified', median 758 ms (296-1782). Replaying selectAnalysisTarget over all 18 stored analyses and 138 clickable segments: 0 of 138 hits in stored form, 137 of 138 after conversion, and all 137 pass validateEncounter. The only miss is the fused 'im'.
5. resolveGrammar (production.ts:115-226, judgments.ts). One jev call for the features (median 330 ms, 284-604). Then, only when needed:
   - DET/PRON authored-identity jev call
   - Luna generateCanonicalForm (1222 and 1248 ms; happened on 2 of 11 resolved clicks: überlebt, waren)
   - jev follow-up for lexical strings
   - jev follow-up for noun Case
6. draftKnowledge is forked (lines 478-488). Inside it: 2 Convex queries and a dynamic import, then 4 parallel Luna calls (definition, transcription, translations en and ru). Relation candidates are added when qualified kinds exist. Per-aspect medians: 1198, 1506, 1689 and 1297 ms. The whole operation has a median of about 2.1 s and a maximum of 3.5 s. It is off the critical path until the join.
7. In parallel: advance(GrammarAvailable) (43 ms) and findStoredReadings (a query, 32 ms). Both must settle before the next step (lines 489-516). GrammarAvailable is the first thing the user sees: resolving-reading-note.tsx:29-45 renders the lemma from note.grammar.
8. resolveReading (resolve.ts). An authored closed-class lemma needs no call. Stored candidates mean a jev compare (about 310 ms). Empty candidates or NoMatch mean Luna generateReadingEmojiDescription: median 2210 ms (848-3491) over 11 calls, input 1.6-2.0k tokens mostly cached, output 6-10 tokens. Every emoji call opened a new TLS connection (connection.reused=false, 76-240 ms). On all 11 resolved clicks the candidates were empty.
9. advance(ReadingAvailable) (39 ms, sequential). The UI shows the emoji at this point (resolving-reading-note.tsx:53-76).
10. Draft handling (lines 553-566). A New reading joins the draft: measured wait after ReadingAvailable was median 101 ms, mean 459, maximum 1966. A reused reading polls the draft and interrupts it if unfinished, which is effectively always, so those Luna calls are wasted.
11. persistResolvedClick (mutation, 67 ms). It plans the dictionary change in the transaction, settles the session to Complete and schedules knowledge generation. That action starts about 3 ms later; produceKnowledge takes 4 ms because it reuses the drafts; publishing takes about 200 ms more.
12. recordRunSuccess (28 ms) runs after completion and is not user-visible.

End-to-end, 11 resolved clicks from click to commit: median 4281 ms (2217-5407).
- Grammar visible: about 1.3 s.
- Emoji visible: about 3.5 s.
- Complete: about 4.3 s.

Convex hops cost 28-86 ms each locally. Module weights: resolutionSessions.ts 1.3 MB, persistence.ts 1.2 MB, dumdictStorage 1.0 MB. So hops are no longer the bottleneck; model calls are.

Known Lemma with stored Readings (Reuse; from code, no logged case): 91 + 53 + 39 + classify 758 (the bug) + features 330 (canonical comes from storedLemmas, so usually no Luna) + 43 + jev compare ~310 + 39 + commit 67 ≈ 1.7 s. After the H1 fix, about 0.95 s. A NoMatch adds the Luna emoji (~2.2 s) and the draft join.

Failure handling. Unresolved from any stage ends as Terminal Unresolved. classifyResolutionFailure marks every ProviderFailure and InvalidModelOutput as retryable:false (resolutionFailure.ts:38-53). recordRunFailure therefore never schedules the durable retry, and the click becomes a PermanentFailure. Neither jev nor Luna retries (maxRetries 0), and the Luna fetch has no timeout: one logged emoji call failed with 'fetch failed' after 70,141 ms. Observed outcomes: 8 of 19 clicks were Unresolved. 7 of them followed a wrong classifier membership (Mr → PROPN[Mr, Mrs, Dursley], stolz → ADJ[stolz, darauf], darauf → Idiom[stolz, darauf, gar]) and ended with grammar 'Unresolved applicable question support'. The 8th was namens, where classifyTarget itself failed ('Assembled target is not defensible').

INTAKE. submitText:
1. splitInSentences uses Intl.Segmenter, which breaks at every single line break.
2. dumgen.segment is NOT deterministic. It makes one jev call per sentence (language / validity / stitching), plus a Luna whitespace-repair call when stitching=Needed (segment.ts:42-160). It runs all sentences in parallel since commit a6b665cf (2026-09-22); before that it was sequential, 6.2 s for 18 sentences.
3. analyzeSentence runs per German sentence with concurrency 4. Each sentence is one jev call, split into 220-question chunks (O(n²) membership).
4. persistSubmittedText runs only after ALL analyses finish.

Measured 18-sentence submission: 10.3 s total, of which analysis took 4.0 s.

unusedOrRedundantInputs: ResolutionContext.analysis on the production session path: beginRun loads it on every click (resolutionContext.ts:91). resolutionSessionLifecycle.ts:58-64 hands it on in stored form, so selectAnalysisTarget returns null 138 of 138 times, and a paid classifyTarget call replaces it (median 758 ms).

The intake Identity Mass is thrown away at click time. analyzeSentence already judges per-cell rubric options for DET/PRON (identity.ts, questions.ts:63-80), but resolveGrammar redoes identity: locateAuthoredIdentity plus a jev /identity call on a non-Hit (authored-identity.ts:31-63). The intake result is used only to override the route (analysis.ts:214-223).
The grammar features state duplicates stored lemmas. It carries full storedLemmas objects AND their canonical forms as canonicalFormAlternatives (judgments.ts:152-165, 330-336).

canonicalFormAlternatives for NOUN adds the raw source members, including the article and inflected forms (judgments.ts:161). Trace 1e976b81 offered ['Die','Banken'], and the model chose 'Banken' (p=0.84) as the Lemma.

loadResolutionContext looks up every word of the sentence, not just the ±3 phrase window (resolutionContext.ts:115-129). Same-kind lemmas of other words then become canonical-form alternatives for the clicked word. Cheap today (beginRun 39 ms), but it is noise in the prompt.

draftKnowledge on the Reuse path: 4 Luna calls start and are then interrupted, because the poll comes ~350 ms after the fork and drafts take 1.1-3.5 s (linguisticOrchestration.ts:557-565). Transcription is Lemma-level but is drafted again on every click.
draftKnowledge for authored or closed-class lemmas: the host runs 2 Convex queries and a dynamic import (orchestration.ts:422-457) before dumgen returns an empty draft (draft.ts:88-93).
advance(ReadingAvailable) on Reuse, or when the draft has already finished: persistResolvedClick settles the same Reading about 67 ms later.

The legacy orchestration.resolveSegment action and createConvexPersistence.loadResolutionContext (orchestration.ts:296-313, 499-514) are not used by the client, yet they hold the only correct stored→dumgen analysis conversion.
promptProblems: The word 'Canonical' is used for two different things in resolveGrammar. sharedPolicy.identity (judgments.ts:108) says 'Spelling Canonical does not mean Grundform: finite and declined forms may be Canonical'. That sentence is about the `spelling` question, but it sits beside the `canonical` question on Canonical Form, and canonicalForm policy (line 110) adds 'Inflection does not prevent identical spelling.' Evidence: 'sind' → CandidateIsCanonical 0.56 vs CandidateIsNotCanonical 0.40, stored Lemma 'sind'. 'überlebt' and 'waren' were only rescued by the Luna call (1.2 s each).

The canonicalForm policy says the alternatives include 'for nouns, individual source members without the article'. The code instead adds every source member, including the article and inflected plurals (judgments.ts:161). Offering an inflected surface as a 'headword' alternative gets it accepted: 'Banken' p=0.84.

The Lexeme and Phraseme criteria contradict each other on valency. targetCriteria (target-classification/judgments.ts:24) says 'an adjective with a governed preposition (stolz auf, zufrieden mit) is a singleton ADJ…' and 'A pronominal adverb (darauf…) is always a singleton ADV'. fixednessCriteria (criteria.ts:37) never mentions valency. The stored analysis therefore made 'stolz darauf' a Collocation (fixedness 1.54, barely above the 1.5 floor). Once H1 is fixed, clicks on stolz or darauf will select that Collocation.

Pipeline misconception in the task framing: dumgen.segment is not 'deterministic code, no model'. It makes one jev judgment per sentence and optionally a Luna stitching call (segment.ts:42-160). Any Unresolved answer on any sentence rejects the whole text.

Stored traces show the emoji borrowing a neighbouring word's meaning: bleiben → '🚪🔒' in 'Morgen bleiben sie geschlossen.'. This happens even though the compare prompt says 'Do not borrow a neighboring word's meaning'. The generation prompt (reading-generation/de, 7.9k chars) should be checked for the same rule. Owned by the emoji auditor.

hypotheses.title: Resolution Sessions pass the stored-form Sentence Analysis, so every click falls back to classifyTarget
hypotheses.claim: On the production path (selectSegment → runResolutionSession), context.analysis is never converted with fromStoredSentenceAnalysis. Its routeMass and identity mass are arrays of {key, share}, so argmax/selectRoute return 'Unresolved' and resolvedUnitAt returns null. selectAnalysisTarget has therefore never succeeded in production. Every click pays a classifyTarget jev call, and the classifier's membership errors cause most observed Unresolved clicks.
hypotheses.evidence:
Where the conversion is missing:
- resolutionSessionLifecycle.ts:58-64 spreads `...input.context` and fixes only lemmaCandidates.
- beginRun returns the stored validator shape (resolutionContext.ts:42, loadSentenceAnalysis in resolutionLookup.ts:118-127).
- The only conversion is orchestration.ts:509-512, on the unused action adapter.
- sentenceAnalysisStorage.ts:16-22 stores masses as [{key, share}], and analysis.ts:145-153 runs argmax with Object.entries over it.
- Tests pass dumgen-form analyses directly (tests/linguistic-orchestration.test.ts:1170-1200), so the adapter is not covered.

Replay (/tmp/select-audit.ts over 18 stored analyses, 138 clickable segments):
- stored form: 0 of 138 hits
- converted: 137 of 138 hits, all passing validateEncounter; the only miss is the fused 'im'.

Inspection log:
- 19 of 19 clicks were 'Select target · classified'. Classify latency (ms): 296, 314, 320, 384, 543, 719, 748, 751, 756, 783, 787, 789, 793, 794, 796, 797, 1126, 1132, 1782; median 783.
- 8 of 19 clicks were Unresolved: 7 after a wrong classifier membership (Mr → PROPN[0,4,6], Mrs → PROPN[0,2,4,6], stolz → ADJ[stolz, darauf], darauf → Idiom[18,20,27]) followed by 'Unresolved applicable question support', and 1 where classifyTarget itself failed (namens: 'Assembled target is not defensible').

Better still, make the lifecycle return type non-castable so the `as ResolutionSessionRunInput["context"]` cast cannot hide the mismatch again. Add an adapter-level test that runs beginRun and asserts 'Select target · analysis'. Optionally, for a clicked fused contraction with no phraseme, return ADP[clicked] from the fusion table instead of calling the classifier.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes one jev round trip from about 99% of clicks: −~760 ms median (range 300-1780) on grammar-visible, emoji-visible and commit. Click-to-commit median would go from 4281 to about 3520 ms, and grammar would be visible at about 0.55 s instead of about 1.3 s. hypotheses.title: No Luna timeout, no retries, and every generation failure is marked non-retryable
hypotheses.claim: One transient provider error, hang or invalid response turns the whole click into a PermanentFailure. The durable-retry machinery (3 runs, backoff) never runs for generation failures, and a hung Luna request can block a click for more than a minute.
hypotheses.evidence:
- promptsmith openai.ts:75-87: fetch has only request.signal, no timeout.
- Trace 95830705: generateReadingEmojiDescription 'fetch failed' after 70,141 ms; the user had to retry manually, and the retry succeeded in 1146 ms.
- resolutionFailure.ts:38-53 maps ProviderFailure and InvalidModelOutput to retryable:false, so resolutionSessions.ts:683-716 computes canRetry=false and ends Terminal PermanentFailure.
- judgment.ts:131-137 and trace.ts:24-36 set maxRetries 0; the jev timeout is 10 s.
hypotheses.proposedChange:
- Add a per-call timeout for Luna. The observed maximum is about 3.5 s, so 6-8 s via AbortSignal.any.
- Retry once in-process on ProviderFailure or timeout, for both Luna and jev.
- For generation-stage InvalidModelOutput, regenerate once.
- Mark ProviderFailure retryable:true so the durable retry catches the rest.
- Keep jev Unresolved answers unretried.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Transient provider failures become +1 call of latency instead of a failed click. Worst-case latency is capped at about 8 s + retry instead of 70 s. Frequency is low but user-visible; there are 6 more failures in the log, which came from a dev missing OPENAI_API_KEY (a fail-fast config check would stop those from wasting a classify and a grammar call first).
hypotheses.risk: Duplicate spend on the retried call (negligible). An invalid-output retry could hide a systematic prompt bug; log each retry as a generation event.
hypotheses.experiment: Fault injection through DumgenOptions.execute and judge in tests: fail, hang, or return invalid output 1 in 3 times, then assert the click completes. Live: 50 local clicks with a stub that drops 10% of fetches; metric is PermanentFailure count (expected 0) and added latency.

hypotheses.title: Produce headword proposals at intake so the click-time canonical question selects them instead of calling Luna
hypotheses.claim: When the surface is not the headword, the canonical question either triggers a sequential Luna generateCanonicalForm call (~1.2 s on the critical path) or wrongly accepts the inflected surface. One Luna call per sentence at intake (background) could propose each target's dictionary headword. Passed in as a canonicalFormAlternative, it would remove the click-time Luna call and the wrong Lemmas.
hypotheses.evidence:
Traces:
- 2ce3993d überlebt and ea390a13 waren: features → CandidateIsNotCanonical (0.74 / 0.77) → Luna 1222 / 1248 ms, sequential (judgments.ts:568-570, 608-690).
- 1e976b81 Banken: alternatives ['Die','Banken'] → candidate_1 0.84 → Lemma 'Banken'.
- c5446c8c sind: CandidateIsCanonical 0.56 → Lemma 'sind'.

So 4 of 11 resolved clicks needed a headword different from the surface: 2 paid 1.2 s and 2 stored a wrong Lemma, which splits the dictionary. The emoji and the drafts both take lemma.canonicalForm as input (resolve.ts:153-162, draft.ts:120-133), so everything waits on the canonical form.
hypotheses.proposedChange:
After intake analysis (background):
- Make one Luna call per sentence: marked sentence plus target list in, {targetId: headword} out.
- Store it on the analysis.
- At click time, inject a route-matched synthetic Lemma candidate carrying that headword into resolveGrammar's existing lemmaCandidates parameter (production.ts:115-135).
- Drop raw inflected NOUN members from the alternatives.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: −~1.2 s on clicks whose surface is not the headword (~20-40% of open-class clicks: verbs, plurals, declined adjectives) for grammar, emoji and commit. Fewer wrong Lemma identities (2 of 11 in the log). Cost about $0.0005 per sentence, including never-clicked sentences.
hypotheses.risk: jev may accept a wrong proposal, since candidates are only 'suggestions'. The headword quality of Luna on context-free lists is unmeasured. Staleness is not an issue because a headword does not depend on the dictionary.
hypotheses.experiment:
A harness that calls dumgen.resolveGrammar with a Luna-proposed headword injected as a lemmaCandidate, against production with an empty candidate list:
- grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb (77), noun (45) and adjective (32)
- 2 runs each

hypotheses.title: Persist the text before analysis finishes, then analyse in the background with higher concurrency
hypotheses.claim: submitText only returns after every sentence's analyzeSentence finishes, at concurrency 4, behind a barrier on all segment decisions. The learner waits several seconds to see text that could appear after segmentation.
hypotheses.evidence:
- linguisticOrchestration.ts:319-359: segment Promise.all, then Effect.forEach(concurrency 4), then persist.
- Submission 2c7c856e, 18 sentences, 10,303 ms total. Segment took 6,180 ms (sequential then; parallel since a6b665cf). The analysis phase ran from 6,191 to 10,168 ms: 4.0 s for per-sentence durations of 305-1805 ms, running ⌈18/4⌉ waves.

hypotheses.proposedChange:
- Persist segments right after segment, and return textId.
- Schedule an internal action that analyses with concurrency ≈ sentence count (bounded to about 12-25) and inserts each analysis as it lands.
- Start analysis per sentence as soon as its segment decision arrives, removing the barrier.

hypotheses.risk: TypeSafe rate limits at 25+ concurrent chunked requests. Clicks in the first ~2 s pay classify (~760 ms). The UI must tolerate the analysis arriving later.
hypotheses.experiment: Submit a 25-sentence text (unwrapped HP chapter) 3 times at concurrency 4 and 3 times at 25, with inspection. Metrics: 'Analyze submitted text' duration, persist time, per-call latency, and failed or 429 analyses.

hypotheses.title: One Unresolved intake judgment rejects the whole submitted text
hypotheses.claim: If any sentence's language, validity or stitching answer is Unresolved, dumgen.segment throws, Promise.all rejects, and submitText fails with no partial result. Short headings, fragments (see H2) and code-switched lines raise the odds.
hypotheses.evidence: segment.ts:101-111 throws DumgenFailure('Unresolved', 'segment'); segment.ts:186-190 uses Promise.all; linguisticOrchestration.ts:319-326 yields it without a catch; convex orchestration.ts:260-293 has only `finally`. By contrast, analyzeSentence failures are caught and dropped (linguisticOrchestration.ts:381-390).
hypotheses.proposedChange: Re-ask once per sentence. If still Unresolved, degrade that sentence instead of failing the text: accept it as German with stitchTrustedText when language argmax is de and validity is not Unintelligible; otherwise drop it as Unintelligible.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Fewer whole-text rejections (rate unknown until measured); each one currently loses the whole submission.
hypotheses.risk: May accept a few poor sentences, which then produce Unresolved clicks instead.
hypotheses.experiment: Run `cli/evaluate.ts --experiment intake` (6 cases), plus dumgen.segment over the 30 stored sentences and 16 wrapped fragments, 3 runs each; count Unresolved per sentence. Add a unit test that injects one Unresolved to confirm the whole-text failure.

hypotheses.title: Every Luna call opens a new TLS connection; warm or multiplex it before the emoji call
hypotheses.claim: The emoji call on the critical path, and the 4 concurrent draft calls, each open a fresh connection to api.openai.com, adding ~80-240 ms to the emoji call. The first jev call probably pays the same.
hypotheses.evidence: resolutionRuns trace metadata.timing.detailed for all 16 successful emoji calls: connection.reused=false. connectionMs was 86.7, 84.1, 75.9, 95.3, 143.3, 91.1 and 240.5 ms. headersMs minus providerProcessingMs was typically 300-500 ms. Drafts and emoji start within about 40 ms of each other (inspection timelines), so HTTP/1.1 needs 5 handshakes.
hypotheses.proposedChange: At action start (in parallel with beginRun and grammar), fire-and-forget a cheap request to api.openai.com and the TypeSafe host through a shared keep-alive undici Agent. Optionally enable allowH2 so the 5 concurrent Luna calls share one connection.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: −80-240 ms on the emoji call (emoji-visible and commit milestones), and probably a similar saving on the first jev call.
hypotheses.risk: Low. Confirm HTTP/2 support and keep-alive behaviour in the Convex node runtime.
hypotheses.experiment: cli/sample-reading.ts or benchmark-reading.ts on reading-generation/de with and without a warm-up request before each sample: 30 interleaved samples. Metrics: detailed.connection.connectionMs and totalMs.

hypotheses.title: The emoji call may be slowed by the 4 concurrent draft calls; measure, then stagger or duplicate
hypotheses.claim: The critical emoji call (6-10 output tokens) is slower than the concurrent drafts that produce longer outputs. It always runs alongside 4-5 Luna draft calls started 20-40 ms earlier. Contention at the org, queue or connection level may be inflating it.
hypotheses.evidence: Emoji median 2210 ms (n=11, 848-3491), against a ~1 s median measured alone (memory note, 2026-09-18). Draft-aspect medians were 1198-1689 ms. providerProcessingMs was 612-2932, with non-provider gaps up to 2.1 s (098724c9: headers 3129 vs provider 1067). The draft fork comes just before the emoji call (linguisticOrchestration.ts:478-512). There is no control group without drafts in the log.
hypotheses.proposedChange: If confirmed: delay the draft fork until the emoji request has its response headers, or cap drafts to 2 concurrent calls; alternatively send the emoji request twice and take the first (cost +~$0.0001).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: If contention is real: −0.5-1.0 s median on emoji-visible. If it is not, duplicating the request alone should still cut the >2 s tail (6 of 16 calls) at roughly double emoji spend.
hypotheses.risk: Delaying drafts pushes definition visibility later. Duplicates make things worse if the latency comes from contention.
hypotheses.experiment: cli/sample-reading.ts on reading-generation/de (52 cases), 3 samples, --concurrency 1 vs 5 in interleaved order, plus a variant that fires 4 draft-shaped calls per emoji call. Metrics: emoji totalMs and providerProcessingMs, p50 and p90.

hypotheses.title: Start emoji generation in parallel with the jev compare when stored candidates exist
hypotheses.claim: For a known Lemma, the jev compare (~310 ms) and the Luna generation on NoMatch (~1.3-2.2 s) run one after the other. Starting generation speculatively hides the compare on NoMatch clicks.
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:100-153 runs the compare, then resolve.ts:152-163 generates. All 11 logged clicks had empty candidates, so this matters only once the dictionary has Readings.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Fire textModelCaller for the emoji concurrently with the compare and discard it on Reuse. Combine with emoji-collision-as-reuse.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: −~310-400 ms on NoMatch clicks for known Lemmas; 0 on first clicks. Wasted Luna spend on Reuse is about $0.0001 per click.
hypotheses.risk: Wasted calls; more collisions (see next hypothesis).
hypotheses.experiment: Use reading-resolution/de (67 cases) to get the NoMatch share, then simulate the latency gain from the measured distributions. Live A/B on 30 known-lemma clicks.

hypotheses.title: A generated emoji that equals a stored candidate fails the whole click
hypotheses.claim: When jev says NoMatch but Luna, independently and without seeing the candidates, produces an existing candidate, dumgen throws InvalidModelOutput. That is non-retryable, so the click fails permanently, even though the collision is strong evidence that the Reading should be reused.
hypotheses.evidence: resolve.ts:164-170 throws 'Generated Reading collides with a candidate rejected by TypeSafe'. The generation input is only markedContext and the lemma (resolve.ts:153-162). resolutionFailure.ts:43-52 makes it retryable:false.
hypotheses.proposedChange: On a collision, return {decision: 'Reuse', emojiDescription}, or regenerate once with the rejected candidates listed as descriptions to avoid.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes a whole-click failure mode whose rate grows as the dictionary fills; the rate is unmeasured.
hypotheses.risk: May reuse a Reading that jev correctly rejected, if Luna keeps producing a generic emoji.
hypotheses.experiment: reading-resolution/de NoMatch cases: sample generation 5 times each with cli/sample-reading.ts and count exact collisions with the stored candidates.

hypotheses.title: NOT worth it now: hop and module-weight work, draft-join decoupling, GrammarAvailable/find reordering
hypotheses.claim: The remaining waits the task framing suspected are small or do not change what the learner sees.
hypotheses.evidence:
- Convex hops measured locally: selectSegment 91 ms, beginRun 39, GrammarAvailable 43, find 32, ReadingAvailable 39, commit 67, recordRunSuccess 28.
- Module bundles are 1.0-1.3 MB (my esbuild measurement), but hops are not 300-700 ms any more.
- GrammarAvailable and findStoredReadings already run in parallel; waiting for both costs about 10 ms.
- The draft join delays only the Complete state, not the definition: definitions come from the drafts either way (knowledge generation starts about 3 ms after commit), and the grammar and emoji are shown before commit (resolving-reading-note.tsx:29-76). Draft-join waits: median 101 ms, mean 459.
- Inspection capture adds no hops while running (inspectionAction.ts:42-76).
- Fused-contraction fallback: 1 of 138 segments.
- Publishing drafts inside persistResolvedClick instead of the scheduled action would save about 200 ms on definition visibility only.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Do not split resolutionSessions.ts, reorder GrammarAvailable and findStoredReadings, or decouple the draft join. At most, skip advance(ReadingAvailable) on Reuse (~40 ms), and gate drafts on New (saves about $0.001 per reuse click, no latency change).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Under 50 ms each, versus about 760 ms (H1), 1.2 s (H4) and 0.4 s (H5).
hypotheses.risk: None if not done.
hypotheses.experiment: After H1, re-run 20 inspected clicks and read the hop steps; revisit only if cloud hops exceed about 150 ms.

audits.stage: Target selection at click time (stored Sentence Analysis vs the classifyTarget jev fallback), plus segmentation and placement (segment, latin-segmentation, placement.ts, host sentence splitting)
audits.howItWorks:
CORRECTION to the brief: dumgen.segment is not model-free. universal/segment.ts:37-111 makes one jev call per source sentence ("segment"/"intake": 3 Choices for language, validity and stitching, about 650 input tokens, p50 408 ms in today's waterfall). If stitching=="Needed" it then makes one Luna whitespace-repair generation (segment.ts:114-160). Only after that does the deterministic segmentLatin run. All sentences are judged in one Promise.all (segment.ts:186-190). A sentence whose language or validity comes back Unresolved throws (segment.ts:101-111), and so does any transport failure (judgment.ts:136 sets retry maxRetries 0). The host has no catch around segment (linguisticOrchestration.ts:320), so one bad sentence fails the whole text submission.

INTAKE: once every sentence's segment decision is in, the host runs analyzeSentence for each accepted German sentence with Effect.forEach concurrency 4 (linguisticOrchestration.ts:351), then makes one persistSubmittedText call (:354).
- analyzeGermanSentence (sentence-analysis/operation.ts) calls placeSegments first. That is pure code: fusion split, clitic and abbreviation surfaces.
- It then asks one jev call over state {sentence: indexedContext, criteria: notation+realizationCriteria, fixedness}. The questions are: n(n-1) anchored membership Choices, n route, n role, one identity Choice per closed-class spelling, n fixedness Scores, n Phraseme-Kind Choices and n(n-1)/2 pair Nouls. Batches are chunked at 220 questions and the chunks run in parallel. In the waterfall this averaged 71-78 questions and about 17k input tokens, p50 422-431 ms.
- assembleAnalysis (pure code) builds the partition: connected components at tau 0.6, groupVote route, noun-article and route guards, a fusion-table ADP singleton plus a fused article attached to the next NOUN, and Phraseme pairs projected by Head with a fixedness floor of 1.5.
- Any failure of the analysis is swallowed and the sentence is stored with no analysis (linguisticOrchestration.ts:365-390).

CLICK: after loadResolutionContext, selectTarget (linguisticOrchestration.ts:668-716) calls selectAnalysisTarget (sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:33-83). This is pure code: stitched-text check, then the anchor, which is the first analysed ResolvableText inside the clicked Segment. Then resolvedUnitAt picks the largest unit: the Phraseme if its Kind is not None/Unresolved, otherwise the Lexeme target by argmax route. A stored Segment counts as a member only if every analysed piece inside it is covered. The host then runs validateEncounter.

The fallback is dumgen.classifyTarget (target-classification/judgments.ts:33-76): one jev call with state {sentence, clickedSegmentIndex, criteria: the full targetCriteria}, one member_<i> Choice per other resolvable Segment, plus one route Choice over 19 routes (Lexeme and Phraseme, no PUNCT/X). assembleTarget then fails the whole click if any member Choice's argmax is Unresolved, if the route is Unresolved, or if a NOUN has a stray article. The fallback sits on the critical path, sequential before resolveGrammar: 325 ms p50, about 3.5k input tokens. It runs when:
- there is no analysis (intake failed, or a legacy sentence);
- the analysis stitchedText differs from the stored one;
- the anchor unit is null (guard or Unresolved route);
- the clicked Segment is not covered by the unit (every fused-word click);
- validateEncounter throws.

Downstream, only family, kind and memberSegmentIndices are consumed. Roles and identity mass are not passed to resolveGrammar.

MEASURED (no API calls): prototypes/audit/target-fallback-replay.ts replays the stored production-shaped intake run (/tmp/intake-clicks-...-layered-trimmed-roles-phraseme-score-1.json: 110 sentences, 620 occurrences, 238 gold clicks) through the production placeSegments, assembleAnalysis and resolvedUnitAt, plus a verbatim copy of selectAnalysisTarget.
- Shipped selector: 229 of 238 gold clicks served from the analysis, 9 fall back (6 from the stitched-text mismatch, 3 fused). Clicking every occurrence: 596 analysis, 18 stitched, 6 clickedNotMember, 0 guard.
- On other production-shaped stored runs, guard fallbacks are 0-3 of 620.
- Live waterfall from today (prototypes/audit/results/summary-baseline.json): 68 of 78 clicks served from the analysis, 10 classified. 8 of those are one sentence whose analyze call hit a socket error; 2 are fused words (ins, am).
- Gold match: analysis 58/68, classified 7/10. Of the 8 non-fused classified clicks, 5 matched gold. Examples of fallback errors: [auf dem Markt] ADP, [dem Markt] DET, usw. Unresolved.

calls.name: segment (language/validity/stitching judgment)
calls.when: always, once per source sentence at text submit
calls.sequentialAfter: host splitInSentences (Intl.Segmenter); all sentences in parallel via Promise.all

calls.name: segment stitching repair
calls.when: conditional: stitching judgment == Needed

calls.name: analyzeSentence
calls.when: always for each Accepted German sentence; chunked at 220 questions per call, chunks run in parallel
calls.sequentialAfter: ALL segment decisions (Promise.all), then host Effect.forEach concurrency 4
calls.questions: n(n-1) membership + n route + n role + id per closed-class spelling + n fix + n pk + n(n-1)/2 same; 36-145 in the 16 fixture sentences

calls.name: classifyTarget (fallback)
calls.when: conditional: no stored analysis, stitchedText mismatch, fused-word click (clickedNotMember), Unresolved or guarded unit, or validateEncounter failure; 10/78 clicks live, 9/238 gold clicks and 24/620 occurrences in the offline replay
calls.questions: (resolvable-1) member_i Choices + 1 route Choice (19 routes + Unresolved)

unusedOrRedundantInputs: The stored analysis carries per-member roles (Article, Auxiliary, Reflexive, GovernedPreposition, Expletive, SeparableParticle) and an Identity Mass for closed-class heads. The click path uses only family, kind and offsets (sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:69-82). Identity only affects single-member routes through effectiveRoute (analysis.ts:214-223). resolveGrammar gets only Encounter and lemmaCandidates (production.ts resolveGrammar), so it re-derives structure and may pay a second authoredIdentity round trip (6/77 clicks live, about 300 ms each).

Abbreviation entries in the fusion table carry an authored `kind` (fusion-entries.ts:314 on; 31 entries). Nothing reads it at runtime. placement.ts:86-87 sets only `surface`, and no question sees `surface` because the judge reads indexedContext of the original text. Offline, the table kind matches gold 9/9 while the intake route vote matches 4/9 (usw. -> X twice, o.Ä. -> X, d.h. -> ADV, Dipl.-Ing. -> PROPN).
Clitic and abbreviation `surface` expansions (for example 's -> es, z.B. -> zum Beispiel) are computed in placement but never shown to the judge in analyzeSentence or classifyTarget.

target-classification/projection.ts (compact <target> prompt seam, additionalMemberIndices) and guidance.ts (productionDemonstrationGuidance) are used only by corpus.ts for golden-corpus projection and explanations. Neither is on the production path, and classifyGermanTarget sends no demonstrations. Their wording ('return only mit's i as the additional member', 'Return Unresolved with both nullable fields null') describes a retired output format.
When a target is guarded, assemble.ts:344 replaces its routeMass with {Unresolved:1}. The model's route mass is thrown away, so no host-side floor or second-best policy can ever use it.
classifyTarget resends the full targetCriteria (~1,055 words) on every fallback click, even though the intake already judged the same sentence under a near-identical text.
promptProblems: The two prompts define a unit in two different ways. The fallback's targetCriteria (judgments.ts:22) opens 'Select the largest complete fixed learner-facing unit containing the clicked occurrence' and says (judgments.ts:26) 'A Funktionsverbgefüge ... is one Collocation target whose members are the verb, the noun and the noun's own article or fused preposition'. The intake's realizationCriteria (criteria.ts:14-34) replaces the opening with 'one dictionary word together with its fixed grammatical members. A multiword expression (an idiom, a collocation, a Funktionsverbgefüge, a proverb, a formula) is not a unit here'. As a result, a fallback click inside an FVG or idiom whose Phraseme layer stayed under the 1.5 floor returns the whole expression, while intake-served clicks in the same sentence return single words. That is a MembershipConflict ('partialOverlap', convex/persistence.ts:509-535) after all grammar, emoji and draft work has already been spent.

Fused words are handled differently too. Fallback (judgments.ts:28): 'A fused preposition/article source word (im, zum, zur, ins) is a singleton ADP unless inside a larger fixed expression.' Intake (criteria.ts:25 replacement): 'A fused preposition and article (im, zum, ins, zur) is one ADP unit whose article part belongs to the following noun.' The gold follows neither prompt fully for fixed adverbials: 'zum Beispiel', 'zum Teil' and 'Im Allgemeinen' are gold Lexeme/ADV [zum, Beispiel] (ADR 0009). The intake can never produce that shape, because the model puts route ADP and role Free on every fused word and assemble.ts:297-321 forces the ADP into a singleton. The stranded article then becomes a 'fusion-table:unattached-article' DET (4-6 per 110 sentences).

The route inventories differ. Fallback routes (assembly.ts:13-43) have 5 Phraseme routes, no Lexeme/PUNCT or Lexeme/X, and shorter descriptions ('Determiner modifying a noun'). Intake lexemeRoutes (criteria.ts:42-70) have PUNCT and X, and a DET 'never the absorbed article der/die/das/ein of a noun'. So the same word can get different Kinds on the two paths. Example: 'Ihc' is X from the intake, then grammar fails with 'support Unresolved'.

The fallback's route Unresolved option (assembly.ts:41-42) reads 'The exact assembled group is invalid, incomplete, includes free material, or has no defensible allowed route'. But routeQuestion (assembly.ts:102-105) is asked in the same round trip as membership, and the judge never sees an assembled group; the comment at judgments.ts:39-43 admits this. The same stale two-call wording closes targetCriteria (judgments.ts:31: 'A target is defensible only when the exact assembled members form ... do not repair, trim, extend or replace the assembled group'), and it survives verbatim into the intake realizationCriteria. Neither one-call design has an assembled group. Per prototypes/intake/README, rewording collapsed membership accuracy (114 vs 164), so this should be measured, not simply edited.

Intake realizationCriteria still speaks of clicks ('containing the clicked occurrence', 'All fixed-member clicks must select exactly the same unit', 'Article clicks resolve the same noun', 'clicking Weg in Der Weg ist das Ziel'), even though intake asks about every anchor and has no click. The measurements say to keep it verbatim. Listed here as a known oddity, not a recommendation to change.

realizationCriteria is built by five string .replace() calls on targetCriteria (criteria.ts:14-34). All five match today (checked locally). An edit to targetCriteria for the fallback's sake would silently change the intake prompt, or leave a replace() as a no-op, and no test would fail.

The fallback fails the whole click if any single member question has argmax Unresolved (assembly.ts:136-142). The intake instead symmetrizes Include mass and thresholds it at 0.6. Same question, two decision rules.

hypotheses.title: Capitalized fused words (Im/Am/Zum/Beim/Vom/Ins...) break the stitched-text check, so every click in that sentence falls back to classifyTarget
hypotheses.claim: placeSegments writes the fusion table's lowercase spans ('i','m') in place of the source letters. For 'Im Sommer...' the analysis stitchedText becomes 'im Sommer...', and selectAnalysisTarget returns null at sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:41 for every click in that sentence. Each click then pays one more jev round trip (~330 ms) and gets the less accurate single-anchor classification under the other unit definition.
hypotheses.evidence: placement.ts:64-71: `for (const component of fusion.components) push("ResolvableText", component.span, first(component.surface))`. fusionEntry lowercases the lookup (fusion-table.ts:123-129). Local check (/tmp/tc-audit/stitch.ts): 'Im Sommer fahren wir ans Meer.' -> 'im Sommer...' MISMATCH; same for Am/Zum/Beim/Vom/Ins and 'INS'. Offline replay (prototypes/audit/target-fallback-replay.ts): 18 of 620 occurrences (2.9%) and 6 of 238 gold clicks fall back for this reason alone (2 of 110 sentences: 'Im Workshop...', 'Im Allgemeinen...'). With the placement repaired, gold clicks served from the analysis go 229 -> 235 and gold matches 152 -> 156. In the 330 unique corpus sentences, 1.2% contain a capitalized fused word; in real prose, sentence-initial Im/Am/Zum/Beim is common, but I have not measured that rate. No test covers it: tests use lowercase 'zur'.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In placement.ts, push `segment.text.slice(pos, pos + component.span.length)` as the text and keep the table surface. Add a unit test that placeSegments(x).stitchedText equals the source for 'Im Sommer...'. Host mitigation for analyses already stored in Convex with lowercase text: in selectAnalysisTarget, compare stitchedText case-insensitively and require equal length, since the offsets are identical.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 330 ms saved on every click in affected sentences, which also move to the more accurate intake target (58/68 vs 7/10 gold in the waterfall; 162 vs 146 of 206 in the intake README). Mean saving is about 0.03 x 330 ≈ 10 ms per click on corpus-like text, more on prose with sentence-initial fused prepositions. Removes one source of definitional inconsistency. Zero model cost.
hypotheses.risk: Very low. Offsets and lengths do not change, only letter case in analysed Segment text. The playground lattice will show 'Im' instead of 'im'.
hypotheses.experiment: Offline first: `bun prototypes/audit/target-fallback-replay.ts` shows shipped 229/9 vs repaired 235/3 on 238 gold clicks, and every-occurrence fallback 24 -> 6 of 620. Live: add 3-4 sentences with sentence-initial Im/Am/Zum to the sentence-analysis/de fixtures (or pass them via waterfall --sentences), then run `bun --env-file=../../.env.local prototypes/audit/waterfall.ts --sentences <ids> --label caps` before and after. Metrics: coverage.classified count, meanSelectClassifiedMs, targetMatchesGold. One run is enough because the effect is deterministic; judge noise only affects targets, not the path taken.

hypotheses.title: Retry analyzeSentence (and segment) once on ProviderFailure; today one transport blip silently sends a whole sentence's clicks to the fallback
hypotheses.claim: judgmentCaller hard-codes `retry: { maxRetries: 0 }`, and the host swallows analyze failures. A fast-failing transport error on one intake call therefore drops the analysis, and every later click in that sentence pays classifyTarget (+~330 ms) with lower accuracy and the inconsistent unit definition. The same zero-retry policy on the segment call can fail the whole submission.
hypotheses.evidence: judgment.ts:136 `retry: { maxRetries: 0 }`. linguisticOrchestration.ts:381 `Effect.catchAll(... return null)`. In today's waterfall (baseline-baseline.json), 3 of 48 intake.analyze calls failed in about 40 ms each with 'Connection error: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly', on different sentences each time (usw, relativ, passiv), so the errors are transient. The 'usw' sentence lost its analysis, and 8 of 78 clicks (10%) went to classifyTarget: gold match 5/8, including [auf dem Markt] ADP, [dem Markt] DET and usw. classify:Unresolved. Caveat: that run used Bun; production runs in Convex 'use node' (convex/orchestration.ts), where the flake rate is unknown.
hypotheses.proposedChange: For the analyzeSentence and segment stages only (off the click path), retry once when transport == Failure, including chunk-level retry inside analyzeGermanSentence's Promise.all. Either pass maxRetries:1 from judgmentCaller when the stage is analyzeSentence or segment, or wrap in the host with Effect.retry({times:1}) when the tag is ProviderFailure. Log the analyze failure rate in production.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes the whole-sentence fallback for transient failures. At the observed ~6% per-call failure rate this is ≈6% of sentences, whose clicks each save ~330 ms (mean ≈ 20 ms/click) and gain the intake's accuracy (≈ +1-2 points on overall target accuracy). The retry costs about 40 ms plus one call, only on failed sentences.
hypotheses.risk: Low. The retry is at intake, so worst-case latency on a failed sentence is +~450 ms of intake wall time. It must not retry InvalidModelOutput blindly on the click path; this change is intake-only.
hypotheses.experiment: Measure the base rate for free with a Convex query: the fraction of German sentences stored with analysis == null, plus Convex logs for 'Sentence Analysis failed'. Live: `bun --env-file=../../.env.local prototypes/audit/waterfall.ts --intake-only --intake-repeats 5 --label retry` with and without the retry. Metric: sentences stored without analysis per 80 analyze calls, and intake wall time. Five repeats are needed because the flake is rare.

hypotheses.title: Serve fused-word clicks (im/zum/zur/ins/am...) from the stored fusion-table ADP target instead of calling classifyTarget
hypotheses.claim: Today 100% of clicks on a non-capitalized fused word fall back ('clickedNotMember'). The selector demands that every analysed piece of the stored Segment be in the unit, and a fused word's article piece belongs to the NOUN or a stray DET. The intake already holds the answer: a fusion-table ADP singleton, or the Phraseme when the whole expression was established. The fallback returns exactly that ADP singleton anyway.
hypotheses.evidence: sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:72-81 (all-inside rule, then `if (!memberSegmentIndices.includes(clickedSegmentIndex)) return null`). The tested design at app/tf-demo/tests/linguistic-orchestration.test.ts:1219 ('a click on the fused `zur` itself ... is classified') has the mock classifier return [8] ADP. In the live waterfall, kino#6 'ins' and museum#8 'am' were classified as [ins] ADP and [am] ADP (325-340 ms each). In the offline replay, all 6 non-capitalized fused occurrences of 620 fall back. With an 'anchor-member' rule (a stored Segment belongs when its own first ResolvableText piece is in the unit), gold clicks served go 235 -> 238, gold match +1, and no previously served click changes: the rule differs only on multi-piece stored Segments, which are fusions. The rule also fixes a latent bug. For 'zum Beispiel', the Phraseme covers zu and Beispiel but not the stranded m, so a click on 'Beispiel' today yields a one-member Phraseme/Collocation [Beispiel]. Fused words are 1.8% of resolvable tokens (34/1897) and appear in 9.7% of the 330 corpus sentences.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In selectAnalysisTarget, decide membership by each stored Segment's anchor piece (the same rule already used to anchor the click), not by requiring every piece to be covered. Optionally, in assembleAnalysis, add the fused-article offset to a Phraseme's derived offsets whenever the Phraseme contains its fusion's ADP. Update the test at linguistic-orchestration.test.ts:1219 to expect zero classifyTarget requests.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About 330 ms saved on every fused-word click (≈1-2% of clicks; mean ≈ 5 ms). Removes the main live path to fallback-produced whole-FVG targets such as [stellte, zur, Verfügung] next to intake-produced [Verfügung] NOUN, which is the MembershipConflict scenario. Zero model cost.
hypotheses.risk: Low. Fixed adverbials whose gold is multi-member ADV (zum Beispiel, zum Teil, im Allgemeinen: 3 gold cases) get ADP [zum] or Collocation [zum, Beispiel] instead of whatever the fallback would say, and I have no stored fallback outputs for those 3. 'am' before a superlative (am besten) is split as a fusion regardless.
hypotheses.experiment: Offline: `bun prototypes/audit/target-fallback-replay.ts` (variants 'repaired' vs 'repaired+anchorMember', plus the per-case fused-click listing at the end). Live: `bun --env-file=../../.env.local prototypes/audit/waterfall.ts --sentences kino,museum,verfuegung --label fused` before and after. Metrics: classify calls (2 -> 0), critical path on those clicks, grammar outcome. Also run classifyTarget 3x on the 3 fixed-adverbial gold cases to see whether the fallback beats the intake there (≈ $0.001).

hypotheses.title: When a German sentence has no stored analysis, run analyzeSentence at click (in parallel with, or instead of, classifyTarget) and persist it
hypotheses.claim: The classifyTarget fallback is a per-click re-ask of the intake's own membership question, from one anchor only. It is slower in aggregate and less accurate. For sentences with no analysis (legacy rows, failed intake), analyzing lazily once makes every later click in the sentence free and consistent.
hypotheses.evidence: Per click: classify p50 325 ms, 3.5k tokens. Per sentence: analyze p50 422-431 ms, about 17k tokens (summary-baseline.json stageStats). Accuracy: intake 162 vs click-time 146 of 206 same-day (prototypes/intake/README 'Route policy'); live waterfall gold match analysis 58/68 vs classified 7/10. The usw sentence took 8 sequential fallback clicks in the waterfall, each paying +~330 ms.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In selectTarget (linguisticOrchestration.ts:668-716), when context.analysis is null and the sentence is German, fork analyzeSentence and persist its result off the critical path. For the current click, either (a) still run classifyTarget concurrently, so first-click latency is unchanged and later clicks use the analysis, or (b) await the analysis, which costs +~100 ms on the first click and makes it consistent. Prefer (a) while classifyTarget exists.

audits.stage: Cross-cutting audit of input bloat and prompt consistency across all dumgen stages (intake segment + analyzeSentence, click classify fallback, resolveGrammar and its follow-ups, reading compare/generate, draftKnowledge), measured offline with no model calls
audits.howItWorks:
The measurements come from a new throwaway script, /Users/annagorelova/work/textfresser-batteries/battery/dumgen/prototypes/audit/measure-inputs.ts. It runs with `bun prototypes/audit/measure-inputs.ts` (options `--json out.json` and `--dump <label>:<caseId>`), takes about 4 s and needs no API keys. It builds the real Dumgen from src with stub `judge`/`execute` executors and records every request through `onModelExchange`: state and questions for jev, system prompt and input for Luna. Grammar answers come from the reviewed ideal output via tests/grammar-fixture.ts, so every follow-up fires exactly when gold answers would trigger it. The other stages get neutral answers.

Coverage: 330 distinct sentences (the 16 in the sentence-analysis corpus plus the distinct target-classification sentences), 541 classification clicks, all 21 grammar corpora (1,165 cases), 75 reading operation cases and 352 draft runs.

Token calibration: jev bills about 3.52 JSON chars per input token on 332 recorded grammar calls in .runs/dumgen, and 3.40 on the 15 live intake calls in prototypes/audit/results. So chars/3.5 is accurate to about 3%.

Verified pipeline (corrects the brief):
1. Intake: tf-demo splits the text into sentences, then `dumgen.segment`. This is not deterministic code. It makes one jev call per sentence (language, validity and stitching questions; about 650 tokens; p50 408 ms), all concurrent through Promise.all. A Luna whitespace-repair call follows only when stitching is Needed.
2. Then one `analyzeSentence` per German sentence at concurrency 4. Each is one jev call over state {sentence, criteria, fixedness}, with questions split into chunks of up to 220 run in parallel. The question count is n(n-1) membership + n route + n role + n fixedness + n phraseme-kind + n(n-1)/2 pair questions, plus one identity question per closed-class spelling.
3. The text is persisted only after all analyses finish.
4. Click: the stored analysis gives family, kind and member indices. Otherwise `classifyTarget` runs: one jev call of about 3.1k tokens.
5. `resolveGrammar` features: one jev call of 1.6k–6.1k tokens (p50 by route), 7–26 questions, all speculative in one round trip. Then, in series, only when needed: Luna canonical form or normalized members; jev lexical-strings; jev noun Case; jev DET/PRON authoredIdentity.
6. After grammar, `draftKnowledge` forks: 4 concurrent uncached Luna calls (definition, transcription, en, ru), 118–306 tokens each. In parallel: the Convex reading lookup, then `resolveOrGenerateReadingEmojiDescription`. That is a jev compare (about 335 tokens) when candidates exist, or an authored choice when a Lemma has several reviewed Readings, then Luna emoji generation (about 2.3k tokens, 1.9k of them cached).
7. The draft is joined when the Reading is New.
8. `produceKnowledge` runs later, off the click path.

Main measured facts:
- Intake payload grows O(n²): p50 9.7k tokens for ≤5 words, 17k for ≤8, 31k for ≤11, 50k for ≤15 and 77k for 16+. 82% of criteria chars and 86% of instruction chars are verbatim repeats. 39 of 381 calls exceed the 32k budget the chunker assumes; the largest is about 56k.
- Grammar payload has almost no latency cost: recorded medians are 304, 317 and 328 ms for 2–4k, 4–6k and 6–8k tokens.
- The costly items are round trips and whole-click Unresolved gates:
  - the `support` question;
  - Luna canonical-form follow-ups, which fire for 80/87 VERB cases under gold answers;
  - DET/PRON Core questions whose values the catalog already fixes;
  - emoji free-text failures.

The stitching question itself lists mostly deterministic conditions ('leading/trailing whitespace, non-ASCII whitespace or repeated spaces'). Its 498 ms sits serially on the intake wall time.

(:30); 'do not repair, trim, extend or replace the assembled group' (:31). Intake has no click and no assembled group. Established property predicates are ADJ with a separate VERB copula' (target-classification/judgments.ts:26). The grammar verbal policy (verbal-guidance.ts) has no such rule, yet the passive question offers 'State: State passive (Zustandspassiv) under the verbal route' (feature-questions.ts:451). (judgments.ts:195); policy.target 'Return Unresolved when a valid analysis is not defensible.' (judgments.ts:106); verbal policy 'An uncertain required analysis is Unresolved, never a guessed replacement or a repaired target'; and every feature's 'This feature applies, but the supplied evidence does not support a defensible value' (feature-questions.ts:521-522).
