DET gets no coverage question. partialCoveragePolicy says 'Partial coverage is otherwise allowed only for Idiom, DiscourseFormula, Proverb and Aphorism' (judgments.ts:127-128). production.ts:186 throws 'Partial realization requires a Phraseme or licensed shared noun article'.

Dangling references in route guidance. ADP says 'partType Vbp requires the lexical particle policy' (route-guidance.ts:22), but no state field supplies such a policy. NOUN says 'except the constrained binary suspended-compound completion described in the shared policy' (route-guidance.ts:15), but the text lives in policy.noun.suspension, not the shared policy.

Canonical-form policy conflicts with the orthography policy. 'The concrete `canonicalFormCandidate` is the attested members joined with single spaces; accept it only when that exact text already is the headword' (judgments.ts:110), and the candidate is the raw join (judgments.ts:151). The orthography policy calls sentence-initial capitals Standard. So 'Heute', 'Aber' or 'Obwohl' at a sentence start can never be CandidateIsCanonical and always cost a Luna call (32 open-route corpus cases).

Verbal policy mentions things that are not in play: 'Membership and the VERB/ADJ route are fixed.' (verbal-guidance.ts:16; ADJ inside the verbal policy) and 'Do not use aspect or gender in this verbal bag.' (features that are never asked).

Route inventories differ between intake (sentence-analysis/criteria.ts:42-70) and the classifyTarget fallback (target-classification/assembly.ts:13-43) for ADJ, ADP, ADV, CCONJ, DET, NOUN, SCONJ, VERB and Unresolved. The fallback has no Lexeme/X or Lexeme/PUNCT. So the same click can be routed under different definitions depending on whether intake covered it.

Fallback route question vs its own options: the Unresolved option says 'The exact assembled group is invalid, incomplete, includes free material, or has no defensible allowed route' (assembly.ts:41-42). The question asks about 'the complete fixed unit in `sentence` that contains the occurrence' (assembly.ts:103), and the code comment says 'The route is asked about the complete unit containing the click, not about the assembled group'.

Emoji generation prompt: 'Return only one to four emoji graphemes, directly as text.' is sent with outputFormat "text" and no schema (universal/model.ts:54). Demonstrations cover only ADJ/NOUN/VERB (generate/cases.ts: 38 ADJ, 27 VERB, 10 NOUN), yet production also generates for ADP, CCONJ, SCONJ, PART, ADV, PRON and others. Failing live outputs: '🔗 принадлагч' (des), '👩‍🦰relativpronomen' (relative die), '📅 monday calendar emoji maybe "📅" only? ...' (am), '🚪 escape?' (Ausweg), '😔 unfortunately' (leider).

Draft and produce prompts use different sense anchors. draft.ts:32 says 'The sentence is the sense anchor'; produce.ts:262 says 'The Reading's emojiDescription is the sense anchor: describe the meaning it names'. The same Reading's texts therefore depend on which path produced them. The draft translation prompt also lacks produce's guard ('gestern <TARGET>anstrengend</TARGET> gives strenuous in English, not yesterday was strenuous'). The emoji prompt's rule 'A copula, light verb, or other verb whose sentence meaning is carried by its complement contributes only its own part' has no counterpart in the draft definition prompt, so 'bleibt ... ruhig' can get 📍 but a definition about being calm.

text-guidance.ts:5 says 'All grammatical judgments and target membership are fixed and are not restated here', but the Luna input restates judgedCore, judgedSurface and memberOrthographies (judgments.ts:627-647). Minor.

Compare and generate disagree by construction. After jev answers NoMatch, the generation prompt never sees the rejected candidates (resolve.ts:158-161), yet resolve.ts:164-170 fails the whole click with 'Generated Reading collides with a candidate rejected by TypeSafe' (1/20 pass-2 runs in the waterfall).

hypotheses.title: Fail the grammar `support` gate only at P(Unresolved) >= 0.8, at least for targets selected from stored Sentence Analysis
hypotheses.claim: `support` is the biggest source of whole-click Unresolved in grammar. It is consumed first and any argmax Unresolved kills the click, but on gold targets its Unresolved mass is mostly 0.5-0.75. Those borderline rejections hit typos, separable verbs, perfect/passive complexes and governed prepositions.
hypotheses.evidence:
judgments.ts:194-199 (support choice: Supported 'Yes, keep route and membership unchanged' / Unresolved 'No defensible analysis on the supplied target'); judgments.ts:383 selected('support').

Recorded verb runs (.runs/dumgen, revision afaecd59 WIP, 77 eval cases each): support-gate failures 8/6/14/15, out of 12/8/15/16 total failures. Replaying the recorded probabilities, false rejections on gold-supported targets at thresholds >0.5 / >0.65 / >0.8 are 8/3/1, 6/4/1, 13/7/1 and 15/7/1. Examples: tanzd U=0.86-0.90; 'ist geschlossen' 0.74-0.80; 'wirken ... nach' 0.68-0.77; 'wartet auf' 0.74-0.75.

HEAD waterfall (77 natural clicks, prototypes/audit/results/baseline-baseline.json): support failures on museum#6 z.B. ADV at 0.75 (false), typo#0 Ihc X at 0.84 and verfuegung#6 [den] NOUN at 0.91 (true rejections of mis-assembled intake targets).
hypotheses.proposedChange: In resolveGrammarJudgments, fail on support only when probabilities.Unresolved >= 0.8 for analysis-selected targets. Keep argmax for classifyTarget fallback targets. Optionally add to the support criteria: 'Typos, separated particles, perfect/future/passive complexes, governed prepositions and state passives are supported targets.'
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Verb corpus false rejections drop from 6-15 to 1 per 77 cases (-7 to -18 points on hard verbal constructions). On natural clicks it removes the false rejection (z.B.) and keeps both true ones: about -1.3% whole-click failures. No latency change.
hypotheses.risk: Mis-assembled intake targets with U in 0.5-0.8 would reach Reading generation. The recorded runs predate HEAD. Must check the gold-Unresolved cases (Collocation 11, PRON 8, DET 1, NOUN 1) are still rejected.
hypotheses.experiment: From battery/dumgen: bun run build:js, then baseline vs variant with `bun --env-file=../../.env.local cli/evaluate.ts --experiment grammatical-resolution/de/lexeme/verb --revision <rev>-support08`. Repeat for lexeme/noun, lexeme/pronoun, lexeme/determiner and phraseme/collocation, 2 runs each. Metrics: pass count, 'Unresolved applicable question support' count, gold-Unresolved still rejected. Compare case by case (noise ~5 cases). The zero-cost pre-check is already done by measure-inputs.ts recordedSupport().

hypotheses.title: Add the lowercase-initial joined members to canonicalFormAlternatives on every non-noun route
hypotheses.claim: canonicalFormCandidate is the raw attested join and non-NOUN alternatives contain only stored Lemmas. A capitalized sentence-initial open-class word therefore can never be CandidateIsCanonical and always forces the serial Luna generateCanonicalForm call (p50 970 ms).
hypotheses.evidence: judgments.ts:151 (candidate = members.join(' ')); judgments.ts:158-165 (alternatives = stored Lemmas plus noun members only); policy judgments.ts:110 'accept it only when that exact text already is the headword'. measure-inputs.ts canonicalCoverage: under gold answers, 32 open-route corpus cases need Luna only to lowercase the first letter (ADV 10, ADP 8, SCONJ 4, INTJ 3, CCONJ 2, PART 2, ADJ 1, NUM 1, X 1).
hypotheses.proposedChange: canonicalFormAlternatives += lowerInitial(canonicalFormCandidate) for all Kinds except NOUN/PROPN (the choice already caps at 64).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes one ~1 s Luna round trip from each click on a sentence-initial adverb, conjunction, preposition or particle. The natural rate is unknown (0 of 13 live follow-ups were casing-only), so the mean gain is small but the per-click gain is large where it applies.
hypotheses.risk: Near zero: jev still has to judge the exact headword. NOUN/PROPN are excluded to avoid lowercase homographs.
hypotheses.experiment: Evaluate lexeme/adverb, adposition, subordinating-conjunction, coordinating-conjunction, particle and interjection, baseline vs variant, 2 runs. Metrics: grammar.text follow-up count (from traces), pass count, canonicalForm exact match.

hypotheses.title: Supply rule-derived infinitive/base candidates in the features round trip (VERB, ADJ, NOUN, ADV)
hypotheses.claim: Even with perfect jev answers, the serial Luna canonical-form call fires for 80/87 VERB, 26/38 ADJ, 22/53 NOUN and 32/56 ADV corpus cases. It is the main reason VERB grammar p50 is 1231 ms vs 327 ms for NOUN in the HEAD waterfall. Cheap deterministic candidates would let the existing `canonical` choice select the headword in the same round trip.
hypotheses.evidence: judgments.ts:280-296 (canonical choice over alternatives, capped by .slice(0,64)) and 608-690 (Luna generation). measure-inputs.ts: suffix, participle, zu, particle and sich rules cover VERB 43/80, ADJ 16/26, NOUN 11/22 and ADV 11/32; with a 30-form irregular table VERB reaches 60/80 (optimistic because the table is corpus-informed). Rules cover 10 of 13 live waterfall follow-ups (heiße→heiß, kauft→kaufen, öffnet→öffnen, habe→haben, wird geliefert→liefern, wartet→warten, hat sich an erinnert→sich erinnern, kennt→kennen, Nachbarn→Nachbar, Schülern→Schüler); a small irregular table covers 2 more (Es gibt→geben, war→sein). VERB candidate list: mean 31, max 106.
hypotheses.proposedChange:
Before the features call, generate ranked candidates from raw members and append at most 64 to canonicalFormAlternatives.
- VERB/AUX: strip -e/-st/-t/-et/-en/-te/-ten; ge-...-t/-en; ...zu...en; particle + infinitive; 'sich ' + x; plus a reviewed irregular-verb table.
- ADJ/ADV: strip -e/-en/-em/-er/-es.
- NOUN: strip plural/case endings and reverse the last umlaut.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About -1 s on roughly 50-75% of first-encounter VERB clicks and 40-60% of ADJ/NOUN clicks. In the waterfall that is about 10/77 clicks, so mean click critical path -130 ms and VERB p50 from ~2.7 s to ~1.7 s.
hypotheses.risk: jev may pick a plausible wrong candidate (wirken vs nachwirken, erinnern vs sich erinnern, pseudo-forms). Noisy lists may lower `canonical` accuracy on cases that are correct today. The list must stay within the 64 cap or the cap must rise.
hypotheses.experiment: Variant build, then evaluate lexeme/verb, adjective, noun and adverb, 2 runs each vs baseline. Metrics: canonicalForm exact match, pass count, Luna follow-up rate from traces, wall ms. Review any changed canonical form case by case.

hypotheses.title: Offload headword hints to intake (one Luna call per analysed sentence) and feed them to resolveGrammar as alternatives
hypotheses.claim: The open-class headword is the remaining click-time Luna dependency. Idiom and Collocation citation forms (Luna needed in 30/33 and 14/28 corpus cases) and strong verbs are not rule-derivable. Intake already knows every Lexeme and Phraseme target once analyzeSentence finishes.
hypotheses.evidence: Luna follow-up rates under gold answers above. resolvedUnitAt (sentence-analysis/analysis.ts:336-360) returns only family, kind and offsets, no headword. Intake runs at submit and is off the click path (tf-demo linguisticOrchestration.ts:331-351). Live grammar.text p50 970 ms, max 2111.
hypotheses.proposedChange: After assembleAnalysis, make one Luna call per sentence that returns the dictionary headword of each resolved target. Store it on the Sentence Analysis and pass it to resolveGrammar as canonicalFormAlternatives (for example through lemmaCandidates-like strings).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About -1 s on 60-90% of first-encounter VERB, ADJ and Idiom clicks, with more coverage than the rules. Cost: one extra Luna call per sentence (~$0.0003) and ~1 s of intake time if run after analysis.
hypotheses.risk: Spend is wasted on sentences nobody clicks (intake README: 'A sentence nobody clicks is pure loss'). jev can accept a wrong hint. Intake wall time grows unless the call runs concurrently on raw words.
hypotheses.experiment: Prototype under prototypes/audit: Luna headwords for the grammar-corpus sentences. Then evaluate lexeme/verb, lexeme/adjective and phraseme/idiom with the hints injected as lemma candidates vs baseline. Metrics: follow-up rate, canonical exact match, pass count.

hypotheses.title: For DET/PRON, ask only the Core features on which the spelling's authored candidates disagree
hypotheses.claim: For closed classes the authored catalog fixes most Core features for a given spelling, yet each one is asked as a fatal Unresolved-able question. Mismatched answers also trigger the extra authoredIdentity round trip.
hypotheses.evidence: judgments.ts:216-233 asks every catalog Core path; authored-identity.ts:23-63 is the follow-up call. measure-inputs.ts closedClassIdentity: DET asks 8.0 Core questions and 0.3 vary across the spelling's candidates (31/41 spellings are unique). PRON asks 11.0 and 2.3 vary (3.8 candidates mean, max 21). HEAD waterfall: 2/7 PRON clicks failed on 'Unresolved applicable question lemma.coreFeatures.referenceNumber' (Manche, viele). 4/7 PRON clicks paid grammar.authoredIdentity (274-440 ms). PRON grammar p50 611 ms vs 327 ms for single-trip routes.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Compute candidatesFor(normalized spelling) filtered by Kind before building questions. Fill Core values that are equal across all candidates from the catalog and skip those questions. Skip Core entirely when one candidate remains. Keep the full set when there is no candidate (3/41 DET, 3/205 PRON: typos).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Removes about 8.7 of 11 PRON and 7.7 of 8 DET fatal questions per click. Fewer authoredIdentity follow-ups should take PRON grammar from ~611 to ~330 ms on affected clicks. In the waterfall sample it would remove 2 of 7 PRON failures.
hypotheses.risk: The intake README reports 14-16 DET-twin confusions, so pruning must be keyed on Kind plus normalized spelling. Typos and variants must keep the full question set.
hypotheses.experiment: Evaluate lexeme/pronoun (167 eval) and lexeme/determiner (32 eval), 2 runs each, baseline vs variant. Metrics: pass count, number of grammar.authoredIdentity calls, Unresolved-question failures.

hypotheses.title: Constrain or salvage the emoji generation output and demonstrate function words
hypotheses.claim: In the HEAD waterfall the emoji call is the largest single whole-click failure: 5/66 generations (7.6%) failed validation because Luna appended words. The prompt is free text with no schema. Its demonstrations cover only ADJ/NOUN/VERB, while 3 of the 5 failures were function words.
hypotheses.evidence: model.ts:54 outputFormat 'text'; prompts.ts 'Return only one to four emoji graphemes, directly as text.'; generate/cases.ts kinds ADJ 38, VERB 27, NOUN 10. Live outputs: des '🔗 принадлагч', relative die '👩‍🦰relativpronomen', am '📅 monday calendar emoji maybe ...', Ausweg '🚪 escape?', leider '😔 unfortunately'. Separately, resolve.ts:164-170 fails the click when Luna regenerates a candidate jev rejected (1/20 pass-2 runs); the generation input (resolve.ts:158-161) never lists those candidates.
hypotheses.proposedChange:
(a) Use JSON output {emoji} with a short pattern, or salvage the leading run of 1-4 emoji graphemes when the rest is non-emoji text.
(b) Retry once on invalid output.
(c) Add 2-3 demonstrations for a preposition, a conjunction and a relative pronoun, or author emoji for ADP/CCONJ/SCONJ/PART.
(d) Pass the rejected candidates as 'avoid', or treat a collision as Reuse.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Generated-Reading failures from 7.6% to about 1%. Salvage fixes 5/5 syntactically, but 2/5 are semantically weak. A retry adds ~1.1 s only on the remaining failures.
hypotheses.risk: Salvaged emoji can be wrong (👩‍🦰 depicts the antecedent, not the relative pronoun). A schema or JSON mode may change emoji quality.
hypotheses.experiment: `bun cli/sample-reading.ts` on the 5 failing inputs plus ~10 function-word inputs from reading-emoji-description/operation-cases.json (13 ADP, 2 CCONJ, 1 SCONJ, 1 PART), 20 samples each, baseline vs variant. Then `bun --env-file=../../.env.local cli/evaluate.ts --experiment reading-generation/de --revision <rev>`. Metrics: invalid-output rate, accepted rate.

hypotheses.title: Retry jev once on connection errors that fail before any response
hypotheses.claim: Every jev call runs with maxRetries 0. A fast socket failure drops a sentence's whole analysis: Promise.all over chunks in analyzeSentence, and Promise.all over sentences in segment, where one failure rejects the whole submitted text. Those lost analyses then push clicks onto the classify fallback.
hypotheses.evidence: judgment.ts:136 and promptsmith/src/typesafe.ts:42,48 (maxRetries 0); sentence-analysis/operation.ts:40; universal/segment.ts:185-190. Waterfall: 3/48 intake.analyze calls failed in 39-42 ms with 'The socket connection was closed unexpectedly'. That left 8/78 clicks without an analysis, so they fell back to classify (+~330 ms). Fallback targets matched gold 7/10 vs 58/68 from analysis.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Retry once in judgmentCaller, or in the host executor, when transport fails before a response (connection closed or reset, under ~200 ms). The judgments are read-only and idempotent.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Per-call intake loss from about 6% to about 0.4%. The classify fallbacks caused by missing analyses disappear (8/78 clicks in the sample: -330 ms each and fewer wrong targets). Text-level segment failure risk also drops.
hypotheses.risk: Do not retry slow timeouts, which would double latency.
hypotheses.experiment: From battery/dumgen: `bun --env-file=../../.env.local prototypes/audit/waterfall.ts --intake-only --intake-repeats 5 --label retry` vs baseline. Count ProviderFailure per call and sentences without analysis. Then one full run to confirm the fallback share.

hypotheses.title: Serve Fusion clicks (am, im, ins, zum, zur, vom, beim) from the stored analysis instead of classifying
hypotheses.claim: The analysis makes a Fusion's adposition component its own ADP singleton. tf-demo selection, however, requires every analysed piece of the clicked stored Segment to belong to the unit, so a click on 'am' always returns null and pays classifyTarget.
hypotheses.evidence: sentence-analysis/assemble.ts:303-315 (fused word: 'its adposition a singleton and its article the next noun's'); app/tf-demo/server/sentenceAnalysisSelection.ts:72-81. Waterfall fallbackReasons clickedNotMember: kino#6 'ins', museum#8 'am' (2 of 10 fallbacks). classify p50 325 ms.
hypotheses.proposedChange: In selectAnalysisTarget, or a dumgen helper, return {Lexeme, ADP, [clickedSegmentIndex]} when the clicked stored segment is a Fusion whose adposition piece is an ADP unit. This matches the intake rule 'A fused preposition and article (im, zum, ins, zur) is one ADP unit'.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About -330 ms and one fewer failure point on every Fusion click (am/im/zum are high-frequency tokens), and the same target at intake and at click.
hypotheses.risk: Low. Confirm the grammar stage accepts the fused word as the ADP member; the fallback already returned [am] ADP in the waterfall.
hypotheses.experiment: waterfall.ts --all-members on sentences with fusions (kino, museum plus a few DW sentences), baseline vs variant. Metrics: classify calls per click, grammar outcome for Fusion clicks.

hypotheses.title: Overlap the segment judgment with analyzeSentence and raise analysis concurrency
hypotheses.claim: The intake critical path is segment (a jev call per sentence, not deterministic code) followed by analyzeSentence at concurrency 4, and the text is persisted only after every analysis finishes. Per-call latency barely changes with concurrency, so the waves are pure queueing.
hypotheses.evidence: segment.ts:42-80; linguisticOrchestration.ts:320-360 ({concurrency: 4} at :351). Waterfall intake for 16 sentences: segment 498 ms, analyze phase 1931 ms, wall 2430 ms. analyze p50 427 ms at concurrency 4 vs 395 ms at concurrency 1.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Run the deterministic segmenter immediately and start analyzeSentence on its output concurrently with the segment judgment; redo only when stitching is Needed or the language is not de. Raise concurrency to 12-16 after checking rate limits. Optionally persist before analyses finish.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Intake wall for 16 sentences from ~2.4 s to ~0.6-1.0 s (about -0.5 s from the overlap and -1 s from fewer waves). Early clicks hit a stored analysis more often instead of classify.
hypotheses.risk: A wasted analysis when stitching is Needed (rare). jev 429s or more socket errors at higher concurrency, so pair this with jev-transport-retry.
hypotheses.experiment: waterfall.ts --intake-only at --intake-concurrency 4, 8 and 16, plus an overlap variant, 3 repeats each. Metrics: intake wallMs, per-call p50/p90, ProviderFailure count.

hypotheses.title: Give the grammar stage intake's state-passive rule and state that typos and particles are supported
hypotheses.claim: Intake accepts [ist, geschlossen] as a VERB state passive by an explicit TIGER rule that the grammar policy lacks. The grammar gate then rejects exactly those targets, and typos too.
hypotheses.evidence: target-classification/judgments.ts:26 'Under TIGER, productive state passive is verbal if an active/werden-passive paraphrase preserves meaning and participants'. The rule is absent from verbal-guidance.ts. feature-questions.ts:451 still offers 'State passive (Zustandspassiv)'. Support U in recorded runs: 'Die Tür ist geschlossen' 0.74-0.80 (4/4), 'wurde um Geduld gebeten' 0.56-0.65 (4/4), tanzd 0.86-0.90, sol 0.50-0.66, mus 0.55-0.61.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Add the TIGER sentence to policy.verbalIdentity or the support criteria, plus: 'A misspelled occurrence of a supported target is still supported; orthography and normalization handle it.'
hypotheses.expectedImpact: -3 to -5 support failures per 77 verb cases. Stacks with support-gate-threshold.
hypotheses.risk: Over-accepting adjectival participles as VERB, so the adjective corpus must be checked.
hypotheses.experiment: lexeme/verb and lexeme/adjective, 2 runs each, baseline vs variant. Metrics: support failures on verbs, ADJ pass count unchanged.

hypotheses.title: Chunk intake questions by estimated tokens instead of a fixed 220 questions
hypotheses.claim: The chunker counts questions under a stated 32k-token budget. Question size ranges from 351 to 2,619 chars, so heavy chunks blow past that budget and whole-sentence payload grows O(n²).
hypotheses.evidence: questions.ts:112-113 ('the request budget is about 32k tokens'; questionsPerCall 220). measure-inputs.ts intakeBreakdown: chars per question are 351 (membership), 1874 (route), 1486 (role), 2619 (identity). 39 of 381 calls are over 32k tokens, the largest about 56k. Whole-sentence p50 by resolvable words: ≤5 9.7k, ≤8 17k, ≤11 31k, ≤15 50k, 16+ 77k. 'Obwohl die überraschend ausführliche Einleitung ... verstanden.' takes 6 calls and 181k tokens. Live latency is about 172 ms + 14.7 ms per 1k tokens (waterfall fit, r = 0.8).
hypotheses.proposedChange: Chunk by chars/3.4 ≤ ~24k tokens and interleave route/role/id questions so no chunk carries all the heavy ones.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: The slowest chunk of a long sentence drops from ~1 s to ~0.5 s, and no request exceeds a possible server limit. No change for sentences of ≤8 words (86% of corpus sentences).
hypotheses.risk: More chunks mean more calls (pair with the retry). It is unknown whether jev enforces 32k at all.
hypotheses.experiment: Live analyzeSentence on the 30 chunked target-classification sentences, baseline vs token-based chunking. Record per-call tokens, latency and ProviderFailure. Run `cli/evaluate.ts --experiment sentence-analysis/de` to confirm no accuracy change.

hypotheses.title: Compress intake per-word inventories (route/role/identity): measure first, low priority
hypotheses.claim: Most of the intake payload is verbatim repetition. Moving the per-word inventories into state with short labels could cut about 30-40% of tokens, roughly -100 ms per intake call. It has no effect on click latency.
hypotheses.evidence: measure-inputs.ts repetition table for intake.analyze: criteria 30,850 chars (mean) vs 5,624 unique (82% repeated); instructions 13,171 vs 1,815 unique (86%). Payload share: membership 19%, route 19%, role 15%, same 13%, id 10%, pk 7%, fix 6%, state 21%.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Move the lexemeRoutes and roles descriptions into state and use short per-question labels. Keep the membership wording verbatim.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: About -100 ms per intake call and nothing on the click path. Not worth doing unless intake latency still matters after the concurrency/overlap and chunking changes.
hypotheses.risk: Project memory: rewording the membership question collapsed accuracy (114 vs ~160). Route and role wording may be just as sensitive, and the gold sentence-analysis corpus has only 16 sentences.
hypotheses.experiment: prototypes/intake/lab.ts on the 212 lemma-gold sentences, 2 runs each, current vs compressed. Metrics: members found, route correct, roles, identity exact, tokens and latency.

hypotheses.title: NOT worth it for speed: trimming grammar policy text or de-duplicating sentence copies
hypotheses.claim: Grammar payloads are small enough that jev latency is nearly flat across them. Removing bloat buys milliseconds. The only reason to edit these texts is to fix contradictions.
hypotheses.evidence: 332 recorded grammar calls: median 304 ms at 2-4k tokens, 317 ms at 4-6k, 328 ms at 6-8k (~6 ms per 1k tokens). verbalComposition is 3,302 chars (~940 tokens ≈ 6 ms). The duplicate NOUN sentence is ~50 tokens. A VERB features call costs about $0.00025 at $0.042/M, and the emoji system prompt is already cached (1,922 of 1,956 tokens).
hypotheses.proposedChange: None for speed. Fix the contradictions listed under promptProblems instead.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Under 10 ms per click; negligible cost difference.
hypotheses.risk: None.
hypotheses.experiment: None needed. Optionally one lexeme/verb run without verbalComposition to confirm a latency delta under 10 ms and to see the accuracy effect.

hypotheses.title: NOT worth it: generating emoji or definitions for every word at intake
hypotheses.claim: Emoji and drafts depend on the click-time Lemma and the learner's stored Reading candidates. Precomputing them for every word multiplies Luna spend by words per sentence, while only a few words per sentence get clicked.
hypotheses.evidence: draft.ts:49-54 and resolve.ts:152-163 key on markedContext + Lemma. A Luna call is ~$0.0002-0.0003. The waterfall had 78 clicks over 16 sentences (~5 per sentence) vs ~10 resolvable words per sentence. Project memory: the emoji is the sense anchor and drafts fork after grammar.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Keep emoji and drafts at click. If anything moves to intake, make it the single per-sentence headword hint (intake-lemma-hints).
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Avoids about 2-4× Luna spend for no latency gain on words nobody clicks.
hypotheses.risk: None.
hypotheses.experiment: None. Revisit only with measured clicks-per-sentence from production.

hypotheses.title: Stop one sentence's segment failure from rejecting the whole text submission
hypotheses.claim: segment resolves all sentences with Promise.all. One sentence with Unresolved language, validity or stitching, or one transport error, rejects the whole text. tf-demo does not catch it, unlike analysis failures.
hypotheses.evidence: segment.ts:95-110 (throws 'Intake unresolved for sentence i') and 185-190 (Promise.all). linguisticOrchestration.ts:320-330 yields segment directly with no catchAll, while analyzeAcceptedSentence (381-389) catches its failures.
hypotheses.proposedChange: Turn a per-sentence failure into a Rejected or Unanalysed decision, optionally after one retry, and keep the rest of the text.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Failure of the whole text drops from 1-(1-p)^N to about 0 for long texts. p is unknown: 0/16 segment failures in the waterfall.
hypotheses.risk: A sentence stored as unanalysable may hide a real language problem.
hypotheses.experiment: `bun --env-file=../../.env.local cli/evaluate.ts --experiment intake --revision <rev>` for the decision contract, plus fault injection in waterfall.ts (one failing sentence) to confirm partial success.

hypotheses.title: Bundle definition and translations into one structured draft call
hypotheses.claim: The draft is 4 concurrent, uncached Luna calls, and their maximum is the click's long pole for most New Readings. One structured call returning {definition, en, ru} would remove the max-of-3 tail.
hypotheses.evidence: Waterfall: the draft is the long pole in 45 of 54 generated New Readings, by 424 ms on average (meanDraftMs 1349 vs reading 1120). Per-call p50/p90: definition 1182/1512, en 1310/1673, ru 1014/1488, transcription 1080/1618 ms. measure-inputs.ts: draft payloads 118-306 tokens, below the 1024-token prompt-cache floor.
hypotheses.proposedChange: One draftKnowledge Luna call with outputSchema {definition, translations: {en, ru}} and the same sense-anchor prompt. Keep transcription separate or defer it. Never bundle into the emoji call.
hypotheses.expectedImpact: Speculative: -100 to -300 ms on the long pole for New Readings, and fewer calls.

intake.latencyVsQuestionsNote: Latency is not flat. It grows linearly with input tokens: per call about 172 ms + 14.7 ms per 1k input tokens (r=0.80, n=48 calls). Per question the slope is 1.25 ms (r=0.33) because tokens per question vary; jev bills about 235 input tokens per intake question. Smallest sentence: ausweg, 36 questions, 11.4k tokens, 373 ms. Largest: erinnert, 120 questions, 27.7k tokens, 571 ms, and museum, 145 questions, 27.4k tokens, 561 ms. The n(n-1) membership matrix dominates. No sentence needed a second chunk (max 145 of the 220 allowed). Whole intake for the 16-sentence text took 2430 ms: segment 498 ms, then the analyze phase 1931 ms. dumgen.segment is not deterministic: it makes one jev call per sentence (language, validity, stitching; about 420 ms) plus an optional Luna stitch, and it is a serial prefix before analyzeSentence. The analyze phase runs as 4 waves because tf-demo uses concurrency 4, and jev does not slow under concurrency (repeat p50 395 ms serial vs 427 ms at c4). Raising intake concurrency to the sentence count would cut the phase to roughly the slowest single call (~600 ms). Starting deterministic segmentation plus analysis speculatively alongside the language/stitching call would remove the ~450-500 ms prefix. Intake quality against gold: 7 of 15 analysed sentences pass. Misses: des Nachbarn and den Schülern split (des routed ADP), geht's dir fragmented, fused m in am Montag unattached (Montag voted PROPN), früh/spät ADV instead of ADJ, very/good not X, Ihc X instead of PRON.

clickCriticalPath.breakdown: Critical path = target selection + resolveGrammar + max(Reading, draft), joined for New Readings. Convex hops are not simulated. All 78 clicks: p50 1860 ms, p90 3033 ms, mean 1843 ms. Resolved (64): p50 1902 ms, p90 3180 ms. By Reading decision: generated New (54) p50 2029 ms, p90 3281 ms. Authored closed-class (10, no Luna) p50 392 ms, p90 771 ms. Share of the summed critical path: Luna emoji generation 55% (mean 1006 ms per click), grammar.features jev 18% (340 ms), draft join excess 13% (245 ms), Luna canonical-form follow-up 9.5% (176 ms averaged over all clicks, about 1.05 s when it fires), classify fallback 2.3%, authored-identity jev 1.3%. Mean segments: select 43 ms (336 ms when classified), grammar 544 ms, tail after grammar 1419 ms (Reading 1120 ms, draft 1349 ms). The draft is the long pole in 45 of 54 generated New Readings, by a mean of 424 ms. The draft is max-of-4 parallel Luna calls, and single 2.8-3.4 s stragglers (translations.en/ru) set every p90 waterfall. Sequential round trips per resolved click: p50 2, max 4. Counterfactuals from the recorded timelines: no draft join gives p50 1613 / p90 2706. Speculative canonical-form Luna call in parallel with features gives p50 1860 / p90 2694. Grammar features precomputed at intake gives p50 1497 / p90 2694. All three give p50 1268 / p90 2357. Luna cost is a latency floor, not a prompt-size effect: provider p50 is about 0.8-1.0 s for both the 1956-token emoji call and the 143-273-token draft calls, plus a constant ~233 ms client/network overhead. jev costs about 170 ms + 15 ms per 1k tokens, so trimming grammar policy text saves at most about 50 ms. Round trips on the path are the lever. Concurrency effect is small: on the same 28 clicks, concurrency 4 vs serial critical p50 is 1879 vs 1864 ms and generated-New p50 is 2220 vs 2159 ms. Luna emoji p50 is 1293 vs 1095 ms (provider +150-200 ms under load); jev is unaffected (features p50 329 vs 332 ms).

ADV 11/9: 1982/3281. PRON 7/4: 618/1882, grammar 611 (authored identity follow-up). DET 6/6: 353/944 (authored, no Luna). ADP 6/4: 1873/2807. ADJ 4/4: 1727/3180. NUM 2/2: 1669/2345. baseline.followUpRates: Counts are over the 77 clicks that reached grammar. Luna canonical form (grammar.text, always the generateCanonicalForm stage) fired 13/77: VERB 9/15, NOUN 2/20, ADJ 1/4, ADP 1/6, never on phrasemes because the judge accepted their joined candidate. The jev lexical-strings follow-up fired 0/77 and the noun Case follow-up 0/77, so the speculative questions in the features call fully absorb them on this corpus. Noun article resolution has no extra call: the article/Case answers ride the features call. Authored identity (DET/PRON jev) fired 6/77: PRON 4/7, DET 2/6; the other closed-class clicks were direct catalog hits. authoredChoice among several reviewed Readings fired 0. Emoji compare fired 0/77 in pass 1 by design (first encounter, candidates []). Emoji generation fired 59/77, 66 calls including clicks that later failed: every open-class route; PRON 1/7 (relative die, a catalog gap that escaped as open). Draft Knowledge averaged 3.38 Luna calls per resolved click: 4 for open-class (definition, transcription, translations en and ru, from tf-demo generationRequestFor with default en+ru settings; relations were not requested because the reviewed relation allowlist qualifiedKinds is empty), 0 for authored DET/PRON. Pass 2 compare-then-generate: with own candidate plus 2 distractors (20), the compare picked its own emoji 18/20. It said NoMatch and regenerated 1/20 (es gibt geben: new 🫴 instead of 👐). One click failed after NoMatch because the regenerated emoji collided with a candidate. Compare p50 326 ms, p90 495 ms; composite critical path p50 692 ms, p90 2078 ms. With 3 distractors only (10), it said NoMatch and generated 5/10 but wrongly reused an unrelated lemma's emoji 5/10: steht auf got 🚶, heute got 🌅⏰, früh got ⏰🔜, Nachbar got 👥🗣️, sein got 🟰. Reading p50 350 ms, p90 1374 ms; composite critical path p50 1630 ms, p90 3817 ms (compare 323 ms plus generate 862 ms sequential).

baseline.analysisCoverage: 68 of 78 clicks (87%) were answered by the stored Sentence Analysis and 10 (13%) fell back to click-time classifyTarget. Of the fallbacks, 8 came from the failed intake transport on sentence usw (noAnalysis). The other 2 are fused-word clicks: kino#6 'ins' and museum#8 'am' hit clickedNotMember, because the analysis splits the fused word and the stored Segment is not wholly inside one unit. This is a structural gap: every click on a fused word (im, am, ins, zur) pays about 335 ms of classify. Target correctness against the corpus gold (largest unit at the clicked Segment): analysis 58/68, classified 7/10. Analysis mismatches: des Nachbarn split with des routed ADP; den Schülern split; früh and spät ADV instead of ADJ; Montag PROPN instead of NOUN; very/good ADV/ADJ instead of X; Ihc X instead of PRON. Classified mismatches: auf dem Markt taken as one ADP; dem Markt routed DET; usw. Unresolved. After dedupe (one click per analysed unit, preferring the Lexeme head member), grammar resolved 64 of 78 clicks, with 5 more lost at the emoji step.
baseline.notes:
Harness: imports current dumgen src directly, which bun resolves. It builds Dumgen exactly like app/tf-demo/server/modelExecution.ts: createOpenAIExecutor per Dumgen, a new TypeSafe client per judgment, default gpt-5.6-luna with reasoning none and service_tier fast (OpenAI reports tier 'priority'), jev-latest, 10 s judgment timeout, maxRetries 0. Knowledge request: imports tf-demo generationRequestFor with effectiveRelationPublicationPolicy, whose qualifiedKinds is currently []. Target selection mirrors selectAnalysisTarget plus the validateEncounter guard, recording the fallback reason.

Limitations: Convex hops (loadResolutionContext, grammarAvailable, findStoredReadings, commit) are not simulated unless --convex-hop-ms is set. The runtime is bun, not the Convex runtime. Clicks were deduplicated to one per analysed unit, giving 78 clicks rather than about 100, because tf-demo reuses the attestation for other members; --all-members lifts that. Pass 1 is always a first encounter (lemmaCandidates [] and candidates []). Pass 2 distractors are other lemmas' emoji. The 'gold' target check is my projection of the sentence-analysis gold onto stored Segments. The dumrel dist may predate the latest dumrel commit; it affects only generationRequestFor, whose extra governedPrepositions aspect the draft ignores.

Spend: pilot $0.0040, baseline $0.0927, serial $0.0269, total $0.1236. The intake is the largest cost line: about $0.0007 per sentence at ~17k jev tokens, versus about $0.0006 per click for the 4 uncached draft calls and about $0.0001 per cached emoji call.

Speed candidates, backed by the recorded timelines:
(1) Stop joining the draft on the click path. Persist the Reading first and attach the draft when it lands. p50 -250 ms, p90 -330 ms. Alternatively fold the 4 draft calls into 1 to remove the max-of-4 straggler tail, or cache transcription per lemma, since it is lemma-only.
(2) Run the Luna canonical-form call speculatively for verbal, phraseme and ADJ targets in parallel with the features call. p90 -340 ms on verbs, and it also fixes 5 wrong headwords.
(3) Precompute grammar features at intake. The intake README grammar-batch.ts showed batching does not hurt accuracy. About -340 ms on 100% of clicks, for roughly $0.00017 of jev per unit.
(4) Emoji generation is 55% of the critical path with a ~1 s Luna floor. Only removing it from the click path helps: generate at intake or speculatively, then compare at click time only when stored candidates exist. The jev compare is about 325 ms.
(5) Intake: raise analyze concurrency from 4 to the sentence count (analyze phase 1.9 s to about 0.6 s for 16 sentences) and overlap the segment language/stitching jev call with deterministic segmentation plus analysis (-450 ms).
Combining (1) to (3) gives p50 1268 ms and p90 2357 ms, from 1860 and 3033 ms.

Reliability candidates:
- Sanitize or retry emoji output (7.6% of generations lose the click).
- Guard canonical form for finite verbal targets.
- Drop Unmarked from noun number when inflection is Marked (3 of 20 nouns lost).
- Stop failing PRON clicks on an Unresolved referenceNumber.
- Retry the stale-socket jev failures on intake.
- Treat a generated emoji that collides with a candidate as Reuse.
- Tighten the compare NoMatch rubric.
- Fix fused-word selection so ins/am/zur clicks do not need classify.

Other checks: no lexical-strings or noun-case follow-ups fired, so those paths add no latency today. jev latency is insensitive to concurrency.
